extraction_notes.note: 92 numbered equations are written with the paper's argument macro \BE{label} (= \begin{equation}\label{label}), which latex_facts.py does not expand; they are not in facts.json. Each was emitted as an equation node (confidence 0.95) and the uses edges for \ref's to them were added by hand with basis 'ref', since finalize does not resolve those labels.

The prompt asks for rigor: semi_formal on a proof sketch but also forbids rigor on proof nodes; the sketch of the Monotonicity Lemma was emitted with alternative: true on its proves edge and no rigor field.

Named classical results (Monotonicity Lemma, Mean Value Inequality, Removal of Singularity, ...) restated by these expository notes with sharpened hypotheses were marked origin external (standard or McDuff-Salamon), though the notes prove them; their proofs are origin paper.

Section 5.4 is one long worked example in prose; it was emitted as one example node containing the definitions, claims and proofs stated inside it, with the final paragraph as the claim describing the limit.

The informal overview in Section 2.1 and pointer sentences ('This theorem is established in Section 5.3') were not made nodes except where they define terms or restate results (kept as also_stated_at).

nodes.name: Riemann surface
nodes.statement: A (smooth) \sf{Riemann surface} (without boundary) is a pair $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ consisting of a smooth two-dimensional manifold~$\Sigma$ (without boundary) and a complex structure~$\mathfrak j$ in the fibers of~$T\Sigma$.

nodes.name: nodal Riemann surface
nodes.statement: A~\sf{nodal Riemann surface} is a pair $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ obtained from a Riemann surface~$(\wt\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ by identifying pairs of distinct points of~$\wt\Sigma$ in a discrete subset~$S_{\Sigma}$ (with no point identified with more than one other point); see the left-hand sides of Figures~\ref{st_fig1} and~\ref{st_fig2}.
nodes.statement_short: A nodal Riemann surface is obtained from a Riemann surface by identifying pairs of points of a discrete subset.

nodes.name: normalization and nodes
nodes.statement: The pair $(\wt\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is called the \sf{normalization} of~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$; the images of the points of~$S_{\Sigma}$ in~$\Sigma$ are called the \sf{nodes} of~$\Sigma$.

nodes.name: smooth locus Sigma^*
nodes.statement: We denote their complement in~$\Sigma$ by~$\Sigma^*$.

nodes.name: irreducible component
nodes.statement: An \sf{irreducible component} of~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is the image of a topological component of~$\wt\Sigma$ in~$\Sigma$.

nodes.name: arithmetic genus
nodes.statement: Let $$\mathfrak a(\Sigma)= \frac{2-\chi(\wt\Sigma)+|S_{\Sigma}|}{2}\,,$$ where $\chi(\wt\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of $\wt\Sigma$, be the (\sf{arithmetic}) \sf{genus} of~$\Sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Arithmetic genus of a nodal surface: (2 - Euler characteristic of the normalization + number of identified points)/2.

nodes.name: equivalence of Riemann surfaces
nodes.statement: An \sf{equivalence} between Riemann surfaces $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ and $(\Sigma',\mathfrak j')$ is a homeomorphism $h\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma'$ induced by a biholomorphic map~$\wt{h}$ from $(\wt\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ to $(\wt\Sigma',\mathfrak j')$.

nodes.name: automorphism group of a Riemann surface
nodes.statement: We denote by $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ the group of automorphisms, i.e.~self-equivalences, of a Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$.

nodes.name: J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface, a smooth map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is called \sf{$J$-holomorphic map} if $$\textnormal{d} u\!\circ\!\mathfrak j=J\!\circ\!\textnormal{d} u\!:T\Sigma\longrightarrow u^*TX.$$

nodes.name: J-holomorphic map from a nodal Riemann surface
nodes.statement: A \sf{$J$-holomorphic map} from a nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a tuple $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$, where $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a continuous map induced by a $J$-holomorphic map $\wt{u}\!:\wt\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$; see Figures~\ref{st_fig1} and~\ref{st_fig2}.
nodes.definiendum: $J$-holomorphic map from a nodal Riemann surface

nodes.name: equivalence of J-holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: An \sf{equivalence} between $J$-holomorphic maps $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ and $(\Sigma',\mathfrak j',u')$ is an equivalence $$h\!: (\Sigma,\mathfrak j)\longrightarrow(\Sigma',\mathfrak j')$$ between the underlying Riemann surfaces such that $u\!=\!u'\!\circ\!h$.

nodes.name: automorphism group of a J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: We denote by $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ the group of automorphisms, i.e.~self-equivalences, of a $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$.

nodes.name: stable J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: A $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ is called \sf{stable} if $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is compact and $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ is a finite group.

nodes.name: stable map from two glued elliptic curves
nodes.statement: The Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ on the left-hand side of Figure~\ref{st_fig1} is obtained by identifying the marked points of two copies of a smooth elliptic curve $(\Sigma_0,\mathfrak j_0,z_1^*)$, i.e.~a torus with a complex structure and a marked point. The Riemann surface $(\Sigma_0,\mathfrak j_0)$ with the marked point~$z_1^*$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}/\Lambda$ with the marked point~$0$ for some lattice $\Lambda\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ and thus has an automorphism of order~2 that preserves~$z_1^*$ (it is induced by the map $z\!\longrightarrow\!-z$ on~$\mathbb{C}$). This is the only non-trivial automorphism of $(\Sigma_0,\mathfrak j_0)$ preserving~$z_1^*$ if~$\mathfrak j_0$ is generic; in special cases, the group of such automorphisms is either ${\mathbb Z}_4$ or~${\mathbb Z}_6$. Each automorphism of $(\Sigma_0,\mathfrak j_0)$ preserving~$z_1^*$ gives rise to an automorphism of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ fixing one of the irreducible components. There is also an automorphism of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ which interchanges the two irreducible components of~$\Sigma$. Since it does not commute with the automorphisms preserving one of the components, $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)\!\approx\!D_4$ in most cases and contains~$D_4$ in the special cases. If $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma_0$ is the identity on each irreducible component, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ is a stable $J$-holomorphic map; the interchange of the two irreducible components is then the only non-trivial automorphism of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$. The $J$-holomorphic maps $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma_0$ obtained by sending either or both irreducible components of~$\Sigma$ to~$z_1^*$ instead are also stable, but have different automorphism groups. If $(\Sigma_0,\mathfrak j_0)$ were taken to be the Riemann sphere~$\mathbb{P}^1$, the $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma_0$ restricting to the identity on each copy of~$\Sigma_0$ would still be stable. However, a map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma_0$ sending either copy of~$\Sigma_0$ to~$z_1^*$ would not be stable, since the group of automorphisms of~$\mathbb{P}^1$ fixing a point is a complex two-dimensional submanifold of~$\textnormal{PSL}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Two elliptic curves glued at a marked point: automorphism groups and stability of the maps to one copy, contrasted with the P^1 case.

nodes.name: finiteness of automorphism groups of Riemann surfaces
nodes.statement: Let $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact connected Riemann surface of genus~$g$. If $g\!\ge\!2$, then $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a finite group. If $g\!=\!1$, then $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is an infinite group, but its subgroup fixing any point is finite. If $g\!=\!0$, then the subgroup of $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ fixing any pair of points is infinite, but the subgroup fixing any triple of points is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Aut of a compact genus-g Riemann surface: finite for g>=2; for g=1 the stabilizer of a point is finite; for g=0 the stabilizer of three points is trivial.

nodes.name: automorphisms preserving a non-constant J-holomorphic map are finite
nodes.statement: If in addition $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map, then the subgroup of $\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ consisting of the automorphisms such that $u\!=\!u\!\circ\!h$ is finite; this is an immediate consequence of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2}.

nodes.name: stability criterion for J-holomorphic maps from nodal surfaces
nodes.statement: If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact nodal Riemann surface, a $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ is thus stable if and only~if \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$,leftmargin=*] \item every genus~1 topological component of the normalization~$\wt\Sigma$ of~$\Sigma$ such that $u$ restricts to a constant map on its image in~$\Sigma$ contains at least 1~element of~$S_{\Sigma}$ and \item every genus~0 topological component of~$\wt\Sigma$ such that $u$ restricts to a constant map on its image in~$\Sigma$ contains at least 3 elements of~$S_{\Sigma}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A map from a compact nodal surface is stable iff every contracted genus-1 component has a special point and every contracted genus-0 component has at least 3.

nodes.name: Eq. Ebndcond_e
nodes.statement: \liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\Big(\big|\pi_0(\Sigma_i)\big|\!+\!\mathfrak a(\Sigma_i)\!+\!E_g(u_i)\!\Big)<\infty

nodes.name: Gromov's convergence
nodes.statement: The notion of \sf{Gromov's convergence} of a sequence of stable $J$-holomorphic maps $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ to another stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ comes down~to \begin{enumerate}[label=(GC\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item $|\pi_0(\Sigma_i)|\!=\!|\pi_0(\Sigma_{\infty})|$ and $\mathfrak a(\Sigma_i)\!=\!\mathfrak a(\Sigma_{\infty})$ for all~$i$ large, \item $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ is at least as singular as $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ for all~$i$ large, \item the energy is preserved, i.e.~$E_g(u_i)\!\longrightarrow\!E_g(u_{\infty})$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$, and \item $u_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_{\infty}^*$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Gromov convergence: same topology and genus, more singular limit domain, energy preserved, C^infty convergence away from the nodes.

nodes.name: Gromov's Compactness I (convergence for a fixed domain)
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$ and $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface. A sequence $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u_i)$ of stable \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} maps \sf{converges} to a stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ if \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),ref=\arabic*,leftmargin=*] \item $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ is obtained from~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ by identifying a point on each of $\ell$~trees of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$, for some $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$, with distinct points $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma$, \item $E_g(u_{\infty})=\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)$, \item there exist $h_i\!\in\!\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ with $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$, \item for each $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma\!\subset\!\Sigma_{\infty}$ and all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, there exist a neighborhood $U_j\!\subset\!\Sigma$ of~$z_j^*$, an open subset $U_{j;i}\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$, and a biholomorphic map $\psi_{j;i}\!:U_{j;i}\!\longrightarrow\!U_j$ such~that \begin{enumerate}[label=(\ref{psi_it2}\alph*),leftmargin=*] \item $U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$ and $\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_{j;i}$ for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$, \item $u_i\!\circ\!h_i\!\circ\!\psi_{j;i}$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes $\infty,w_{j;1}^*,\ldots,w_{j;k_j}^*$ in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_j^1$ attached at $z_j^*\!\in\!\Sigma$, \item condition (\ref{psi_it2}) applies with $\Sigma$, $(z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*)$, and $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ replaced by~$\mathbb{P}^1$, $(w_{j;1}^*,\ldots,w_{j;k_j}^*)$, and $u_i\!\circ\!h_i\!\circ\!\psi_{j;i}$, respectively, for each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A sequence of maps from a fixed compact Riemann surface converges to a stable map with trees of spheres attached at finitely many points, with energy preserved and rescaled C^infty convergence on the bubbles.
nodes.label: GromConv_dfn1

nodes.name: comparison of Definition 1.1 with McDuff-Salamon's axioms
nodes.statement: The recursive condition~(\ref{psi_it2}) in Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn1} is equivalent to the {\it Rescaling} axiom in \cite[Definition~5.2.1]{MS12} on sequences of automorphisms~$\phi_{\alpha}^i$ of~$\mathbb{P}^1$; they correspond to compositions of the maps~$\psi_{j;i}$ associated with different irreducible components of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$. The single energy condition~(\ref{GC1energy_it}) in Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn1} is replaced in \cite[Definition~5.2.1]{MS12} by multiple conditions of the {\it Energy} axiom. These multiple conditions are equivalent to~(\ref{GC1energy_it}) if the other three axioms in \cite[Definition~5.2.1]{MS12} are satisfied.

nodes.name: Gromov's Compactness I
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface, and $u_i\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence of non-constant $J$-holomorphic maps. If $\liminf E_g(u_i)\!<\!\infty$, then the sequence $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u_i)$ contains a subsequence converging to some stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn1}.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded-energy J-holomorphic maps from a fixed compact Riemann surface into a compact almost complex manifold have a Gromov-convergent subsequence.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface
$u_i\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence of non-constant $J$-holomorphic maps
conclusions: the sequence $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u_i)$ contains a subsequence converging to some stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn1}
nodes.label: GromConv_thm1

nodes.name: flat family of deformations
nodes.statement: Let $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a nodal Riemann surface. A \sf{flat family of deformations} of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a holomorphic map $\pi\!:\mathcal U\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta$, where $\mathcal U$ is a complex manifold and $\Delta\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}^N$ is a neighborhood of~$0$, such~that \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$,leftmargin=*] \item $\pi^{-1}(\lambda)$ is a nodal Riemann surface for each $\lambda\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n$ and $\pi^{-1}(0)\!=\!(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, \item $\pi$ is a submersion outside of the nodes of the fibers of~$\pi$, \item for every $\lambda^*\!\equiv\!(\lambda_1^*,\ldots,\lambda_N^*)\!\in\!\Delta$ and every node $z^*\!\in\!\pi^{-1}(\lambda^*)$, there exist $i\!\in\!\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\lambda_i\!=\!0$, neighborhoods $\Delta_{\lambda^*}$ of~$\lambda^*$ in~$\Delta$ and $\mathcal U_{z^*}$ of~$z^*$ in~$\mathcal U$, and a holomorphic~map $$\Psi\!:\mathcal U_{z^*}\longrightarrow \big\{\big((\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N),x,y\big)\!\in\!\Delta_{\lambda^*}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^2\!: xy\!=\!\lambda_i\big\}$$ such that $\Psi$ is a homeomorphism onto a neighborhood of $(\lambda^*,0,0)$ and the composition of~$\Psi$ with the projection to~$\Delta_{\lambda^*}$ equals~$\pi|_{\mathcal U_{z^*}}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A holomorphic map onto a neighborhood of 0 in C^N with nodal fibers, central fiber the given surface, submersive away from nodes, and locally xy=lambda_i at nodes.

nodes.name: trivialization of a flat family away from the nodes
nodes.statement: If $\pi\!:\mathcal U\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta$ is a flat family of deformations of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ and $\Sigma$ is compact, there exists a neighborhood $\mathcal U^*\!\subset\!\mathcal U$ of $\Sigma^*\!\subset\!\pi^{-1}(0)$ such~that $$\pi|_{\mathcal U^*}\!:\mathcal U^*\longrightarrow \Delta_0\!\equiv\!\pi(\mathcal U^*)\subset\Delta$$ is a trivializable $\Sigma^*$-fiber bundle in the smooth category.

nodes.name: smooth identifications psi_lambda
nodes.statement: For each $\lambda\!\in\!\Delta_0$, let $$\psi_{\lambda}\!:\Sigma^*\longrightarrow \pi^{-1}(\lambda)\!\cap\!\mathcal U^*$$ be the corresponding smooth identification.

nodes.name: u.c.s. convergence
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_i\!\in\!\Delta$ is a sequence converging to $0\!\in\!\Delta$ and \hbox{$u_i\!:\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a sequence of continuous maps that are smooth on the complements of the nodes of~$\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)$, we say that the sequence~$u_i$ \sf{converges to} a smooth map $u\!:\!\Sigma^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$ {\sf u.c.s.} if the sequence of maps $$u_i\!\circ\!\psi_{\lambda_i}\!:\Sigma^*\longrightarrow X$$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Maps on fibers converge u.c.s. if their pullbacks by the smooth identifications converge in C^infty on compact subsets of Sigma^*.

nodes.name: u.c.s. convergence is independent of choices
nodes.statement: This notion is independent of the choices of~$\mathcal U^*$ and trivialization of~$\pi|_{\mathcal U^*}$.

nodes.name: Gromov's Convergence II (convergence with varying domains)
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$. A sequence $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ of stable \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} maps \sf{converges} to a stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ if $E_g(u_{\infty})\!\longrightarrow\!E_g(u_i)$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ and there exist \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=*] \item a flat family of deformations $\pi\!:\mathcal U\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta$ of $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$, \item a sequence $\lambda_i\!\in\!\Delta$ converging to $0\!\in\!\Delta$, and \item equivalences $h_i\!:\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)\!\longrightarrow\!(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ \end{enumerate} such that $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}|_{\Sigma_{\infty}^*}$ u.c.s.
nodes.statement_short: Convergence of stable maps with varying domains via a flat family of deformations of the limit domain and equivalences of the fibers, with energy convergence.
nodes.label: GromConv_dfn2

nodes.name: Gromov convergence is independent of the metric
nodes.statement: By the compactness of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$, the notion of convergence of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2} is independent of the choice of metric~$g$ on~$X$.

nodes.name: limiting domains are obtained by pinching circles
nodes.statement: If the Riemann surfaces $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ are smooth, the limiting Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ is obtained by pinching some disjoint embedded circles in the smooth two-dimensional manifold~$\Sigma$ underlying these Riemann surfaces.\\ \noindent If \hbox{$(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)\!=\!(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$} for all~$i$ as in Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn1}, only contractible circles are pinched to produce~$\Sigma_{\infty}$; it then consists of~$\Sigma$ with trees of spheres attached. The family $\pi\!:\mathcal U\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta$ is obtained by starting with the family $$\pi_0\!:\mathcal U_0\!\equiv\!\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathbb{C},$$ then blowing up~$\mathcal U_0$ at a point of $\{0\}\!\times\!\Sigma$ to obtain a family $\pi_1\!:\mathcal U_1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}$ with the central fiber \hbox{$\Sigma_1\!\equiv\!\pi_1^{-1}(0)$} consisting of $\Sigma$ with~$\mathbb{P}^1$ attached, then blowing up a smooth point of~$\Sigma_1$, and so~on. The number of blowups involved is precisely the number of nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$, i.e.~four in the case of Figure~\ref{st_fig2} and two in the case of Figure~\ref{st_fig3}. The pinched annuli on the right-hand side of Figure~\ref{st_fig3} correspond to $\phi_{\alpha}(B_{\delta}(z_{\alpha\beta}))\!\cup\!\phi_{\beta}(B_{\delta}(z_{\beta\alpha}))$ in the notation of \cite[Chapters~4,5]{MS12}.
nodes.statement_short: The limit domain is obtained by pinching circles; for a fixed domain only contractible circles, giving trees of spheres via iterated blowups.

nodes.name: balls B_delta(z^*) in the total space
nodes.statement: With the setup of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2}, let $B_{\delta}(z^*)\!\subset\!\mathcal U$ denote the ball of radius $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ around a point $z^*\!\in\!\mathcal U$ with respect to some metric on~$\mathcal U$.

nodes.name: no bubbling at the nodes of the limit
nodes.statement: Then, \BE{nobubbles_e}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\textnormal{diam}_g\big( u_i\big(h_i(\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}(z^*))\big)\!\big)=0 \qquad\forall~z^*\!\in\!\Sigma_{\infty}\,.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Eq. nobubbles_e
nodes.statement: \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\textnormal{diam}_g\big( u_i\big(h_i(\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}(z^*))\big)\!\big)=0 \qquad\forall~z^*\!\in\!\Sigma_{\infty}\,.

nodes.name: proof of the no-bubbling property
nodes.statement: This is immediate from the last condition in Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2} if $z^*\!\in\!\Sigma_{\infty}^*$. If $z^*\!\in\!\Sigma_{\infty}\!-\!\Sigma_{\infty}^*$ is a node of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$, (\ref{nobubbles_e}) is a consequence of both convergence conditions of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2} and the maps~$u_i$ being $J$-holomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from u.c.s. convergence away from the nodes; at nodes it follows from both convergence conditions and J-holomorphicity.

nodes.name: bubbling requires energy
nodes.statement: It is a reflection of the fact that \sf{bubbling} or any other kind of erratic $C^0$-behavior of a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps requires a nonzero amount of energy in the limit, but the two convergence conditions of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2} ensure that all limiting energy is absorbed by~$u|_{\Sigma_{\infty}^*}$ and thus none is left for bubbling around the nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$.

nodes.name: proof that the homology class is preserved
nodes.statement: An immediate implication of~(\ref{nobubbles_e}) is that $u_i(h_i(\pi^{-1}(\lambda_i)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}(z^*)))$ is contained in a geodesic ball around $u_{\infty}(z^*)$ in~$X$.
nodes.statement_short: By the no-bubbling property, small neighborhoods of nodes map into small geodesic balls.

nodes.name: homology class is preserved under Gromov convergence
nodes.statement: Thus, $$u_{i*}\big[\Sigma_i\big]=u_{\infty*}[\Sigma_{\infty}]\in H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})$$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large.

nodes.name: homotopy class is preserved for trees of spheres
nodes.statement: If $\Sigma_{\infty}$ is a tree of spheres (and thus so is each~$\Sigma_i$), then $u_i$ with $i$ sufficiently large lies in the equivalence class in $\pi_2(X)$ determined by~$u_{\infty}$ for the same reason.

nodes.name: Gromov's Compactness II
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$ and $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ be a sequence of stable $J$-holomorphic maps into a compact almost complex manifold~$(X,J)$. If it satisfies~(\ref{Ebndcond_e}), then it contains a subsequence converging to some stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2}.
nodes.statement_short: Stable J-holomorphic maps with bounded topology, genus and energy have a subsequence converging in the sense of Definition 1.3.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with Riemannian metric~$g$
$(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ be a sequence of stable $J$-holomorphic maps into a compact almost complex manifold~$(X,J)$
conclusions: it contains a subsequence converging to some stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2}
also_stated_at: The fundamental insight in~\cite{Gr} that laid the foundations for the pseudoholomorphic curves techniques in symplectic topology and for the moduli spaces of stable maps and related curve-parametrizing objects in algebraic geometry is that a sequence of stable $J$-holomorphic maps $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ into a compact almost complex manifold~$(X,J)$ with \BE{Ebndcond_e} \liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\Big(\big|\pi_0(\Sigma_i)\big|\!+\!\mathfrak a(\Sigma_i)\!+\!E_g(u_i)\!\Big)<\infty\end{equation} has a subsequence converging in a suitable sense to another stable $J$-holomorphic map.
nodes.label: GromConv_thm2

nodes.name: proof of Gromov's Compactness II for smooth domains
nodes.statement: This theorem is obtained by combining the compactness of the Deligne-Mumford moduli spaces $\ov\mathcal M_{1,1}$ of stable (possibly) nodal elliptic curves and $\ov\mathcal M_g$ of stable nodal genus $g\!\ge\!2$ curves with the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} in Section~\ref{Conver_subs2}. One first establishes Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2} under the assumption that each $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ is a smooth connected Riemann surface of genus $g\!\ge\!1$ (the $g\!=\!0$ case is treated by Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1}). If $g\!=\!1$, we add a marked point to each domain $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ and take a subsequence converging in $\ov\mathcal M_{1,1}$ to the equivalence class of some stable nodal elliptic curve $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}',z_{\infty}')$. If $g\!\ge\!2$, we take a subsequence of $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ converging in $\ov\mathcal M_g$ to the equivalence class of some stable nodal genus~$g$ curve $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}')$. This ensures the existence of a flat family of deformations $\pi'\!:\mathcal U'\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta'$ of $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}')$, of a sequence $\lambda_i'\!\in\!\Delta'$ converging to $0\!\in\!\Delta'$, and of equivalences $h_i\!:\pi'^{-1}(\lambda_i')\!\longrightarrow\!(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$. The associated neighborhood $\mathcal U'^*$ of $\Sigma_{\infty}'^*$ in~$\mathcal U'$ can be chosen so that $\pi'^{-1}(\lambda)\!-\!\mathcal U'^*$ consists of finitely many circles for every $\lambda'\!\in\!\Delta'$ sufficiently small. The complement of the image of the associated identifications $$\psi_{\lambda}'\!:\Sigma_{\infty}'^*\longrightarrow \pi'^{-1}(\lambda)\!\cap\!\mathcal U'^*$$ in $\pi'^{-1}(\lambda)$ has the same property.\\ \noindent One then applies the construction in the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} to the sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps $$u_i\!\circ\!h_i'\!:\Sigma_{\infty}'^*\longrightarrow X$$ to obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $\wt{u}_{\infty}'$ from the normalization $\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ of $\Sigma_{\infty}$ and finitely $J$-holomorphic maps from trees of~$\mathbb{P}^1$. Each of these trees will have one or two special points that are associated with points of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ (the latter happens if bubbling occurs at a preimage of a node of~$\Sigma_{\infty}'$ in~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$). Identifying these trees with the corresponding points of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1}, we obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ satisfying the requirements of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2}. It is necessarily stable if $g\!\ge\!2$, or $\Sigma_{\infty}'$ is smooth, or $\Sigma_{\infty}$ contains a separating node. Otherwise, the identifications~$h_i'$ may first need to be reparametrized to ensure that either the limiting map $\wt{u}_{\infty}'$ is not constant or the sequence $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ produces a bubble at least one smooth point of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine compactness of the Deligne-Mumford spaces with the construction in the proof of Theorem 1.2 applied to the reparametrized maps; attach the bubble trees to the limit domain.

nodes.name: strategy
nodes.statement: This theorem is obtained by combining the compactness of the Deligne-Mumford moduli spaces $\ov\mathcal M_{1,1}$ of stable (possibly) nodal elliptic curves and $\ov\mathcal M_g$ of stable nodal genus $g\!\ge\!2$ curves with the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} in Section~\ref{Conver_subs2}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Deligne-Mumford compactness with the proof of Theorem 1.2.

nodes.name: reduce to smooth connected domains
nodes.statement: One first establishes Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2} under the assumption that each $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ is a smooth connected Riemann surface of genus $g\!\ge\!1$ (the $g\!=\!0$ case is treated by Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1}).
nodes.statement_short: First treat smooth connected domains of genus >= 1.

nodes.name: genus 1
nodes.statement: If $g\!=\!1$, we add a marked point to each domain $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ and take a subsequence converging in $\ov\mathcal M_{1,1}$ to the equivalence class of some stable nodal elliptic curve $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}',z_{\infty}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Add a marked point and use compactness of M_{1,1}.

nodes.name: genus at least 2
nodes.statement: If $g\!\ge\!2$, we take a subsequence of $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$ converging in $\ov\mathcal M_g$ to the equivalence class of some stable nodal genus~$g$ curve $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Use compactness of M_g.

nodes.name: flat family
nodes.statement: This ensures the existence of a flat family of deformations $\pi'\!:\mathcal U'\!\longrightarrow\!\Delta'$ of $(\Sigma_{\infty}',\mathfrak j_{\infty}')$, of a sequence $\lambda_i'\!\in\!\Delta'$ converging to $0\!\in\!\Delta'$, and of equivalences $h_i\!:\pi'^{-1}(\lambda_i')\!\longrightarrow\!(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i)$. The associated neighborhood $\mathcal U'^*$ of $\Sigma_{\infty}'^*$ in~$\mathcal U'$ can be chosen so that $\pi'^{-1}(\lambda)\!-\!\mathcal U'^*$ consists of finitely many circles for every $\lambda'\!\in\!\Delta'$ sufficiently small. The complement of the image of the associated identifications $$\psi_{\lambda}'\!:\Sigma_{\infty}'^*\longrightarrow \pi'^{-1}(\lambda)\!\cap\!\mathcal U'^*$$ in $\pi'^{-1}(\lambda)$ has the same property.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a flat family and identifications of the domains.

nodes.name: apply the construction of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: One then applies the construction in the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} to the sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps $$u_i\!\circ\!h_i'\!:\Sigma_{\infty}'^*\longrightarrow X$$ to obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $\wt{u}_{\infty}'$ from the normalization $\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ of $\Sigma_{\infty}$ and finitely $J$-holomorphic maps from trees of~$\mathbb{P}^1$.
nodes.statement_short: Get a limit on the normalization plus bubble trees.

nodes.name: special points of the trees
nodes.statement: Each of these trees will have one or two special points that are associated with points of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ (the latter happens if bubbling occurs at a preimage of a node of~$\Sigma_{\infty}'$ in~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$).
nodes.statement_short: Each tree has one or two special points.

nodes.name: assemble the limit
nodes.statement: Identifying these trees with the corresponding points of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$ as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1}, we obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$ satisfying the requirements of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2}.
nodes.statement_short: Attach the trees to get the limit map.

nodes.name: stability
nodes.statement: It is necessarily stable if $g\!\ge\!2$, or $\Sigma_{\infty}'$ is smooth, or $\Sigma_{\infty}$ contains a separating node.
nodes.statement_short: Stability holds in the listed cases.

nodes.name: reparametrize otherwise
nodes.statement: Otherwise, the identifications~$h_i'$ may first need to be reparametrized to ensure that either the limiting map $\wt{u}_{\infty}'$ is not constant or the sequence $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ produces a bubble at least one smooth point of~$\wt\Sigma_{\infty}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise reparametrize first.

nodes.name: k-marked Riemann surface
nodes.statement: A \sf{$k$-marked Riemann surface} is a tuple $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ such that $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface and $z_1,\ldots,z_k\!\in\!\Sigma^*$ are distinct points.

nodes.name: k-marked J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, a \sf{$k$-marked \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} map} into~$X$ is a tuple $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k,u)$, where $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ is $k$-marked Riemann surface and $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u)$ is a $J$-holomorphic map into~$X$.

nodes.name: degree of a marked J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: The \sf{degree} of such a map is the homology~class $$A=u_*[\Sigma]\in H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})\,.$$

nodes.name: proof of Gromov's Compactness II, general case
nodes.statement: The general case of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2}, including its extension to stable marked maps, is then obtained by \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$,leftmargin=*] \item passing to a subsequence of $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ with the same topological structure of the domain, \item viewing it as a sequence of tuples of $J$-holomorphic maps with smooth domains with an additional marked point for each preimage of the nodes in the normalization, and \item applying the conclusion of the above argument to each component of the tuple. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce nodal domains to tuples of maps with smooth marked domains and apply the smooth-domain argument componentwise.

nodes.name: reduction
nodes.statement: The general case of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2}, including its extension to stable marked maps, is then obtained by \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$,leftmargin=*]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the general case to smooth domains.

nodes.name: fix the topology
nodes.statement: passing to a subsequence of $(\Sigma_i,\mathfrak j_i,u_i)$ with the same topological structure of the domain,
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a subsequence with fixed domain topology.

nodes.name: normalize the domains
nodes.statement: viewing it as a sequence of tuples of $J$-holomorphic maps with smooth domains with an additional marked point for each preimage of the nodes in the normalization, and
nodes.statement_short: View the maps as tuples of maps with smooth marked domains.

nodes.name: apply the smooth case
nodes.statement: applying the conclusion of the above argument to each component of the tuple. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the smooth-domain argument componentwise.

nodes.name: moduli space of stable maps
nodes.statement: The natural extension of Definition~\ref{GromConv_dfn2} to marked $J$-holomorphic maps topologizes the moduli space $\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)$ of equivalence classes of stable degree~$A$ $k$-marked genus~$g$ $J$-holomorphic maps into $X$ for each $A\!\in\!H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})$.

nodes.name: evaluation maps
nodes.statement: The evaluation~maps $$\textnormal{ev}_i\!:\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\longrightarrow X, \quad (\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k,u)\longrightarrow u(z_i),$$ are continuous with respect to this topology.

nodes.name: forgetful map to the Deligne-Mumford space
nodes.statement: If $2g\!+\!k\!\ge\!3$, there is a continuous map $$\mathfrak f\!:\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\longrightarrow \ov\mathcal M_{g,k}$$ to the Deligne-Mumford moduli space of stable $k$-marked genus~$g$ nodal curves obtained by forgetting the map~$u$ and then contracting the unstable components of the domain.

nodes.name: forgetful map dropping the last marked point
nodes.statement: There is a continuous map \BE{ffkdfn_e}\mathfrak f_{k+1}\!:\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k+1}(X,A;J)\longrightarrow\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\end{equation} obtained by forgetting the last marked point~$z_{k+1}$ and then contracting the components of the domain to stabilize the resulting $k$-marked $J$-holomorphic map.

nodes.name: Eq. ffkdfn_e
nodes.statement: \mathfrak f_{k+1}\!:\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k+1}(X,A;J)\longrightarrow\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)

nodes.name: sections s_i of the universal curve
nodes.statement: For each $i\!=\!1,\ldots,k$, this fibration has a natural continuous section $$s_i\!: \ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\longrightarrow \ov\mathfrak M_{g,k+1}(X,A;J)$$ described as follows. For a $k$-marked nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k)$, let $(\Sigma',\mathfrak j',z_1,\ldots,z_{k+1})$ be the $(k\!+\!1)$-marked nodal Riemann surface so that $(\Sigma',\mathfrak j')$ consists of $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ with $\mathbb{P}^1$ attached at~$z_i$, $z_1',z_i'\!\in\!\mathbb{P}^1$, and $z_j'=\!z_j\!\in\!\Sigma$ for all $j\!=\!1,\ldots,k$ different from~$k$; see Figure~\ref{st_fig4}. We define $$s_i\big([\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_1,\ldots,z_k,u]\big]=\big[\Sigma',\mathfrak j',z_1',\ldots,z_{k+1}',u'\big],$$ with $(\Sigma',\mathfrak j',z_1',\ldots,z_{k+1}')$ as described and $u'$ extending $u$ over the extra~$\mathbb{P}^1$ by the constant map with value~$u(z_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: s_i attaches a constant bubble P^1 at the i-th marked point carrying the i-th and the new marked point.

nodes.name: universal tangent line bundle
nodes.statement: The pullback $$L_i\longrightarrow \ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)$$ of the vertical tangent line bundle of~(\ref{ffkdfn_e}) by $s_i$ is called the \sf{universal tangent line bundle} at the $i$-th marked point.

nodes.name: descendant class
nodes.statement: Let $\psi_i\!=\!c_1(L_i^*)$ be the \sf{$i$-th descendant class}.

nodes.name: Hausdorff property and deformation-obstruction theory
nodes.statement: A remarkable property of Gromov's topology which lies behind most of its applications is that the moduli space $\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)$ is Hausdorff and has a particularly nice deformation-obstruction theory. In the algebraic-geometry category, the latter is known as a perfect \sf{two-term deformation-obstruction theory}. In the almost complex category, this is reflected in the existence of an \sf{atlas of finite-dimensional approximations} in the terminology of~\cite{LT} or of an \sf{atlas of Kuranishi charts} in the terminology of~\cite{LT}.

nodes.name: energy of a J-holomorphic map equals omega(A)
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $J$ is tamed by a symplectic form~$\omega$, then the energy $E_g(u)$ of degree~$A$ $J$-holomorphic map~$u$ with respect to the metric~$g$ determined by~$J$ and~$\omega$ is $\omega(A)$; see~(\ref{Egexp_e}).

nodes.name: compactness of the moduli space
nodes.statement: If in addition $X$ is compact, then Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2} implies that this moduli space is also compact.

nodes.name: virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: Combining this with the remarkable property of the previous paragraph, the constructions of \cite{BF,LT0,LT,FO} endow $\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)$ with a \sf{virtual fundamental class}. It depends only on~$\omega$, in a suitable sense, and not an almost complex structure~$J$ tamed by~$\omega$.

nodes.name: Gromov-Witten invariants
nodes.statement: This class in turn gives rise to \sf{Gromov-Witten invariants} of~$(X,\omega)$: $$\blr{\tau_{a_1}\!\alpha_1,\ldots,\tau_{a_k}\!\alpha_k}_{g,A}^X \equiv \blr{\big(\psi_1^{a_1}\!\textnormal{ev}_1^*\alpha_1)\ldots\big(\psi_k^{a_k}\!\textnormal{ev}_k^*\alpha_k), \big[\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\big]^{\textnormal{vir}}}\in\mathbb Q$$ for all $a_i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$ and $\alpha_i\!\in\!H^*(X;\mathbb Q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Descendant GW invariants: integrals of psi-classes times pulled-back cohomology classes against the virtual class.

nodes.name: order of u at z
nodes.statement: We denote by $\textnormal{ord}_zu\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ the minimum of such integers~$\ell$ and call it the \sf{order of~$u$ at~$z$}; it is independent of the choice of a chart around~$u(z)$. If $u$ is constant on the component of~$\Sigma$ on containing~$z$, we set $\textnormal{ord}_zu\!=\!0$.

nodes.name: singular point
nodes.statement: A point $z\!\in\!u$ is \sf{singular}, i.e.~$\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0$, if and only if $\textnormal{ord}_zu\!\neq\!1$.

nodes.name: order of u at x
nodes.statement: In the case $\Sigma$ is compact, the second statement of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2} implies~that \BE{ordxudfn_e}\textnormal{ord}_xu\!\equiv\!\sum_{z\in u^{-1}(x)}\!\!\!\!\!\!\textnormal{ord}_zu ~~\in{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0} \qquad\forall\,x\!\in\!X;\end{equation} we call this number the \sf{order of~$u$ at~$x$}. If $x\!\not\in\!\textnormal{Im}(u)$, then $\textnormal{ord}_xu\!=\!0$.

nodes.name: Eq. ordxudfn_e
nodes.statement: \textnormal{ord}_xu\!\equiv\!\sum_{z\in u^{-1}(x)}\!\!\!\!\!\!\textnormal{ord}_zu ~~\in{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0} \qquad\forall\,x\!\in\!X;

nodes.name: pairings g(mu tensor eta) and g(mu wedge eta)
nodes.statement: Let $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a Riemann surface, $V$ be a vector bundle over~$\Sigma$, and $$\mu,\eta\in\Gamma\big(\Sigma;T^*\Sigma\!\otimes_{\mathbb R}\!V\big) \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad g\in\Gamma\big(\Sigma;T^*\Sigma^{\otimes2}\!\otimes_{\mathbb R}\!V\big).$$ For a local coordinate $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$, define \BE{muetadfn_e}\begin{split} g(\mu\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)&= \big(g\big(\mu(\partial_s),\eta(\partial_s)\!\big)\!+\!g\big(\mu(\partial_t),\eta(\partial_t)\!\big)\!\big) \textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\,,\\ g(\mu\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)&=\big(g\big(\mu(\partial_s),\eta(\partial_t)\!\big)\!-\! g\big(\mu(\partial_t),\eta(\partial_s)\!\big)\!\big) \textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\,. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Local-coordinate formulas for the 2-forms obtained by pairing V-valued 1-forms via g.

nodes.name: Eq. muetadfn_e
nodes.statement: \begin{split} g(\mu\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)&= \big(g\big(\mu(\partial_s),\eta(\partial_s)\!\big)\!+\!g\big(\mu(\partial_t),\eta(\partial_t)\!\big)\!\big) \textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\,,\\ g(\mu\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)&=\big(g\big(\mu(\partial_s),\eta(\partial_t)\!\big)\!-\! g\big(\mu(\partial_t),\eta(\partial_s)\!\big)\!\big) \textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\,. \end{split}

nodes.name: the pairings are coordinate-independent
nodes.statement: By a direct computation, the 2-forms $g(\mu\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)$ and $g(\mu\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!\eta)$ are independent of the choice of local coordinate \hbox{$z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$}. Thus, (\ref{muetadfn_e}) determines global 2-forms on~$\Sigma$ (which depend on the choice of~$\mathfrak j$).

nodes.name: standard complex structures i and J_{C^n}
nodes.statement: We denote by~$\mathfrak i$ the standard complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}$ and by~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ the standard complex structures on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ and~$T\mathbb{C}^n$.

nodes.name: metric g_J and 2-form omega_J
nodes.statement: For an almost complex structure~$J$ and a 2-form~$\omega$ on a manifold~$X$, we define a 2-tensor and a 2-form on~$X$ by \BE{omJdfn_e}\begin{split} g_J(v,v')&=\frac12\big(\omega(v,Jv')-\omega(Jv,v')\big),\\ \omega_J(v,v')&=\frac12\big(\omega(Jv,Jv')-\omega(v,v')\big) \end{split} \qquad\forall\,v,v'\!\in\!T_xX,~x\!\in\!X.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Eq. omJdfn_e
nodes.statement: \begin{split} g_J(v,v')&=\frac12\big(\omega(v,Jv')-\omega(Jv,v')\big),\\ \omega_J(v,v')&=\frac12\big(\omega(Jv,Jv')-\omega(v,v')\big) \end{split} \qquad\forall\,v,v'\!\in\!T_xX,~x\!\in\!X.

nodes.name: Eq. omEner_e
nodes.statement: g_J(v,v)+g_J(v',v')=2\omega(v,v')+g_J(v\!+\!Jv',v\!+\!Jv') +2\omega_J(v,v') \quad\forall\,v,v'\!\in\!T_xX,~x\!\in\!X.

nodes.name: taming 2-form
nodes.statement: The 2-form $\omega$ \sf{tames} $J$ if $g(v,v)\!>\!0$ for all $v\!\in\!TX$ nonzero; in such a case, $\omega$ is nondegenerate and $g_J$ is a metric.

nodes.name: omega-compatible almost complex structure
nodes.statement: The almost complex structure~$J$ is \sf{$\omega$-compatible} if $\omega$ tames~$J$ and $\omega_J\!=\!0$.

nodes.name: pullback notation for g and omega
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a Riemann surface, and $f\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a smooth map. We denote the pullbacks of a 2-tensor~$g$ and a 2-form~$\omega$ on~$X$ to the vector bundle $f^*TX$ over~$\Sigma$ also by~$g$ and~$\omega$.

nodes.name: energy of a map
nodes.statement: If $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ and $U\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is an open subset, let \BE{Egfdfn_e}E_g(f)\equiv\frac12\int_{\Sigma}g(\textnormal{d} f\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} f)\in[0,\infty] \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad E_g(f;U)\equiv E_g\big(f|_U)\end{equation} be the \sf{energy} of~$f$ and of its restriction to~$U$.

nodes.name: Eq. Egfdfn_e
nodes.statement: E_g(f)\equiv\frac12\int_{\Sigma}g(\textnormal{d} f\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} f)\in[0,\infty] \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad E_g(f;U)\equiv E_g\big(f|_U)

nodes.name: energy is half the squared L^2-norm of df
nodes.statement: By the first equation in~(\ref{muetadfn_e}), \BE{Egfdfn2_e} E_g(f)=\frac12\int_{\Sigma}|\textnormal{d} f|_{g_{\Sigma},g}^2\end{equation} is the square of the $L^2$-norm of $\textnormal{d} f$ with respect to the metric~$g$ on~$X$ and a metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ compatible with~$\mathfrak j$.

nodes.name: Eq. Egfdfn2_e
nodes.statement: E_g(f)=\frac12\int_{\Sigma}|\textnormal{d} f|_{g_{\Sigma},g}^2

nodes.name: dbar_J operator
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an almost complex structure on a manifold~$X$ and $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a Riemann surface. For a smooth map $f:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$, define $$\bar\partial_Jf=\frac{1}{2}\big(\textnormal{d} f\!+\!J\!\circ\!\textnormal{d} f\!\circ\!\mathfrak j\big) \in\Gamma\big(\Sigma;(T^*\Sigma,\mathfrak j)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!f^*(TX,J)\big)\,.$$

nodes.name: energy identity for maps into a manifold with a taming form
nodes.statement: If $\omega$ is a 2-form on~$X$ taming~$J$ and \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is $J$-holomorphic, then \BE{Egexp_e} E_{g_J}(f)=\int_{\Sigma}\big(f^*\omega\!+\!2g_J(\bar\partial_Jf\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\bar\partial_Jf)\!+\!f^*\omega_J\big)\end{equation} by~(\ref{Egfdfn_e}) and~(\ref{omEner_e}).
nodes.statement_short: The energy w.r.t. g_J equals the integral of f^*omega plus twice the dbar-energy plus the integral of f^*omega_J.

nodes.name: Eq. Egexp_e
nodes.statement: E_{g_J}(f)=\int_{\Sigma}\big(f^*\omega\!+\!2g_J(\bar\partial_Jf\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\bar\partial_Jf)\!+\!f^*\omega_J\big)

nodes.name: J-holomorphic map (dbar form)
nodes.statement: A smooth map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is \sf{$J$-holomorphic} if $\bar\partial_Ju\!=\!0$.

nodes.name: balls B_R and punctured balls B_R^*
nodes.statement: For each $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, denote by $B_R\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ the open ball of radius~$R$ around the origin and let $$B_R^*=B_R\!-\!\{0\}.$$

nodes.name: metric balls B_delta^g(x)
nodes.statement: If in addition $(X,g)$ is a Riemannian manifold and $x\!\in\!X$, let $B_{\delta}^g(x)\!\subset\!X$ be the ball of radius~$\delta$ around~$x$ in~$X$ with respect to the metric~$g$.

nodes.name: somewhere injective, multiply covered, simple maps
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold and $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a Riemann surface. A smooth map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is called \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$,leftmargin=*] \item \sf{somewhere injective} if there exists $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ such that $u^{-1}(u(z))\!=\!\{z\}$ and $\textnormal{d}_zu\!\neq\!0$, \item \sf{multiply covered} if $u\!=\!u'\!\circ\!h$ for some smooth connected orientable surface~$\Sigma'$, branched cover \hbox{$h\!:\!\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma'$} of degree different from $\pm1$, and a smooth map $u'\!:\Sigma'\!\longrightarrow\!X$, \item \sf{simple} if it is not multiply covered. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: simple iff somewhere injective
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{SimplMap_prp}, every $J$-holomorphic map from a compact Riemann surface is simple if and only if it is somewhere injective (the {\it if} implication is trivial).

nodes.name: Carleman Similarity Principle
nodes.statement: Suppose $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, \hbox{$p,\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$} with $p\!>\!2$, $J\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$, $C\!\in\!L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$, and $u\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ are such~that \BE{FHScond_e} u(0)=0, \qquad J(z)^2=-\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~ u_s(z)+J(z)u_t(z)+C(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation} Then, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that \BE{FHSconc_e} \sigma(0)=0, \qquad J(z)\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A solution of a perturbed Cauchy-Riemann equation vanishing at 0 is, near 0, a J-linear gauge transform of a holomorphic map.
conclusions: there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that
\sigma(0)=0, \qquad J(z)\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.
nodes.label: FHS_prp

nodes.name: Eq. FHScond_e
nodes.statement: u(0)=0, \qquad J(z)^2=-\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~ u_s(z)+J(z)u_t(z)+C(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.

nodes.name: Eq. FHSconc_e
nodes.statement: \sigma(0)=0, \qquad J(z)\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.

nodes.name: continuity from the Sobolev Embedding Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Sobolev Embedding Theorem \cite[Corollary~4.3]{anal}, the assumption $p\!>\!2$ implies that $u$ is a continuous function. In particular, all equations in~(\ref{FHScond_e}) and in (\ref{FHSconc_e}) make sense. This assumption also implies that the left-hand sides of the third equation in~(\ref{FHScond_e}) and of the second equation in~(\ref{FHSconc_e}) and the right-hand side of the third equations in~(\ref{FHSconc_e}) lie in~$L_1^p$.

nodes.name: Carleman similarity for an explicit almost complex structure on C^2
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak c\!:\mathbb{C}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}$ denote the usual conjugation. Define \begin{gather*} \wh{J}(z_1,z_2)=\left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} \mathfrak i& 0\\ -2\mathfrak i s_1\mathfrak c& \mathfrak i\end{array}\!\!\right) =\left(\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s_1\mathfrak c& 1\end{array}\!\!\right) \!\!J_{\mathbb{C}^2}\!\! \left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s_1\mathfrak c& 1\end{array}\!\!\right)^{\!\!-1}\!:\mathbb{C}^2\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2 \quad\forall\,z_i\!=\!s_i\!+\!\mathfrak i t_i, \\ u\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2, \qquad u(s\!+\!\mathfrak i t)=\big(z,s^2). \end{gather*} Thus, $\wh{J}$ is an almost complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}^2$ and $u$ is a $\wh{J}$-holomorphic map, i.e.~it satisfies the last condition in~(\ref{FHScond_e}) with $J(z)\!=\!\wh{J}(u(z))$ and $C(z)\!=\!0$. The functions $$\sigma\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2, \quad\sigma(z)=(z,0), \qquad \Phi\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\textnormal{GL}_4\mathbb R, \quad \Phi(s\!+\!\mathfrak i t)= \left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s\mathfrak c\!+\!\frac{\mathfrak i st}{z}& 1\end{array}\!\!\right),$$ satisfy~(\ref{FHSconc_e}).
nodes.statement_short: An explicit non-standard almost complex structure on C^2 and a J-holomorphic map with explicit Phi and sigma as in Proposition 3.1.
nodes.label: FHS_eg

nodes.name: leading-order term of a J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: Let $n$, $p$, $\epsilon$, $J$, $C$, and $u$ be as in Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}. If in addition $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ and $u$ does not vanish to infinite order~0, then there exist $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $\alpha\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n\!-\!0$ such~that $$\lim_{z\longrightarrow0}\frac{u(z)-\alpha z^{\ell}}{z^{\ell}}=0\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: A solution not vanishing to infinite order at 0 behaves like alpha z^ell near 0.
assumptions: Let $n$, $p$, $\epsilon$, $J$, $C$, and $u$ be as in Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}
$J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ and $u$ does not vanish to infinite order~0
conclusions: there exist $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $\alpha\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n\!-\!0$ such~that $$\lim_{z\longrightarrow0}\frac{u(z)-\alpha z^{\ell}}{z^{\ell}}=0\,.$$
also_stated_at: For example, for every $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ contained in a component of~$\Sigma$ on which~$u$ is not constant, the $\ell$-th derivative of~$u$ at~$z$ in a chart around~$u(z)$ does not vanish for some $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$; see Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}.
nodes.label: FHS_crl1

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.3
nodes.statement: This follows from~(\ref{FHSconc_e}) and from the existence of such~$\ell$ and~$\alpha$ for~$\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Read off from the similarity u = Phi sigma and the Taylor expansion of the holomorphic sigma.

nodes.name: discreteness of critical preimages and fibers
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface, and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map. If $u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$, then the~subset $$u^{-1}\big(\{u(z)\!:\,z\!\in\!\Sigma,~\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\subset\Sigma$$ is discrete. If in addition $x\!\in\!X$, the subset $u^{-1}(x)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is also discrete.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface
$u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$
conclusions: the~subset $$u^{-1}\big(\{u(z)\!:\,z\!\in\!\Sigma,~\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\subset\Sigma$$ is discrete.
the subset $u^{-1}(x)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is also discrete.

assumptions: $u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$
conclusions: the~subset $$u^{-1}\big(\{u(z)\!:\,z\!\in\!\Sigma,~\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\subset\Sigma$$ is discrete.
the subset $u^{-1}(x)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is also discrete.

also_stated_at: If $u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$, the singular points of~$u$ and the preimages of a point $x\!\in\!X$ are discrete subsets of~$\Sigma$; see Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2}.
nodes.label: FHS_crl2

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.4
nodes.statement: The first and third equations in~(\ref{FHSconc_e}) immediately imply the second claim (but not the first, since~$\Phi$ may not be in~$C^1$). The first claim follows from Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1} and Taylor's formula for~$u$ (as well as from Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl}).
nodes.statement_short: Discreteness of fibers from u = Phi sigma; discreteness of critical preimages from Corollary 3.3 and Taylor's formula.

nodes.name: Carleman Similarity Principle for complex-linear zeroth-order term
nodes.statement: Suppose $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $p,\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are as in Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, $A\!\in\!L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$, and $u\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ are such~that \BE{FHScond4_e} u(0)=0, \qquad u_s+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}u_t(z)+A(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation} Then, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_n\mathbb{C})$, a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that \BE{FHSconc4_e} \sigma(0)=0, \qquad \Phi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, \qquad u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Special case of Carleman similarity with J standard and complex-linear A, with Phi(0)=Id.
assumptions: $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $p,\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are as in Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}
conclusions: there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_n\mathbb{C})$, a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that
\sigma(0)=0, \qquad \Phi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, \qquad u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.
nodes.label: FHS_lmm

nodes.name: Eq. FHScond4_e
nodes.statement: u(0)=0, \qquad u_s+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}u_t(z)+A(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.

nodes.name: Eq. FHSconc4_e
nodes.statement: \sigma(0)=0, \qquad \Phi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, \qquad u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z) ~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: For each $\delta\!\in\![0,\epsilon]$, we define \begin{gather*} A_{\delta}\in L^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \qquad\hbox{by}\quad A_{\delta}(z)=\begin{cases}A(z),&\hbox{if}~z\!\in\!B_{\delta};\\ 0,&\hbox{otherwise};\end{cases}\\ D_{\delta}: L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \qquad\hbox{by}\quad D_{\delta}\Theta=\big(\Theta_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\Theta_t\!+\!A_{\delta}\Theta\big)\textnormal{d}\bar{z}\,. \end{gather*} Since the cokernel of $D_0\!=\!2\bar\partial$ is isomorphic $H^1(S^2;\mathbb{C})\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n$, $D_0$ is surjective and the homomorphism $$\ti{D}_0\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n, \qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_0\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$ is an isomorphism. Since $$\big\|D_{\delta}\Theta-D_0\Theta\big\|_{L^p} \le \|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{C^0} \le C\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{L^p_1} \qquad\forall~\Theta\in L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$$ and $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the homomorphism $$\ti{D}_{\delta}\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n, \qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_{\delta}\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$ is also an isomorphism for $\delta\!>\!0$ sufficient small. Let $\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!D_{\delta}^{-1}(0,\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})$. Since $D_{\delta}$ is an isomorphism, $$\big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{C^0} \le C \big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{L^p_1} \le C'\big\|D_{\delta}(\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})\big\|_{L^p} = C'\big\|A_{\delta}\big\|_{L^p}\,.$$ Since $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, $\Theta_{\delta}\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_n\mathbb{C})$. By (\ref{FHScond4_e}) and $D_{\delta}\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!0$, the function \hbox{$\sigma\!\equiv\!\Theta_{\delta}^{-1}u$} satisfies $$\sigma(0)=0,\qquad \sigma_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\sigma_t\!=\!0\quad\forall~z\in B_{\delta},$$ i.e.~$\sigma$ is $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Perturbation argument: the operator D_delta with A cut off to B_delta is an isomorphism for small delta; invert it to build Theta_delta and set sigma = Theta_delta^{-1} u.

nodes.name: define A_delta and D_delta
nodes.statement: For each $\delta\!\in\![0,\epsilon]$, we define \begin{gather*} A_{\delta}\in L^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \qquad\hbox{by}\quad A_{\delta}(z)=\begin{cases}A(z),&\hbox{if}~z\!\in\!B_{\delta};\\ 0,&\hbox{otherwise};\end{cases}\\ D_{\delta}: L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \qquad\hbox{by}\quad D_{\delta}\Theta=\big(\Theta_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\Theta_t\!+\!A_{\delta}\Theta\big)\textnormal{d}\bar{z}\,. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Cut off A to B_delta and define the operators D_delta on S^2.

nodes.name: D_0 tilde is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Since the cokernel of $D_0\!=\!2\bar\partial$ is isomorphic $H^1(S^2;\mathbb{C})\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n$, $D_0$ is surjective and the homomorphism $$\ti{D}_0\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n) \oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n, \qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_0\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: D_0 = 2 dbar is surjective, so D_0 tilde is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: D_delta tilde is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Since $$\big\|D_{\delta}\Theta-D_0\Theta\big\|_{L^p} \le \|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{C^0} \le C\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{L^p_1} \qquad\forall~\Theta\in L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$$ and $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the homomorphism $$\ti{D}_{\delta}\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n, \qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_{\delta}\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$ is also an isomorphism for $\delta\!>\!0$ sufficient small.
nodes.statement_short: D_delta tilde is a small perturbation of D_0 tilde, hence an isomorphism for small delta.

nodes.name: construct Theta_delta close to Id
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!D_{\delta}^{-1}(0,\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})$. Since $D_{\delta}$ is an isomorphism, $$\big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{C^0} \le C \big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{L^p_1} \le C'\big\|D_{\delta}(\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})\big\|_{L^p} = C'\big\|A_{\delta}\big\|_{L^p}\,.$$ Since $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, $\Theta_{\delta}\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_n\mathbb{C})$.
nodes.statement_short: Theta_delta = D_delta^{-1}(0, Id) is C^0-close to Id, hence invertible.

nodes.name: sigma is holomorphic
nodes.statement: By (\ref{FHScond4_e}) and $D_{\delta}\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!0$, the function \hbox{$\sigma\!\equiv\!\Theta_{\delta}^{-1}u$} satisfies $$\sigma(0)=0,\qquad \sigma_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\sigma_t\!=\!0\quad\forall~z\in B_{\delta},$$ i.e.~$\sigma$ is $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic, as required.
nodes.statement_short: sigma = Theta_delta^{-1} u is J_{C^n}-holomorphic.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 3.1 (Carleman Similarity Principle)
nodes.statement:
(1) Since $B_{\epsilon}$ is contractible, the complex vector bundles $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ and $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J)$ over $B_{\epsilon}$ are isomorphic. Thus, there exists $$\Psi\in L_1^p(B_{\epsilon};	extnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R) \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\quad J(z)\Psi(z)=\Psi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n}~~~ orall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.$$ Let $v\!=\!\Psi^{-1}u$. By the assumptions on $u$, $v\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ and  egin{gather} v(0)=0, \qquad v_s(z)+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t(z)+	i{C}(z)v(z)=0 \quad orall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon},\ \hbox{where}\quad 	i{C}=\Psi^{-1}\cdot ig(\Psi_s+J\Psi_t+C\Psi) \in L^p(B_{\epsilon};	extnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)\,.
otag \end{gather} Thus, we have reduced the problem to the case $J\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$.\ 
oindent (2) Let $	i{C}^{\pm}\!=\! rac12(	i{C}\mp J_{\mathbb{C}^n}	i{C}J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ be the $\mathbb{C}$-linear and $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear parts of~$	i{C}$, i.e.~$	i{C}^{\pm}J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\pm J_{\mathbb{C}^n}	i{C}^{\pm}$. With $\lr{\cdot,\cdot}$ denoting the Hermitian inner-product on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ which is $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear in the second input, define $$D\in L^{\infty}(B_{\epsilon};	extnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n), \quad D(z)w= egin{cases}|v(z)|^{-2}\lr{v(z),w}v(z),&\hbox{if}~v(z)\!
eq\!0;\ 0,&\hbox{otherwise}; \end{cases} \quad A=	i{C}^+ +	i{C}^-D\,.$$ Since $DJ_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\!-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}D$ and $Dv\!=\!v$, $A\in L^p(B_{\epsilon};	extnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$ and $Av\!=\!	i{C}v$. Thus, by~(ef{FHScond_e2}), $$v_s+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t+Av=0\,.$$ The claim now follows from Lemma~ef{FHS_lmm}.
nodes.statement_short: Trivialize to reduce to J = J_{C^n}, then rewrite the zeroth-order term as a complex-linear A and apply Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: reduce to the standard complex structure
nodes.statement: (1) Since $B_{\epsilon}$ is contractible, the complex vector bundles $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ and $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J)$ over $B_{\epsilon}$ are isomorphic. Thus, there exists $$\Psi\in L_1^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R) \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\quad J(z)\Psi(z)=\Psi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n}~~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.$$ Let $v\!=\!\Psi^{-1}u$. By the assumptions on $u$, $v\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ and \begin{gather} v(0)=0, \qquad v_s(z)+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t(z)+\ti{C}(z)v(z)=0 \quad\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon},\\ \hbox{where}\quad \ti{C}=\Psi^{-1}\cdot\big(\Psi_s+J\Psi_t+C\Psi) \in L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)\,.\notag \end{gather} Thus, we have reduced the problem to the case $J\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Gauge transform by Psi to reduce to J = J_{C^n}.

nodes.name: Eq. (3.1) FHScond_e2
nodes.statement: v(0)=0, \qquad v_s(z)+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t(z)+\ti{C}(z)v(z)=0 \quad\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon},\\ \hbox{where}\quad \ti{C}=\Psi^{-1}\cdot\big(\Psi_s+J\Psi_t+C\Psi) \in L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)\,.\notag
nodes.label: FHScond_e2

nodes.name: make the zeroth-order term complex linear
nodes.statement: (2) Let $\ti{C}^{\pm}\!=\!\frac12(\ti{C}\mp J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\ti{C}J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ be the $\mathbb{C}$-linear and $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear parts of~$\ti{C}$, i.e.~$\ti{C}^{\pm}J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\pm J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\ti{C}^{\pm}$. With $\lr{\cdot,\cdot}$ denoting the Hermitian inner-product on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ which is $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear in the second input, define $$D\in L^{\infty}(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n), \quad D(z)w=\begin{cases}|v(z)|^{-2}\lr{v(z),w}v(z),&\hbox{if}~v(z)\!\neq\!0;\\ 0,&\hbox{otherwise}; \end{cases} \quad A=\ti{C}^+ +\ti{C}^-D\,.$$ Since $DJ_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\!-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}D$ and $Dv\!=\!v$, $A\in L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$ and $Av\!=\!\ti{C}v$. Thus, by~(\ref{FHScond_e2}), $$v_s+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t+Av=0\,.$$ The claim now follows from Lemma~\ref{FHS_lmm}.
nodes.statement_short: Replace C tilde by a complex-linear A with Av = C tilde v and apply Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: Carleman similarity for J-holomorphic maps with bounded derivative
nodes.statement: Suppose $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, $J$ is a smooth almost complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$, and $u\!:B_{\epsilon}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with $u(0)\!=\!0$. Then, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, $\Phi\!\in\!C^0(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that $\Phi$ is smooth on~$B_{\delta}^*$, $$ \sigma(0)=0, ~~ \Phi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~ J(u(z))\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z), ~~ \big|\textnormal{d}_z\Phi\big|\le C~\forall\,z\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: For smooth J, Phi can be taken continuous, smooth off 0, with bounded derivative and Phi(0)=Id.
assumptions: $J$ is a smooth almost complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$
conclusions: there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, $\Phi\!\in\!C^0(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that $\Phi$ is smooth on~$B_{\delta}^*$, $$ \sigma(0)=0, ~~ \Phi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~ J(u(z))\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z), ~~ \big|\textnormal{d}_z\Phi\big|\le C~\forall\,z\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*\,.$$
nodes.label: FHS_crl

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.6
nodes.statement: We can assume that $u$ is not identically~0 on some neighborhood of $0\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$. Similarly to~(1) in the proof of Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, there exists $$\Psi\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{C}^n;\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R) \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\qquad \Psi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, \quad J(x)\Psi(x)=\Psi(x)J_{\mathbb{C}^n}~~~\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n\,.$$ Let $v(z)\!=\!\Psi(u(z))^{-1}u(z)$. By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}, we can choose complex linear coordinates on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ so~that $$v(z)=\big(f(z),g(z)\big)h(z) \in \mathbb{C}\!\oplus\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon'}$$ for some $\epsilon'\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, holomorphic function $h$ on~$B_{\epsilon'}$ with $h(0)\!=\!0$, and continuous functions $f$ and $g$ on~$B_{\epsilon'}$ with $f(0)\!=\!1$ and $g(0)\!=\!0$. By Lemma~\ref{C1bnd_lmm} below applied with~$f$ above and with each component of~$g$ separately, there exists $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon')$ so that the function $$\Phi\!:B_{\delta}\longrightarrow\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R, \qquad \Phi(z)=\Psi\big(u(z)\big) \left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} f(z)& 0\\ g(z)& 1\end{array}\!\!\right),$$ is continuous on $B_{\delta}$ and smooth on $B_{\delta}\!-\!0$ with $|\textnormal{d}_z\Phi|$ uniformly bounded on $B_{\delta}\!-\!0$. Taking \hbox{$\sigma(z)\!=\!(h(z),0)$}, we conclude the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Gauge transform to standard J, split off the leading holomorphic factor via Corollary 3.3, and control the derivative of Phi with Lemma 3.7.

nodes.name: reduce to non-vanishing u
nodes.statement: We can assume that $u$ is not identically~0 on some neighborhood of $0\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG u is not identically 0 near 0.

nodes.name: gauge transform
nodes.statement: Similarly to~(1) in the proof of Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, there exists $$\Psi\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{C}^n;\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R) \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\qquad \Psi(0)=\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, \quad J(x)\Psi(x)=\Psi(x)J_{\mathbb{C}^n}~~~\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n\,.$$ Let $v(z)\!=\!\Psi(u(z))^{-1}u(z)$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose smooth Psi with Psi(0)=Id intertwining J and J_{C^n}; set v = Psi(u)^{-1} u.

nodes.name: factor out the holomorphic leading term
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}, we can choose complex linear coordinates on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ so~that $$v(z)=\big(f(z),g(z)\big)h(z) \in \mathbb{C}\!\oplus\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon'}$$ for some $\epsilon'\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, holomorphic function $h$ on~$B_{\epsilon'}$ with $h(0)\!=\!0$, and continuous functions $f$ and $g$ on~$B_{\epsilon'}$ with $f(0)\!=\!1$ and $g(0)\!=\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Write v = (f, g) h with h holomorphic.

nodes.name: bound the derivative of Phi
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{C1bnd_lmm} below applied with~$f$ above and with each component of~$g$ separately, there exists $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon')$ so that the function $$\Phi\!:B_{\delta}\longrightarrow\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R, \qquad \Phi(z)=\Psi\big(u(z)\big) \left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} f(z)& 0\\ g(z)& 1\end{array}\!\!\right),$$ is continuous on $B_{\delta}$ and smooth on $B_{\delta}\!-\!0$ with $|\textnormal{d}_z\Phi|$ uniformly bounded on $B_{\delta}\!-\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.7 gives Phi continuous with bounded derivative.

nodes.name: choose sigma
nodes.statement: Taking \hbox{$\sigma(z)\!=\!(h(z),0)$}, we conclude the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Take sigma = (h, 0).

nodes.name: derivative bound for quotients by holomorphic functions
nodes.statement: Suppose $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, and $f,h\!:B_{\epsilon}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}$ are continuous functions such~that $h$ is holomorphic, $h(z)\!\!\neq\!0$ for some $z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$, and the function \BE{C1bnd_e}B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad z\longrightarrow f(z)h(z),\end{equation} is smooth. Then there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $f$ is differentiable on $B_{\epsilon}\!-\!0$ and \BE{C1bnd_e2}\big|\textnormal{d}_zf\big|\le C \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\!-\!0\,.\end{equation}
assumptions: the function \BE{C1bnd_e}B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad z\longrightarrow f(z)h(z),\end{equation} is smooth
conclusions: there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $f$ is differentiable on $B_{\epsilon}\!-\!0$ and \BE{C1bnd_e2}\big|\textnormal{d}_zf\big|\le C \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\!-\!0\,.
nodes.label: C1bnd_lmm

nodes.name: Eq. C1bnd_e
nodes.statement: B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad z\longrightarrow f(z)h(z),

nodes.name: Eq. C1bnd_e2
nodes.statement: \big|\textnormal{d}_zf\big|\le C \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\!-\!0\,.

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement: After a holomorphic change of coordinate on $B_{2\delta}\!\subset\!B_{\epsilon}$, we can assume that $h(z)\!=\!z^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$. Define $$g\!: B_{2\delta}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad g(z)=f(z)z^{\ell}-f(0)z^{\ell}\,.$$ By Taylor's Theorem and the smoothness of the function~(\ref{C1bnd_e}), there exists $C\!>\!0$ such that the smooth function~$g$ satisfies $$\big|g(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad \forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.$$ Dividing~$g$ by $z^{\ell}$, we thus obtain~(\ref{C1bnd_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Change coordinates so h = z^ell, apply Taylor's theorem to f z^ell - f(0) z^ell and divide by z^ell.

nodes.name: normalize h
nodes.statement: After a holomorphic change of coordinate on $B_{2\delta}\!\subset\!B_{\epsilon}$, we can assume that $h(z)\!=\!z^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Change coordinates so that h(z) = z^ell.

nodes.name: Taylor bound for g
nodes.statement: Define $$g\!: B_{2\delta}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad g(z)=f(z)z^{\ell}-f(0)z^{\ell}\,.$$ By Taylor's Theorem and the smoothness of the function~(\ref{C1bnd_e}), there exists $C\!>\!0$ such that the smooth function~$g$ satisfies $$\big|g(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad \forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Define g = f z^ell - f(0) z^ell and bound it by C|z|^{ell+1} via Taylor's theorem.

nodes.name: divide by z^ell
nodes.statement: Dividing~$g$ by $z^{\ell}$, we thus obtain~(\ref{C1bnd_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Dividing by z^ell gives the derivative bound.

nodes.name: Corollary 3.6 versus Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl} refines the conclusion of Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp} for $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast to the output $(\Phi,\sigma)$ of Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, the output of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl} does not depend continuously on the input~$u$ with respect to the $L^p_1$-norms. This makes Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl} less suitable for applications in settings involving families of $J$-holomorphic maps.
nodes.label: FHS_rmk

nodes.name: Unique Continuation
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a connected Riemann surface, and $$u,u'\!:(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)\longrightarrow (X,J)$$ are $J$-holomorphic maps. If $u_0$ and $u_0'$ agree to infinite order at $z_0\!\in\!\Sigma$, then $u'\!=\!u'$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a connected Riemann surface
$u_0$ and $u_0'$ agree to infinite order at $z_0\!\in\!\Sigma$
nodes.label: FHS_crl2a

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.9 (Unique Continuation)
nodes.statement: Since the subset of the points of~$\Sigma$ at which $u$ and $u'$ agree is closed to infinite order, it is enough to show that $u\!=\!u'$ on some neighborhood of~$z_0$. By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $\Sigma\!=\!B_1$, $z_0\!=\!0$, and $u(0),u'(0)\!=\!0$. Let $$w\!=\!u'\!-\!u:B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}^n\,.$$ Since $J$ is $C^1$, \BE{FHS2a_e3}J(x\!+\!y)=J(x)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J(x\!+\!ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^ny_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{x+ty}\textnormal{d} t\,.\end{equation} Since $u$ and $u'$ are $J$-holomorphic, (\ref{FHS2a_e3}) implies that \begin{gather*} \partial_s w + J\big(u(z)\big)\partial_t w+C(z)w(z)=0, \qquad\hbox{where}\quad C\in L^p\big(B_1;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n\big),\\ C(z)y=\sum_{i=1}^ny_i \bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{v(z)+tw(z)}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tw|_z\,. \end{gather*} By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, there thus exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,1)$, \hbox{$\Phi\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$}, and holomorphic map \hbox{$\wt{w}\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$} such~that $$w(z)=\Phi(z)\wt{w}(z) \qquad\forall~z\in B_{\delta}\,.$$ Since $w$ vanishes to infinite order at~$0$, it follows that $\wt{w}(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$ (otherwise, $w$ would satisfy the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}) and thus $w(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a local statement in C^n, write w = u'-u as a solution of a perturbed Cauchy-Riemann equation, and apply the Carleman Similarity Principle.

nodes.name: reduce to a neighborhood
nodes.statement: Since the subset of the points of~$\Sigma$ at which $u$ and $u'$ agree is closed to infinite order, it is enough to show that $u\!=\!u'$ on some neighborhood of~$z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: By closedness it suffices to show u = u' near z_0.

nodes.name: local model
nodes.statement: By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $\Sigma\!=\!B_1$, $z_0\!=\!0$, and $u(0),u'(0)\!=\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Work in C^n on B_1 with z_0 = 0.

nodes.name: equation for the difference
nodes.statement: Let $$w\!=\!u'\!-\!u:B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}^n\,.$$ Since $J$ is $C^1$, \BE{FHS2a_e3}J(x\!+\!y)=J(x)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J(x\!+\!ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^ny_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{x+ty}\textnormal{d} t\,.\end{equation} Since $u$ and $u'$ are $J$-holomorphic, (\ref{FHS2a_e3}) implies that \begin{gather*} \partial_s w + J\big(u(z)\big)\partial_t w+C(z)w(z)=0, \qquad\hbox{where}\quad C\in L^p\big(B_1;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n\big),\\ C(z)y=\sum_{i=1}^ny_i \bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{v(z)+tw(z)}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tw|_z\,. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: w = u'-u satisfies a linear Cauchy-Riemann type equation with L^p coefficient.

nodes.name: Eq. FHS2a_e3
nodes.statement: J(x\!+\!y)=J(x)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J(x\!+\!ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^ny_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{x+ty}\textnormal{d} t\,.

nodes.name: apply Carleman similarity
