nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, there thus exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,1)$, \hbox{$\Phi\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$}, and holomorphic map \hbox{$\wt{w}\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$} such~that $$w(z)=\Phi(z)\wt{w}(z) \qquad\forall~z\in B_{\delta}\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: w = Phi w tilde with w tilde holomorphic.

nodes.name: conclude w = 0
nodes.statement: Since $w$ vanishes to infinite order at~$0$, it follows that $\wt{w}(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$ (otherwise, $w$ would satisfy the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}) and thus $w(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: w tilde vanishes to infinite order, hence w = 0.

nodes.name: local factorization through accumulating intersections
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $$u,u'\!:(\Sigma,\mathfrak j),(\Sigma',\mathfrak j')\longrightarrow (X,J)$$ are $J$-holomorphic maps, $z_0\!\in\!\Sigma$ is such that $\textnormal{d}_{z_0}u\!\neq\!0$, and $z_0'\!\in\!\Sigma'$ is such that $u'(z_0')\!=\!u(z_0)$. If there exist sequences $z_i\!\in\!\Sigma\!-\!z_0$ and $z_i'\!\in\!\Sigma'\!-\!z_0'$ such~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i=z_0\,, \qquad \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i'=z_0'\,, \quad\hbox{and}\quad u(z_i)=u'(z_i)~~\forall~i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+\,,$$ then there exists a holomorphic map $\sigma\!:U'\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma$ from a neighborhood of~$z_0'$ in $\Sigma'$ such that $\sigma(z_0')\!=\!z_0$ and $u'|_{U'}\!=\!u\!\circ\!\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: If the images of two J-holomorphic maps share a sequence of points accumulating at an immersed point, one map locally factors through the other.
assumptions: there exist sequences $z_i\!\in\!\Sigma\!-\!z_0$ and $z_i'\!\in\!\Sigma'\!-\!z_0'$ such~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i=z_0\,, \qquad \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i'=z_0'\,, \quad\hbox{and}\quad u(z_i)=u'(z_i)~~\forall~i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+\,,$$
conclusions: there exists a holomorphic map $\sigma\!:U'\!\longrightarrow\!\Sigma$ from a neighborhood of~$z_0'$ in $\Sigma'$ such that $\sigma(z_0')\!=\!z_0$ and $u'|_{U'}\!=\!u\!\circ\!\sigma$
nodes.label: FHS_crl2b

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.10
nodes.statement: It can be assumed that $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_0),(\Sigma',\mathfrak j',z_0')\!=\!(B_1,\mathfrak j_0,0)$, where $B_1\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is the unit ball with the standard complex structure. Since $\textnormal{d}_{z_0}u\!\neq\!0$ and $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, $u$ is an embedding near $0\!\in\!B_1$ and so is a slice in a coordinate system. Thus, we can assume that $$u,u'\!\equiv\!(v,w)\!: (B_1,0)\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1},0), \qquad u(z)=(z,0)\in\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,,$$ and $u,u'$ are $J$-holomorphic with respect to some almost complex structure $$J(x,y)=\left(\begin{array}{cc}J_{11}(x,y)& J_{12}(x,y)\\ J_{21}(x,y)& J_{22}(x,y)\end{array}\right)\!: \mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,, \qquad (x,y)\in\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,.$$ Since $J$ is $C^1$, \BE{Jexpand_e}J_{ij}(x,y)=J_{ij}(x,0)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J_{ij}(x,ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J_{ij}(x,0)+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}y_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{ij}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(x,ty)}\textnormal{d} t\,.\end{equation} Since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, \BE{J0cond_e} J_{21}(x,0)=0,\quad J_{22}(x,0)^2=-\textnormal{Id} \qquad\forall~x\in B_1\subset\mathbb{C}.\end{equation} Since $u'$ is $J$-holomorphic, $$ \partial_s w + J_{22}\big(v(z),w(z)\big)\partial_t w +J_{21}\big(v(z),w(z)\big)\partial_t v=0.$$ Combining this with~(\ref{Jexpand_e}) and the first equation in~(\ref{J0cond_e}), we find that \begin{gather*} \partial_s w + J_{22}\big(v(z),0\big)\partial_t w+C(z)w(z)=0, \qquad\hbox{where}\quad C\in L^p\big(B_1;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\big),\\ C(z)y=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}y_i\Bigg( \bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{22}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(v(z),tw(z))}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tw|_z +\bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{21}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(v(z),tw(z))}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tv|_z\Bigg)\,. \end{gather*} By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp} and the second identity in~(\ref{J0cond_e}), there thus exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,1)$, \hbox{$\Phi\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n-2}\mathbb R)$}, and holomorphic map $\wt{w}\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$ such~that $$w(z)=\Phi(z)\wt{w}(z) \qquad\forall~z\in B_{\delta}\,.$$ Since \hbox{$u'(z_i')\!=\!u(z_i)$}, $\wt{w}(z_i')\!=\!0$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$. Since $z_i'\!\longrightarrow\!0$ and $z_i'\!\neq\!0$, it follows that $w\!=\!0$. This implies the claim with $U'\!=\!B_{\delta}$ and $\sigma\!=\!v$.
nodes.statement_short: Put u in a slice chart, derive a perturbed Cauchy-Riemann equation for the normal component w of u', and use Carleman similarity and the accumulating zeros to get w = 0.

nodes.name: local model
nodes.statement: It can be assumed that $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,z_0),(\Sigma',\mathfrak j',z_0')\!=\!(B_1,\mathfrak j_0,0)$, where $B_1\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is the unit ball with the standard complex structure.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to maps from B_1 with base points 0.

nodes.name: slice coordinates
nodes.statement: Since $\textnormal{d}_{z_0}u\!\neq\!0$ and $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, $u$ is an embedding near $0\!\in\!B_1$ and so is a slice in a coordinate system. Thus, we can assume that $$u,u'\!\equiv\!(v,w)\!: (B_1,0)\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1},0), \qquad u(z)=(z,0)\in\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,,$$ and $u,u'$ are $J$-holomorphic with respect to some almost complex structure $$J(x,y)=\left(\begin{array}{cc}J_{11}(x,y)& J_{12}(x,y)\\ J_{21}(x,y)& J_{22}(x,y)\end{array}\right)\!: \mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,, \qquad (x,y)\in\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: u is an embedding near 0, so u(z) = (z,0) in suitable coordinates.

nodes.name: expand J
nodes.statement: Since $J$ is $C^1$, \BE{Jexpand_e}J_{ij}(x,y)=J_{ij}(x,0)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J_{ij}(x,ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J_{ij}(x,0)+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}y_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{ij}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(x,ty)}\textnormal{d} t\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expand J_{ij}(x,y) around y = 0.

nodes.name: Eq. Jexpand_e
nodes.statement: J_{ij}(x,y)=J_{ij}(x,0)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J_{ij}(x,ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t =J_{ij}(x,0)+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}y_i\!\! \int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{ij}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(x,ty)}\textnormal{d} t\,.

nodes.name: equation for w
nodes.statement: Since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, \BE{J0cond_e} J_{21}(x,0)=0,\quad J_{22}(x,0)^2=-\textnormal{Id} \qquad\forall~x\in B_1\subset\mathbb{C}.\end{equation} Since $u'$ is $J$-holomorphic, $$ \partial_s w + J_{22}\big(v(z),w(z)\big)\partial_t w +J_{21}\big(v(z),w(z)\big)\partial_t v=0.$$ Combining this with~(\ref{Jexpand_e}) and the first equation in~(\ref{J0cond_e}), we find that \begin{gather*} \partial_s w + J_{22}\big(v(z),0\big)\partial_t w+C(z)w(z)=0, \qquad\hbox{where}\quad C\in L^p\big(B_1;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\big),\\ C(z)y=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}y_i\Bigg( \bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{22}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(v(z),tw(z))}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tw|_z +\bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J_{21}}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{(v(z),tw(z))}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tv|_z\Bigg)\,. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: J-holomorphicity of u and u' gives a linear equation for w.

nodes.name: Eq. J0cond_e
nodes.statement: J_{21}(x,0)=0,\quad J_{22}(x,0)^2=-\textnormal{Id} \qquad\forall~x\in B_1\subset\mathbb{C}.

nodes.name: apply Carleman similarity
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp} and the second identity in~(\ref{J0cond_e}), there thus exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,1)$, \hbox{$\Phi\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n-2}\mathbb R)$}, and holomorphic map $\wt{w}\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$ such~that $$w(z)=\Phi(z)\wt{w}(z) \qquad\forall~z\in B_{\delta}\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: w = Phi w tilde with w tilde holomorphic.

nodes.name: w vanishes
nodes.statement: Since \hbox{$u'(z_i')\!=\!u(z_i)$}, $\wt{w}(z_i')\!=\!0$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$. Since $z_i'\!\longrightarrow\!0$ and $z_i'\!\neq\!0$, it follows that $w\!=\!0$. This implies the claim with $U'\!=\!B_{\delta}$ and $\sigma\!=\!v$.
nodes.statement_short: w tilde has accumulating zeros, so w = 0 and u' = u o v.

nodes.name: energy density at a point equals the order
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$ and $x\!\in\!X$ be such that $g$ is compatible with~$J$ at~$x$. If $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map from a compact Riemann surface with boundary, then $$\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\frac{E_g(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x)))}{\pi\delta^2}=\textnormal{ord}_xu\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: The energy in the preimage of a small ball around x, divided by pi delta^2, tends to ord_x u.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
$x\!\in\!X$ be such that $g$ is compatible with~$J$ at~$x$
$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map from a compact Riemann surface with boundary
conclusions: $$\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\frac{E_g(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x)))}{\pi\delta^2}=\textnormal{ord}_xu\,.$$
nodes.label: FHS_crl3

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.11
nodes.statement: By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $J$ agrees with the standard complex structure~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin, $g$ agrees with the standard metric~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin, $\Sigma\!=\!\ov{B_R}$ for some $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, and $u(0)\!=\!0$. In particular, there exists $C\!\ge\!1$ such that \BE{FHScrl3_e0} \big|J_x-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x|, \quad \big|g_x-g_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x| \qquad\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n~\hbox{s.t.}~|x|\le1,\end{equation} where $|\cdot|$ denotes the usual norm of~$x$ (i.e.~the distance to the origin with respect to~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$).\\ \noindent Let $\ell\!\equiv\!\textnormal{ord}_0u$ and $\alpha\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\!-\!0$ be as in Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}, where $0\!\in\!B_R$ is the origin in the domain of~$u$. Thus, there exist $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{FHScrl3_e1} u(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(z^{\ell}\!+\!f(z)\big),~~ \big|f(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation} Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ as before. By (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), there exists $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{FHScrl3_e2} u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_s(z)\big),~~ u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell \mathfrak i z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_t(z)\big),~~ \big|f_s(z)\big|,\big|f_t(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell} \quad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation} We can also assume that the three constants~$C$ in~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0}), (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}) are the same, $C\!\ge\!1$, $$C_{\alpha}\epsilon \equiv (C\!+\!C|\alpha|\!+\!C^2|\alpha|\big)\epsilon\le 1\,,$$ and $|u(z)|\!\le\!1$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$. By~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0})-(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}), \BE{FHScrl3_e5}\begin{split} \bigg|\frac{|u(z)|_g}{|\alpha||z|^{\ell}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg| &\le C|z|+C|\alpha||z|^{\ell}+C^2|\alpha||z|^{\ell+1}\\ &\le C_{\alpha}|z|\quad\forall~z\in B_{\epsilon}, \end{split}\end{equation} where $|\cdot|_g$ denotes the distance to the origin in~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with respect to the metric~$g$ and the corresponding norm on~$T\mathbb{C}^n$.\\ \noindent Given $r\!\in\!(0,1)$, let $\delta_r\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$ be such that \BE{FHScrl3_e7} C_{\alpha}\bigg(\frac{2\delta_r}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\le r\,.\end{equation} For any $\delta\!\in\![0,\delta_r]$, (\ref{FHScrl3_e5}) and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e7}) give \begin{alignat*}{2} |z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!+\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad u(z)\in B_{\delta}^g(0)\,,\\ u(z)&\in B_{\delta}^g(0) &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad |z|\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\,,\\ |z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad 1\!-\!r \le \frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}},\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}} \le 1\!+\!r. \end{alignat*} Combining these, we obtain \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1+r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}} (1\!-\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2 &\le \frac12\int_{u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))}\!\!\big(|u_s|_g^2\!+\!|u_t|_g^2\big)\\ &\le \int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1-r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}} (1\!+\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2 \,. \end{split}\end{equation*} Evaluating the outer integrals, we find that $$\bigg(\frac{1\!-\!r}{1\!+\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2 \le E_g\big(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))\big) \le \bigg(\frac{1\!+\!r}{1\!-\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2\,.$$ These inequalities hold for all $r\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_r)$; the claim is obtained by sending $r\!\longrightarrow\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Local expansion u = alpha(z^ell + f) near the preimage, compare |u| and |du| with the model, and integrate over the preimage of B_delta.

nodes.name: local model
nodes.statement: By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $J$ agrees with the standard complex structure~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin, $g$ agrees with the standard metric~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin, $\Sigma\!=\!\ov{B_R}$ for some $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, and $u(0)\!=\!0$. In particular, there exists $C\!\ge\!1$ such that \BE{FHScrl3_e0} \big|J_x-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x|, \quad \big|g_x-g_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x| \qquad\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n~\hbox{s.t.}~|x|\le1,\end{equation} where $|\cdot|$ denotes the usual norm of~$x$ (i.e.~the distance to the origin with respect to~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$).
nodes.statement_short: Work in C^n with J and g standard at 0.

nodes.name: Eq. FHScrl3_e0
nodes.statement: \big|J_x-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x|, \quad \big|g_x-g_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x| \qquad\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n~\hbox{s.t.}~|x|\le1,

nodes.name: leading-order expansion
nodes.statement: Let $\ell\!\equiv\!\textnormal{ord}_0u$ and $\alpha\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\!-\!0$ be as in Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}, where $0\!\in\!B_R$ is the origin in the domain of~$u$. Thus, there exist $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{FHScrl3_e1} u(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(z^{\ell}\!+\!f(z)\big),~~ \big|f(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: By Corollary 3.3, u = alpha(z^ell + f) with |f| <= C|z|^{ell+1}.

nodes.name: Eq. FHScrl3_e1
nodes.statement: u(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(z^{\ell}\!+\!f(z)\big),~~ \big|f(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.

nodes.name: derivative expansion
nodes.statement: Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ as before. By (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), there exists $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{FHScrl3_e2} u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_s(z)\big),~~ u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell \mathfrak i z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_t(z)\big),~~ \big|f_s(z)\big|,\big|f_t(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell} \quad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on the partial derivatives of u.

nodes.name: Eq. FHScrl3_e2
nodes.statement: u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_s(z)\big),~~ u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell \mathfrak i z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_t(z)\big),~~ \big|f_s(z)\big|,\big|f_t(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell} \quad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.

nodes.name: compare with the model map
nodes.statement: We can also assume that the three constants~$C$ in~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0}), (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}) are the same, $C\!\ge\!1$, $$C_{\alpha}\epsilon \equiv (C\!+\!C|\alpha|\!+\!C^2|\alpha|\big)\epsilon\le 1\,,$$ and $|u(z)|\!\le\!1$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$. By~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0})-(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}), \BE{FHScrl3_e5}\begin{split} \bigg|\frac{|u(z)|_g}{|\alpha||z|^{\ell}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg| &\le C|z|+C|\alpha||z|^{\ell}+C^2|\alpha||z|^{\ell+1}\\ &\le C_{\alpha}|z|\quad\forall~z\in B_{\epsilon}, \end{split}\end{equation} where $|\cdot|_g$ denotes the distance to the origin in~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with respect to the metric~$g$ and the corresponding norm on~$T\mathbb{C}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative errors of |u|, |u_s|, |u_t| are O(|z|).

nodes.name: Eq. FHScrl3_e5
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \bigg|\frac{|u(z)|_g}{|\alpha||z|^{\ell}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg|, \bigg|\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg| &\le C|z|+C|\alpha||z|^{\ell}+C^2|\alpha||z|^{\ell+1}\\ &\le C_{\alpha}|z|\quad\forall~z\in B_{\epsilon}, \end{split}

nodes.name: sandwich the preimage of the ball
nodes.statement: Given $r\!\in\!(0,1)$, let $\delta_r\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$ be such that \BE{FHScrl3_e7} C_{\alpha}\bigg(\frac{2\delta_r}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\le r\,.\end{equation} For any $\delta\!\in\![0,\delta_r]$, (\ref{FHScrl3_e5}) and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e7}) give \begin{alignat*}{2} |z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!+\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad u(z)\in B_{\delta}^g(0)\,,\\ u(z)&\in B_{\delta}^g(0) &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad |z|\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\,,\\ |z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad 1\!-\!r \le \frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}},\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}} \le 1\!+\!r. \end{alignat*}
nodes.statement_short: Preimage of B_delta lies between two disks and |du| is within a factor (1 +/- r) of the model.

nodes.name: Eq. FHScrl3_e7
nodes.statement: C_{\alpha}\bigg(\frac{2\delta_r}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\le r\,.

nodes.name: energy bounds
nodes.statement: Combining these, we obtain \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1+r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}} (1\!-\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2 &\le \frac12\int_{u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))}\!\!\big(|u_s|_g^2\!+\!|u_t|_g^2\big)\\ &\le \int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1-r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}} (1\!+\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2 \,. \end{split}\end{equation*} Evaluating the outer integrals, we find that $$\bigg(\frac{1\!-\!r}{1\!+\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2 \le E_g\big(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))\big) \le \bigg(\frac{1\!+\!r}{1\!-\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to bound E_g(u; u^{-1}(B_delta)) between multiples of ell pi delta^2.

nodes.name: let r tend to 0
nodes.statement: These inequalities hold for all $r\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_r)$; the claim is obtained by sending $r\!\longrightarrow\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Send r to 0.

nodes.name: Monotonicity Lemma
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$, there exists a continuous function $C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary, \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map, $x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are such that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then \BE{MonThm_e} E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.\end{equation} If $\omega(\cdot,\cdot)\equiv\!g(J\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symplectic form on~$X$, then the above fraction can be replaced by the product $\pi\delta^2\textnormal{e}^{-C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: A J-holomorphic map whose boundary avoids B_delta(x) has energy at least ord_x u times about pi delta^2.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary
conclusions: there exists a continuous function $C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property
E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.
the above fraction can be replaced by the product $\pi\delta^2\textnormal{e}^{-C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2}$
E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.
the above fraction can be replaced by the product $\pi\delta^2\textnormal{e}^{-C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2}$

nodes.label: MonotLmm_prp

nodes.name: Eq. MonThm_e
nodes.statement: E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.

nodes.name: L^2_1-norm controls C^0-norm only for J-holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: According to this proposition, ``completely getting out" of the ball $B_{\delta}(x)$ via a $J$-holomorphic map requires an energy bounded below by a little less than~$\pi\delta^2$. Thus, the $L^2_1$-norm of a $J$-holomorphic map~$u$ exerts some control over the $C^0$-norm of~$u$. If $p\!>\!2$, the $L^p_1$-norm of any smooth map~$f$ from a two-dimensional manifold controls the $C^0$-norm of~$f$. However, this is not the case of the $L^2_1$-norm, as illustrated by the example of \cite[Lemma~10.4.1]{MS12}: the function $$f_{\epsilon}\!:\mathbb R^2\longrightarrow[0,1], \qquad f_{\epsilon}(z)=\begin{cases}1,&\hbox{if}~|z|\le\epsilon;\\ \frac{\ln|z|}{\ln\epsilon},&\hbox{if}~\epsilon\le|z|\le1;\\ 0,&\hbox{if}~|z|\ge1; \end{cases}$$ with any $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,1)$ is continuous and satisfies $$\int_{\mathbb R^2}|\textnormal{d} f_{\epsilon}|_g^2=-\frac{2\pi}{\ln\epsilon}\,.$$ It is arbitrarily close in the $L^2_1$-norm to a smooth function~$\ti{f}_{\epsilon}$. Thus, it is possible to ``completely get out" of $B_{\delta}^g(x)$ using a smooth function with arbitrarily small energy ($\ti{f}_{\delta}$ does this for the ball $B_1(1)$ in~$\mathbb R$).
nodes.statement_short: Escaping a ball needs energy about pi delta^2 for J-holomorphic maps, unlike general maps, as the log cutoff function of [MS12] shows.

nodes.name: holomorphic maps minimize the modified energy
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{Egexp_e}), the holomorphic maps are the local minima of the functional $$C^{\infty}(\Sigma;X)\longrightarrow\mathbb R, \qquad f\longrightarrow E_g(f)-\int_{\Sigma}f^*\omega_J\,,$$ for every compact Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ without boundary.

nodes.name: proof outline of the Monotonicity Lemma
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{CritEner_lmm} implies that the ratio of $E_g(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x)))$ and the fraction on the right-hand side~(\ref{MonThm_e}) is a non-decreasing function of~$\delta$, as long as \hbox{$u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$}. By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl3}, this ratio approaches $\textnormal{ord}_xu$ as~$\delta$ approaches~0. These two statements imply Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp}.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: Lemma 3.16 makes the energy ratio monotone in delta and Corollary 3.11 gives its limit ord_x u.

nodes.name: monotone ratio
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{CritEner_lmm} implies that the ratio of $E_g(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x)))$ and the fraction on the right-hand side~(\ref{MonThm_e}) is a non-decreasing function of~$\delta$, as long as \hbox{$u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.16 makes the ratio non-decreasing.

nodes.name: limit of the ratio
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl3}, this ratio approaches $\textnormal{ord}_xu$ as~$\delta$ approaches~0.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 3.11 gives the limit ord_x u.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: These two statements imply Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine.

nodes.name: exponential map
nodes.statement: Let $(X,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold. Denote by $\exp\!:\mathcal W_g\!\longrightarrow\!X$, the exponential map from a neighborhood of~$X$ in~$TX$ with respect to the Levi-Civita connection~$\nabla$ of~$g$.

nodes.name: geodesic gamma_v
nodes.statement: For each $v\!\in\!TX$, we denote~by $$\gamma_v\!:[0,1]\longrightarrow X, \qquad \gamma_v(\tau)=\exp_x(\tau v),$$ the geodesic with $\gamma_v'(0)\!=\!v$.

nodes.name: injectivity radius and distance function
nodes.statement: Let $$r_g\!:X\longrightarrow\mathbb R^+ \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad d_g\!:X\!\times\!X\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{\ge0}$$ be the injectivity radius of~$\exp$ and the distance function.

nodes.name: vector field zeta_x
nodes.statement: For each $x\!\in\!X$, define $$\zeta_x\in\Gamma\big(B_{r_g(x)}^g(x);TX\big) \quad\hbox{by}\quad \exp_y\!\big(\zeta_x(y)\!\big)=x, ~g\big(\!\zeta_x(y),\zeta_x(y)\!\big)<r_g(x)^2 ~~\forall\,y\!\in\!B_{r_g(x)}^g(x).$$
nodes.statement_short: zeta_x(y) is the tangent vector at y whose geodesic reaches x.

nodes.name: derivative of the squared distance
nodes.statement: Let $(X,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold and $x\!\in\!X$. If $\alpha\!:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a smooth curve such that $\alpha(0)\!\in\!B_{r_g(x)}^g(x)$, then $$\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}d_g\big(x,\alpha(\tau)\big)^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =-g\big(\alpha'(0),\zeta_x(\alpha(0))\big)\,.$$
assumptions: $\alpha\!:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a smooth curve such that $\alpha(0)\!\in\!B_{r_g(x)}^g(x)$
conclusions: $$\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}d_g\big(x,\alpha(\tau)\big)^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =-g\big(\alpha'(0),\zeta_x(\alpha(0))\big)\,.$$
nodes.label: distder_lmm

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 3.13
nodes.statement: If $\beta(\tau)\!=\!\exp_x^{-1}\alpha(\tau)$, then $$\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}d_g\big(x,\alpha(\tau)\big)^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}|\beta(\tau)|^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =g\big(\beta'(0),\beta(0)\big)\,.$$ By Gauss's Lemma, $$g\big(\beta'(0),\beta(0)\big) =g\big(\{\textnormal{d}_{\beta(0)}\exp_x\}(\beta'(0)),\{\textnormal{d}_{\beta(0)}\exp_x\}(\beta(0))\!\big) =g\big(\alpha'(0),-\zeta_x(\alpha(0))\big)\,.$$ This establishes the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Pull back by exp_x and apply Gauss's Lemma.

nodes.name: differentiate in exponential coordinates
nodes.statement: If $\beta(\tau)\!=\!\exp_x^{-1}\alpha(\tau)$, then $$\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}d_g\big(x,\alpha(\tau)\big)^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}|\beta(\tau)|^2\bigg|_{\tau=0} =g\big(\beta'(0),\beta(0)\big)\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: In exponential coordinates the derivative is g(beta', beta).

nodes.name: apply Gauss's Lemma
nodes.statement: By Gauss's Lemma, $$g\big(\beta'(0),\beta(0)\big) =g\big(\{\textnormal{d}_{\beta(0)}\exp_x\}(\beta'(0)),\{\textnormal{d}_{\beta(0)}\exp_x\}(\beta(0))\!\big) =g\big(\alpha'(0),-\zeta_x(\alpha(0))\big)\,.$$ This establishes the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Gauss's Lemma converts this into -g(alpha', zeta_x).

nodes.name: Jacobi field estimate
nodes.statement: If $(X,g)$ is a Riemannian manifold, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property. If $x\!\in\!X$, $v\!\in\!T_xX$ with $|v|_g\!<\!\frac12r_g(x)$, and $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!J(\tau)$ is a Jacobi vector field along the geodesic~$\gamma_v$ with $J(0)\!=\!0$, then $$\big|J'(1)-J(1)\big|_g\le C_g(x)|v|_g^2\big|J(1)\big|_g\,.$$
assumptions: $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!J(\tau)$ is a Jacobi vector field along the geodesic~$\gamma_v$ with $J(0)\!=\!0$
conclusions: there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property
nodes.label: JacDer_lmm

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 3.14
nodes.statement: Let $R_g$ be the Riemann curvature tensor of~$g$ and $f(\tau)\!=\!|\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)|_g$. Then, $f(0)\!=\!0$ and \begin{equation*}\begin{split} f(\tau)f'(\tau)=\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}f(\tau)^2 =g\big(\tau J''(\tau),\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)\!\big) &=\tau g\big(R(\gamma'(\tau),J(\tau))\gamma'(\tau),\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)\big)\\ &\le C_g(x)|v|_g^2|J(\tau)|_g\tau f(\tau). \end{split}\end{equation*} If $C_g$ is sufficiently large, then $|J(\tau)|_g\!\le\!C_g(x)|J(1)|_g$. Thus, $$f(\tau)f'(\tau)\le C_g(x)|v|_g^2|J_v(\tau)|_g\tau f(\tau) \le C_g(x)^2|v|_g^2|J(1)|_g\tau f(\tau), \quad f'(\tau)\le C_g(x)^2|v|_g^2|J(1)|_g\tau.$$ The claim follows from the last inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Differential inequality for f = |tau J' - J| via the Jacobi equation and curvature bound.

nodes.name: differentiate f
nodes.statement: Let $R_g$ be the Riemann curvature tensor of~$g$ and $f(\tau)\!=\!|\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)|_g$. Then, $f(0)\!=\!0$ and \begin{equation*}\begin{split} f(\tau)f'(\tau)=\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}f(\tau)^2 =g\big(\tau J''(\tau),\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)\!\big) &=\tau g\big(R(\gamma'(\tau),J(\tau))\gamma'(\tau),\tau J'(\tau)\!-\!J(\tau)\big)\\ &\le C_g(x)|v|_g^2|J(\tau)|_g\tau f(\tau). \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the Jacobi equation to bound f f'.

nodes.name: bound f'
nodes.statement: If $C_g$ is sufficiently large, then $|J(\tau)|_g\!\le\!C_g(x)|J(1)|_g$. Thus, $$f(\tau)f'(\tau)\le C_g(x)|v|_g^2|J_v(\tau)|_g\tau f(\tau) \le C_g(x)^2|v|_g^2|J(1)|_g\tau f(\tau), \quad f'(\tau)\le C_g(x)^2|v|_g^2|J(1)|_g\tau.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound |J(tau)| by |J(1)| to get f' <= C|v|^2|J(1)| tau.

nodes.name: integrate
nodes.statement: The claim follows from the last inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the bound on f'.

nodes.name: covariant derivative of zeta_x is close to minus the identity
nodes.statement: If $(X,g)$ is a Riemannian manifold, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property. If $x\!\in\!X$, then $$\big|\nabla_w\zeta_x|_y+w\big|_g\le C_g(x)d_g(x,y)^2|w|_g \qquad \forall~w\!\in\!T_yX,~y\!\in\!B_{r_g(x)/2}^g(x).$$
conclusions: there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property
$$\big|\nabla_w\zeta_x|_y+w\big|_g\le C_g(x)d_g(x,y)^2|w|_g \qquad \forall~w\!\in\!T_yX,~y\!\in\!B_{r_g(x)/2}^g(x).$$
nodes.label: JacDer_crl

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 3.15
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(s,\tau)$ be a family of geodesics such that $$u(s,0)=x,\qquad u(0,1)=y, \qquad \frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d} s}u(s,1)\bigg|_{s=0}=w.$$ Since $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(s,\tau)$ is a geodesic, \begin{gather*} \frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}u(s,\tau)\bigg|_{\tau=1} =\big\{\!\textnormal{d}_{u_{\tau}(s,0)}\exp_x\!\big\}\big(u_{\tau}(s,0)\big) =-\zeta_x\big(u(s,1)\big),\\ \frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d} s}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)} =\frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d} s}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)} =-\nabla_w\zeta_x|_y\,. \end{gather*} Furthermore, $J(\tau)\!\equiv\!\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d} s}u(s,\tau)\big|_{s=0}$ is a Jacobi vector field along the geodesic $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(0,\tau)$ with $$J(0)=\!0,\quad J(1)=w, \quad J'(1)=\frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d} s}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)}=- \nabla_w\zeta_x|_y\,.$$ Thus, the claim follows from Lemma~\ref{JacDer_lmm}.
nodes.statement_short: Realize the variation of zeta_x as a Jacobi field along a geodesic and apply Lemma 3.14.

nodes.name: family of geodesics
nodes.statement: Let $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(s,\tau)$ be a family of geodesics such that $$u(s,0)=x,\qquad u(0,1)=y, \qquad \frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d} s}u(s,1)\bigg|_{s=0}=w.$$
nodes.statement_short: Take a family of geodesics from x with endpoint variation w.

nodes.name: derivatives at tau = 1
nodes.statement: Since $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(s,\tau)$ is a geodesic, \begin{gather*} \frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}u(s,\tau)\bigg|_{\tau=1} =\big\{\!\textnormal{d}_{u_{\tau}(s,0)}\exp_x\!\big\}\big(u_{\tau}(s,0)\big) =-\zeta_x\big(u(s,1)\big),\\ \frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d} s}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)} =\frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d} s}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)} =-\nabla_w\zeta_x|_y\,. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the derivatives at tau = 1 through zeta_x and its covariant derivative.

nodes.name: Jacobi field
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $J(\tau)\!\equiv\!\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d} s}u(s,\tau)\big|_{s=0}$ is a Jacobi vector field along the geodesic $\tau\!\longrightarrow\!u(0,\tau)$ with $$J(0)=\!0,\quad J(1)=w, \quad J'(1)=\frac{\textnormal{D}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\frac{\textnormal{d} u(s,\tau)}{\textnormal{d} s}\bigg|_{(s,\tau)=(0,1)}=- \nabla_w\zeta_x|_y\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: The variation field is a Jacobi field with J(1) = w and J'(1) = -nabla_w zeta_x.

nodes.name: apply Lemma 3.14
nodes.statement: Thus, the claim follows from Lemma~\ref{JacDer_lmm}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.14.

nodes.name: first variation of the modified energy
nodes.statement:
Suppose $(X,\omega)$ is a symplectic manifold, $J$ is an almost complex structure on~$X$ tamed by~$\omega$, and $
abla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of the metric~$g_J$. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map, then $$\int_{\Sigma}g_J ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi ig)= \int_{\Sigma} ig(u^*\{
abla_{\xi}\omega_J\}\!+\! \omega_J(	extnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi) ig) \qquad orall~\xi\!\in\!\Gamma(\Sigma;u^*TX)~\hbox{s.t.}~\xi|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing of the first variation of E_{g_J} minus the omega_J term for J-holomorphic maps, for variations vanishing on the boundary.
assumptions: $J$ is an almost complex structure on~$X$ tamed by~$\omega$
$\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of the metric~$g_J$
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary
conclusions:
$$\int_{\Sigma}g_J ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi ig)= \int_{\Sigma} ig(u^*\{
abla_{\xi}\omega_J\}\!+\! \omega_J(	extnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi) ig) \qquad orall~\xi\!\in\!\Gamma(\Sigma;u^*TX)~\hbox{s.t.}~\xi|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0.$$
nodes.label: CritEner_lmm

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 3.16
nodes.statement:
For $	au\!\in\!\mathbb R$ sufficiently close to~0, define $$u_{	au}\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow X, \qquad u_{	au}(z)\!=\!\exp_{u(z)}(	au\xi(z)).$$ Since $\xi|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0$, $u_{	au}|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!u|_{\partial\Sigma}$. Denote by $\wh\Sigma$ the closed oriented surface obtained by gluing two copies of~$\Sigma$ along the common boundary and reversing the orientation on the second copy. Let $$\wh{u}_{	au}\!: \wh\Sigma\longrightarrow X$$ be the map restricting to~$u_{	au}$ on the first copy of~$\Sigma$ and to~$u$ on the second.\ 
oindent By~(ef{Egexp_e}), $$E(	au)\equiv E_{g_J}(u_{	au})-\int_{\Sigma}u_{	au}^*\omega_J-E_{g_J}(u) =\int_{\wh\Sigma}\wh{u}_{	au}^*\omega+ 2\int_{\Sigma}g_J ig( ar\partial u_{	au}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\! ar\partial u_{	au} ig) \ge0\quad orall	au.$$ Since $\omega$ is closed and $\wh{u}_*$ represents the zero class in $H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})$, the first integral on the right-hand side above vanishes. Thus, the function \hbox{$	au\!\longrightarrow\!E(	au)$} is minimized at $	au\!=\!0$ (when it equals 0) and~so \BE{Ediff_e2} egin{split} 0=E'(0) &= rac{	extnormal{d}}{	extnormal{d}	au} igg(E_{g_J}(u_{	au}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{	au}^*\omega_J igg) igg|_{	au=0}\ &= rac{	extnormal{d}}{	extnormal{d}	au} igg(  rac12\int_{\Sigma}\!\!g_J(	extnormal{d} u_{	au}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!	extnormal{d} u_{	au}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{	au}^*\omega_J igg) igg|_{	au=0}\,; \end{split}\end{equation} the last equality above uses the definition of $E(u_{	au})$ in~(ef{Egfdfn_e}).\ 
oindent Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ be a local coordinate on~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$. Since $
abla$ is torsion-free, $$ rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_s\Big|_{	au=0} \equiv rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au} rac{	extnormal{d} u_{	au}}{	extnormal{d} s} igg|_{	au=0} = rac{D}{	extnormal{d} s} rac{	extnormal{d} u_{	au}}{	extnormal{d}	au} igg|_{	au=0} = rac{D}{	extnormal{d} s}\xi\equiv
abla_s\xi, \qquad  rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_t\Big|_{	au=0}=
abla_t\xi\,.$$ Since $
abla$ is also $g$-compatible,  egin{gather*} egin{split}  rac12 rac{	extnormal{d}}{	extnormal{d}	au}g_J(	extnormal{d} u_{	au}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!	extnormal{d} u_{	au})  igg|_{	au=0} &= igg(g_J igg(u_s, rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_s\Big|_{	au=0} igg) +g_J igg(u_t, rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_t\Big|_{	au=0} igg)\! igg) 	extnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!	extnormal{d} t\ &=g_J(u_s,
abla_s\xi)+g_J(u_t,
abla_t\xi) =g_J ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi ig)\,, \end{split}\  egin{split}  rac{	extnormal{d}}{	extnormal{d}	au}u_{	au}^*\omega_J igg|_{	au=0} &= igg(\!\! ig\{
abla_{\xi}\omega_J ig\}(u_s,u_t)+ \omega_J igg( rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_s\Big|_{	au=0},u_t\!\! igg) +\omega_J igg(\!\!u_s, rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_t\Big|_{	au=0} igg)\! igg) 	extnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!	extnormal{d} t\ &=u^*\{
abla_{\xi}\omega_J\}\!+\!\omega_J ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi ig)\,. \end{split}\end{gather*} Combining this with~(ef{Ediff_e2}), we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Variational argument: the modified energy of the variation u_tau minus that of u is a nonnegative function minimized at tau = 0; differentiate at tau = 0.

nodes.name: variation and doubled surface
nodes.statement: For $\tau\!\in\!\mathbb R$ sufficiently close to~0, define $$u_{\tau}\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow X, \qquad u_{\tau}(z)\!=\!\exp_{u(z)}(\tau\xi(z)).$$ Since $\xi|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0$, $u_{\tau}|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!u|_{\partial\Sigma}$. Denote by $\wh\Sigma$ the closed oriented surface obtained by gluing two copies of~$\Sigma$ along the common boundary and reversing the orientation on the second copy. Let $$\wh{u}_{\tau}\!: \wh\Sigma\longrightarrow X$$ be the map restricting to~$u_{\tau}$ on the first copy of~$\Sigma$ and to~$u$ on the second.
nodes.statement_short: Define u_tau = exp_u(tau xi) and the doubled map on the closed surface.

nodes.name: the modified energy is minimized at 0
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{Egexp_e}), $$E(\tau)\equiv E_{g_J}(u_{\tau})-\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J-E_{g_J}(u) =\int_{\wh\Sigma}\wh{u}_{\tau}^*\omega+ 2\int_{\Sigma}g_J\big(\bar\partial u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\bar\partial u_{\tau}\big) \ge0\quad\forall\tau.$$ Since $\omega$ is closed and $\wh{u}_*$ represents the zero class in $H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})$, the first integral on the right-hand side above vanishes. Thus, the function \hbox{$\tau\!\longrightarrow\!E(\tau)$} is minimized at $\tau\!=\!0$ (when it equals 0) and~so \BE{Ediff_e2}\begin{split} 0=E'(0) &=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg(E_{g_J}(u_{\tau}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\\ &=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg( \frac12\int_{\Sigma}\!\!g_J(\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\,; \end{split}\end{equation} the last equality above uses the definition of $E(u_{\tau})$ in~(\ref{Egfdfn_e}).
nodes.statement_short: By the energy identity E(tau) >= 0 = E(0), so E'(0) = 0.

nodes.name: Eq. Ediff_e2
nodes.statement: \begin{split} 0=E'(0) &=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg(E_{g_J}(u_{\tau}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\\ &=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg( \frac12\int_{\Sigma}\!\!g_J(\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}) -\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\,; \end{split}

nodes.name: commute derivatives
nodes.statement:
Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ be a local coordinate on~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$. Since $
abla$ is torsion-free, $$ rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_s\Big|_{	au=0} \equiv rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au} rac{	extnormal{d} u_{	au}}{	extnormal{d} s} igg|_{	au=0} = rac{D}{	extnormal{d} s} rac{	extnormal{d} u_{	au}}{	extnormal{d}	au} igg|_{	au=0} = rac{D}{	extnormal{d} s}\xi\equiv
abla_s\xi, \qquad  rac{D}{	extnormal{d}	au}(u_{	au})_t\Big|_{	au=0}=
abla_t\xi\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Torsion-freeness gives D_tau (u_tau)_s = nabla_s xi.

nodes.name: differentiate the integrands
nodes.statement_short: Compute the tau-derivatives of the energy density and of u_tau^* omega_J.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.statement: Combining this with~(\ref{Ediff_e2}), we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with E'(0) = 0.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 3.12 (Monotonicity Lemma)
nodes.statement:
Let $\delta_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ be a continuous function such that for every $x\!\in\!X$ there exists a symplectic form~$\omega_x$ on $B_{2\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$ so that~$J$ is tamed by~$\omega_x$ on $B_{2\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$ and compatible with~$\omega_x$ at~$x$. We assume that $2\delta_g(x)\!\le\!r_g(x)$ for every $x\!\in\!X$. It is sufficient to establish the proposition for each $x\!\in\!X$ and each $\delta\!\le\!\delta_g(x)$ under the assumption that the metric~$g$ is determined by~$J$ and~$\omega_x$ on $B_{\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$.\ 
oindent Choose a $C^{\infty}$-function $\eta\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\![0,1]$ such that \BE{etadfn_e}\eta(	au)= egin{cases}1,&\hbox{if}~	au\le rac12;\ 0,&\hbox{if}~	au\ge1; \end{cases} \qquad \eta'(	au)\le0.\end{equation} For a compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, a smooth map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, $x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, define  egin{gather*} \eta_{u,x,\delta}\in C^{\infty}(\Sigma;\mathbb R), \qquad \eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)=\eta igg( rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta} igg),\ E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)= rac12\int_{\Sigma} \eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!	extnormal{d} u ig)\,,\quad E_{u,x}(\delta)=E_g ig(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x)) ig). \end{gather*} \vspace{.2in} 
oindent We show in the remainder of this proof that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that \BE{Aetabd_e} -\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le 2C_{g,J}(x)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)+C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)\end{equation} for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and \hbox{$\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$} such that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$. This inequality is equivalent~to $$ igg(E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta) igg/ rac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4} igg)'\ge 0.$$ By Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem, $E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)$ approaches~$E_{u,x}(\delta)$ from below as~$\eta$ approaches the characteristic function~$\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$ of~$(-\infty,1)$. Thus, the function $$\delta\longrightarrow E_{u,x}(\delta) igg/ rac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}$$ is non-decreasing as long as $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$. By Corollary~ef{FHS_crl3}, $$\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0} igg(E_{u,x}(\delta)\!\! igg/\!\! rac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4} igg) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0} rac{E_{u,x}(\delta)}{\delta^2}= ig(	extnormal{ord}_xu ig)\pi.$$ This implies the first claim.\ 
oindent Fix $x\!\in\!X$. We note~that \BE{MonLem_e6} E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)=- rac12\int_{\Sigma}\eta'\! igg(\! rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\! igg)  rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta^2} g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!	extnormal{d} u ig).\end{equation} For a compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, a smooth map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and \hbox{$\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$}, let $$\xi_{u,x,\delta}\in \Gamma(\Sigma;u^*TX), \qquad \xi_{u,x,\delta}(z)=-\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\zeta_x ig(u(z) ig);$$ the vanishing assumption in~(ef{etadfn_e}) implies that $\xi_{u,x,\delta}$ is well-defined. If $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then $\xi_{u,x,\delta}|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0$. By Lemma~ef{distder_lmm}, \BE{MonLem_e0} egin{split} 
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta}|_z =\eta' igg( rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta} igg) rac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))} g ig(	extnormal{d}_zu,\zeta_x(u(z))\! ig)\zeta_x(u(z)) -\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)
abla\zeta_x\!\circ\!	extnormal{d}_zu. \end{split}\end{equation} Along with Corollary~ef{JacDer_crl}, (ef{MonLem_e6}), and the last assumption in~(ef{etadfn_e}), this implies~that \BE{MonLem_e8} \int_{\Sigma}\!d_g(x,u(z)) ig|g(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta}) ig| \le 2\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2 ig(1\!+\!C_g(x)\delta^2 ig)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta).\end{equation} \vspace{.1in} 
oindent By the $\omega_x$-compatibility assumption on~$J$ at~$x$, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that $$\int_{\Sigma} ig|(\omega_x)_J(	extnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta}) ig| \le C(x)\!\!\int_{\Sigma}d_g ig(x,u(z)\! ig) ig|g(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta}) ig|$$ for all $u$ and $\delta$ as above. Along with this, Lemma~ef{CritEner_lmm} implies that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that $$ igg|\int_{\Sigma}g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig) igg| \le C(x)\!\!\int_{\Sigma}\! ig(g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!	extnormal{d} u ig)|\xi_{u,x,\delta}| \!+\!d_g(x,u(z)) ig|g(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta}) ig| ig)$$ for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$ such that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$. Combining this with~(ef{MonLem_e8}), we conclude that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that \BE{MonLem_e0b}  igg|\int_{\Sigma}g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig) igg| \le C(x) ig(\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\!+\!\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta) ig)\end{equation} for all $u$ and $\delta$ as above.\ 
oindent Suppose $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary, $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a smooth map, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$. Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ be a coordinate on~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$. By~(ef{MonLem_e0}), \BE{MonLem_e1} egin{split} g ig(u_s,
abla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig) =\eta' igg(\! rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\! igg) rac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))}g ig(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z)) ig)^2&\ +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)g ig(u_s,
abla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z ig)&. \end{split}\end{equation} By Corollary~ef{JacDer_crl}, \BE{MonLem_e2} |u_s|^2\le g ig(u_s,
abla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z ig) +C_g(x)d_g(x,u(z))^2|u_s|^2 \quad orall\,z\!\in\!u^{-1} ig(B_{\delta_g(x)}^g(x) ig)\,.\end{equation} If $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, then $|u_s|\!=\!|u_t|$, $\lr{u_s,u_t}\!=\!0$, and \BE{MonLem_e3}  rac12 ig(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2 ig)d_g(x,u(z))^2=|u_s|^2|\zeta_x(u(z))|^2 \ge g ig(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z)) ig)^2+g ig(u_t,\zeta_x(u(z)) ig)^2\,.\end{equation} Since $\eta'\!\le\!0$, (ef{MonLem_e1})-(ef{MonLem_e3}) give \BE{MonLem_e4} egin{split} & rac12\eta' igg(\! rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\! igg) rac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta} ig(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2 ig) +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z) ig(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2 ig)\ &\qquad\le g ig(u_s,
abla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig)+g ig(u_t,
abla_t\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig)+ C_g(x)\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)d_g(x,u(z))^2 ig(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2 ig). \end{split}\end{equation} Along with~(ef{MonLem_e6}), this implies that \BE{MonLem_e9}-\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le \int_{\Sigma}g ig(	extnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!
abla\xi_{u,x,\delta} ig) +2C_g(x)\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\end{equation} for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$. Combining this inequality with~(ef{MonLem_e0b}), we obtain~(ef{Aetabd_e}).\ 
oindent Suppose $\omega\!\equiv\!g(J\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symplectic form on~$X$. By Lemma~ef{CritEner_lmm}, the left-hand side of~(ef{MonLem_e0b}) then vanishes. From~(ef{MonLem_e9}), we thus obtain $$-\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le 2C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\,.$$ The reasoning below~(ef{Aetabd_e}) now yields the second claim.
nodes.statement_short: Smoothed energy E_{u,x,eta}(delta) satisfies a differential inequality making its ratio to delta^2/(1+C delta)^4 non-decreasing; the limit at 0 is ord_x u pi by Corollary 3.11. The key step tests Lemma 3.16 with the vector field -eta zeta_x.

nodes.name: local symplectic forms
nodes.statement: Let $\delta_g\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ be a continuous function such that for every $x\!\in\!X$ there exists a symplectic form~$\omega_x$ on $B_{2\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$ so that~$J$ is tamed by~$\omega_x$ on $B_{2\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$ and compatible with~$\omega_x$ at~$x$. We assume that $2\delta_g(x)\!\le\!r_g(x)$ for every $x\!\in\!X$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose delta_g with local taming symplectic forms omega_x compatible at x.

nodes.name: localize
nodes.statement: It is sufficient to establish the proposition for each $x\!\in\!X$ and each $\delta\!\le\!\delta_g(x)$ under the assumption that the metric~$g$ is determined by~$J$ and~$\omega_x$ on $B_{\delta_g(x)}^g(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to delta <= delta_g(x) with g determined by J and omega_x.

nodes.name: cutoff and smoothed energies
nodes.statement: Choose a $C^{\infty}$-function $\eta\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\![0,1]$ such that \BE{etadfn_e}\eta(\tau)=\begin{cases}1,&\hbox{if}~\tau\le\frac12;\\ 0,&\hbox{if}~\tau\ge1; \end{cases} \qquad \eta'(\tau)\le0.\end{equation} For a compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, a smooth map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, $x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, define \begin{gather*} \eta_{u,x,\delta}\in C^{\infty}(\Sigma;\mathbb R), \qquad \eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)=\eta\bigg(\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\bigg),\\ E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)=\frac12\int_{\Sigma} \eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u\big)\,,\quad E_{u,x}(\delta)=E_g\big(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(x))\big). \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Define the cutoff eta and the energies E_{u,x,eta}, E_{u,x}.

nodes.name: Eq. etadfn_e
nodes.statement: \eta(\tau)=\begin{cases}1,&\hbox{if}~\tau\le\frac12;\\ 0,&\hbox{if}~\tau\ge1; \end{cases} \qquad \eta'(\tau)\le0.

nodes.name: reduce to a differential inequality
nodes.statement: We show in the remainder of this proof that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that \BE{Aetabd_e} -\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le 2C_{g,J}(x)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)+C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)\end{equation} for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and \hbox{$\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$} such that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$. This inequality is equivalent~to $$\bigg(E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\bigg/\frac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}\bigg)'\ge 0.$$
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to prove (3.4), equivalent to monotonicity of the normalized smoothed energy.

nodes.name: Eq. Aetabd_e
nodes.statement: -\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le 2C_{g,J}(x)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)+C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)

nodes.name: pass to the sharp cutoff
nodes.statement: By Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem, $E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)$ approaches~$E_{u,x}(\delta)$ from below as~$\eta$ approaches the characteristic function~$\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$ of~$(-\infty,1)$. Thus, the function $$\delta\longrightarrow E_{u,x}(\delta)\bigg/\frac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}$$ is non-decreasing as long as $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity passes to E_{u,x}(delta) by dominated convergence.

nodes.name: first claim
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl3}, $$\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\bigg(E_{u,x}(\delta)\!\!\bigg/\!\!\frac{\delta^2}{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}\bigg) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\frac{E_{u,x}(\delta)}{\delta^2}=\big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\pi.$$ This implies the first claim.
nodes.statement_short: The limit at delta = 0 is ord_x u pi, giving the first claim.

nodes.name: derivative of the smoothed energy
nodes.statement: Fix $x\!\in\!X$. We note~that \BE{MonLem_e6} E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)=-\frac12\int_{\Sigma}\eta'\!\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg) \frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta^2} g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u\big).\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Formula for E'_{u,x,eta}.

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e6
nodes.statement: E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)=-\frac12\int_{\Sigma}\eta'\!\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg) \frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta^2} g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u\big).

nodes.name: test vector field
nodes.statement: For a compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, a smooth map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and \hbox{$\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$}, let $$\xi_{u,x,\delta}\in \Gamma(\Sigma;u^*TX), \qquad \xi_{u,x,\delta}(z)=-\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\zeta_x\big(u(z)\big);$$ the vanishing assumption in~(\ref{etadfn_e}) implies that $\xi_{u,x,\delta}$ is well-defined. If $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then $\xi_{u,x,\delta}|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define xi_{u,x,delta} = -eta zeta_x(u), vanishing on the boundary.

nodes.name: covariant derivative of xi
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{distder_lmm}, \BE{MonLem_e0}\begin{split} \nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}|_z =\eta'\bigg(\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\bigg)\frac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))} g\big(\textnormal{d}_zu,\zeta_x(u(z))\!\big)\zeta_x(u(z)) -\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\nabla\zeta_x\!\circ\!\textnormal{d}_zu. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compute nabla xi via Lemma 3.13.

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e0
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}|_z =\eta'\bigg(\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\bigg)\frac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))} g\big(\textnormal{d}_zu,\zeta_x(u(z))\!\big)\zeta_x(u(z)) -\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\nabla\zeta_x\!\circ\!\textnormal{d}_zu. \end{split}

nodes.name: bound (3.6)
nodes.statement: Along with Corollary~\ref{JacDer_crl}, (\ref{MonLem_e6}), and the last assumption in~(\ref{etadfn_e}), this implies~that \BE{MonLem_e8} \int_{\Sigma}\!d_g(x,u(z))\big|g(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta})\big| \le 2\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2\big(1\!+\!C_g(x)\delta^2\big)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta).\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the weighted integral of g(du, nabla xi).

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e8
nodes.statement: \int_{\Sigma}\!d_g(x,u(z))\big|g(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta})\big| \le 2\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2\big(1\!+\!C_g(x)\delta^2\big)\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta).

nodes.name: bound the omega_J term
nodes.statement: By the $\omega_x$-compatibility assumption on~$J$ at~$x$, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that $$\int_{\Sigma}\big|(\omega_x)_J(\textnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta})\big| \le C(x)\!\!\int_{\Sigma}d_g\big(x,u(z)\!\big)\big|g(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta})\big|$$ for all $u$ and $\delta$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: The (omega_x)_J term is controlled by d_g times the g term.

nodes.name: apply Lemma 3.16
nodes.statement: Along with this, Lemma~\ref{CritEner_lmm} implies that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that $$\bigg|\int_{\Sigma}g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)\bigg| \le C(x)\!\!\int_{\Sigma}\!\big(g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u\big)|\xi_{u,x,\delta}| \!+\!d_g(x,u(z))\big|g(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta})\big|\big)$$ for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$ such that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: The first variation formula bounds the integral of g(du, nabla xi).

nodes.name: bound (3.7)
nodes.statement: Combining this with~(\ref{MonLem_e8}), we conclude that there exists a continuous function \hbox{$C\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} such~that \BE{MonLem_e0b} \bigg|\int_{\Sigma}g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)\bigg| \le C(x)\big(\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\!+\!\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)\big)\end{equation} for all $u$ and $\delta$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain (3.7).

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e0b
nodes.statement: \bigg|\int_{\Sigma}g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)\bigg| \le C(x)\big(\delta E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\!+\!\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)\big)

nodes.name: pointwise formula
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary, $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a smooth map, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$. Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ be a coordinate on~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$. By~(\ref{MonLem_e0}), \BE{MonLem_e1}\begin{split} g\big(u_s,\nabla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big) =\eta'\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg)\frac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))}g\big(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2&\\ +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)g\big(u_s,\nabla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z\big)&. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expand g(u_s, nabla_s xi).

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e1
nodes.statement: \begin{split} g\big(u_s,\nabla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big) =\eta'\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg)\frac{1}{\delta\,d_g(x,u(z))}g\big(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2&\\ +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)g\big(u_s,\nabla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z\big)&. \end{split}

nodes.name: apply Corollary 3.15
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{JacDer_crl}, \BE{MonLem_e2} |u_s|^2\le g\big(u_s,\nabla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z\big) +C_g(x)d_g(x,u(z))^2|u_s|^2 \quad\forall\,z\!\in\!u^{-1}\big(B_{\delta_g(x)}^g(x)\big)\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound for g(u_s, nabla_s(-zeta_x)).

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e2
nodes.statement: |u_s|^2\le g\big(u_s,\nabla_s(-\zeta_x)|_z\big) +C_g(x)d_g(x,u(z))^2|u_s|^2 \quad\forall\,z\!\in\!u^{-1}\big(B_{\delta_g(x)}^g(x)\big)\,.

nodes.name: conformality
nodes.statement: If $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, then $|u_s|\!=\!|u_t|$, $\lr{u_s,u_t}\!=\!0$, and \BE{MonLem_e3} \frac12\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big)d_g(x,u(z))^2=|u_s|^2|\zeta_x(u(z))|^2 \ge g\big(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2+g\big(u_t,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For J-holomorphic u, |u_s| = |u_t| and <u_s,u_t> = 0.

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e3
nodes.statement: \frac12\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big)d_g(x,u(z))^2=|u_s|^2|\zeta_x(u(z))|^2 \ge g\big(u_s,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2+g\big(u_t,\zeta_x(u(z))\big)^2\,.

nodes.name: pointwise inequality
nodes.statement: Since $\eta'\!\le\!0$, (\ref{MonLem_e1})-(\ref{MonLem_e3}) give \BE{MonLem_e4}\begin{split} &\frac12\eta'\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg)\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big) +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big)\\ &\qquad\le g\big(u_s,\nabla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)+g\big(u_t,\nabla_t\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)+ C_g(x)\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)d_g(x,u(z))^2\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big). \end{split}\end{equation}

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e4
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\frac12\eta'\bigg(\!\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\!\bigg)\frac{d_g(x,u(z))}{\delta}\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big) +\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big)\\ &\qquad\le g\big(u_s,\nabla_s\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)+g\big(u_t,\nabla_t\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big)+ C_g(x)\eta_{u,x,\delta}(z)d_g(x,u(z))^2\big(|u_s|^2\!+\!|u_t|^2\big). \end{split}

nodes.name: integrated inequality
nodes.statement: Along with~(\ref{MonLem_e6}), this implies that \BE{MonLem_e9}-\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le \int_{\Sigma}g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big) +2C_g(x)\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\end{equation} for every compact Riemann surface with boundary $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$}, and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_g(x))$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get (3.12).

nodes.name: Eq. MonLem_e9
nodes.statement: -\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le \int_{\Sigma}g\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi_{u,x,\delta}\big) +2C_g(x)\delta^2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)

nodes.name: obtain (3.4)
nodes.statement: Combining this inequality with~(\ref{MonLem_e0b}), we obtain~(\ref{Aetabd_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine with (3.7) to get (3.4).

nodes.name: symplectic case
nodes.statement: Suppose $\omega\!\equiv\!g(J\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symplectic form on~$X$. By Lemma~\ref{CritEner_lmm}, the left-hand side of~(\ref{MonLem_e0b}) then vanishes. From~(\ref{MonLem_e9}), we thus obtain $$-\delta E_{u,x,\eta}'(\delta)+2E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\le 2C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2 E_{u,x,\eta}(\delta)\,.$$ The reasoning below~(\ref{Aetabd_e}) now yields the second claim.
nodes.statement_short: If omega is symplectic, Lemma 3.16 kills the error term and gives the exponential bound.

nodes.name: Cauchy's Integral Formula
nodes.statement: According to Cauchy's Integral Formula, a holomorphic map $u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ satisfies $$u'(0)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathfrak i}\oint_{|z|=r}\frac{u(z)}{z^2}\textnormal{d} z \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,R).$$

nodes.name: bounded entire functions are constant
nodes.statement: This immediately implies that a bounded holomorphic function defined on all of~$\mathbb{C}$ is constant.

nodes.name: Mean Value Inequality
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$\hbar_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property. If \hbox{$u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map such that $$u(B_R)\subset B_r^g(x) \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad E_g(u)<\hbar_{J,g}(x,r)$$ for some $x\!\in\!X$ and $r\!\in\!\mathbb R$, then \BE{PtBnd_e} \big|\textnormal{d}_0u\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g(u)\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For a J-holomorphic map from B_R with small energy and image in a ball, |d_0 u|^2 is bounded by 16/(pi R^2) times the energy.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$
conclusions: there exists a continuous function \hbox{$\hbar_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property
\big|\textnormal{d}_0u\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g(u)\,.
nodes.label: PtBnd_prp

nodes.name: Eq. PtBnd_e
nodes.statement: \big|\textnormal{d}_0u\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g(u)\,.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4.1 (Mean Value Inequality)
nodes.statement: Let $\phi(z)\!=\!\frac12|\textnormal{d}_zu|_g^2$. By Lemma~\ref{LapEng_lmm} below, $\Delta\phi\!\ge\!-A_{J,g}\phi^2$ with \hbox{$A_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} determined by $(X,J,g)$. The claim with $\hbar_{J,g}\!=\!\pi/8A_{J,g}$ thus follows from Proposition~\ref{Lapl_prp}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.7 to the energy density and then Proposition 4.6.

nodes.name: energy density inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\phi(z)\!=\!\frac12|\textnormal{d}_zu|_g^2$. By Lemma~\ref{LapEng_lmm} below, $\Delta\phi\!\ge\!-A_{J,g}\phi^2$ with \hbox{$A_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} determined by $(X,J,g)$.
nodes.statement_short: phi = |du|^2/2 satisfies Delta phi >= -A phi^2 by Lemma 4.7.

nodes.name: apply Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement: The claim with $\hbar_{J,g}\!=\!\pi/8A_{J,g}$ thus follows from Proposition~\ref{Lapl_prp}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 4.6 with hbar = pi/8A.

nodes.name: Lower Energy Bound
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, then there exists $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $E_g(u)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every non-constant $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-constant J-holomorphic spheres in a compact almost complex manifold have energy at least a fixed hbar>0.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$
conclusions: there exists $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $E_g(u)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every non-constant $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$
nodes.label: LowEner_crl

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 4.2 (Lower Energy Bound)
nodes.statement: By the compactness of $X$, we can assume that $g$ is compatible with~$J$. Let $\hbar_{J,g}\!>\!0$ be the minimal value of the function~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in the statement of Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} on the compact space $X\!\times\![0,\textnormal{diam}_g(X)]$. If $u\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$, $$\big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g\big(u;B_R(z)\big) \le \frac{16}{\pi R^2}E_g(u)\qquad\forall~z\!\in\!\mathbb{C},~R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$$ by Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}, since $B_R(z)\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ as Riemann surfaces. Thus, $\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$, and so $u$ is constant.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Mean Value Inequality on arbitrarily large disks to a sphere of small energy to get du = 0.

nodes.name: compatible metric
nodes.statement: By the compactness of $X$, we can assume that $g$ is compatible with~$J$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG g is compatible with J.

nodes.name: apply the Mean Value Inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\hbar_{J,g}\!>\!0$ be the minimal value of the function~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in the statement of Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} on the compact space $X\!\times\![0,\textnormal{diam}_g(X)]$. If $u\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$, $$\big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g^2<\frac{16}{\pi R^2} E_g\big(u;B_R(z)\big) \le \frac{16}{\pi R^2}E_g(u)\qquad\forall~z\!\in\!\mathbb{C},~R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$$ by Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}, since $B_R(z)\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ as Riemann surfaces.
nodes.statement_short: For small energy |du|^2 <= 16 E/(pi R^2) for all R.

nodes.name: u is constant
nodes.statement: Thus, $\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$, and so $u$ is constant.
nodes.statement_short: Letting R grow gives du = 0.

nodes.name: Laplacian
nodes.statement: If $\phi\!:U\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$-function on an open subset of~$\mathbb R^2$, let $$\Delta\phi=\frac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial s^2}+\frac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial t^2} \equiv \phi_{ss}+\phi_{tt}$$ denote the Laplacian of~$\phi$.

nodes.name: Laplacian in polar coordinates
nodes.statement: Show that in the polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ on $\mathbb R^2$, \BE{LaplPol_e}\Delta\phi=\phi_{rr}+r^{-1}\phi_r+r^{-2}\phi_{\theta\theta}\,.\end{equation}
nodes.label: LaplPol_exer

nodes.name: Eq. LaplPol_e
nodes.statement: \Delta\phi=\phi_{rr}+r^{-1}\phi_r+r^{-2}\phi_{\theta\theta}\,.

nodes.name: Green-type representation on a disk
nodes.statement: If $\phi\!:\ov{B_R}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R$ is $C^2$, then \BE{Lapl_e1} 2\pi R\,\phi(0)=-R\int_{(r,\theta)\in B_R}\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln r)\Delta\phi +\int_{\partial B_R}\phi\,.\end{equation}
conclusions: 2\pi R\,\phi(0)=-R\int_{(r,\theta)\in B_R}\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln r)\Delta\phi +\int_{\partial B_R}\phi\,.
nodes.label: Lapl_lmm1

nodes.name: Eq. Lapl_e1
nodes.statement: 2\pi R\,\phi(0)=-R\int_{(r,\theta)\in B_R}\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln r)\Delta\phi +\int_{\partial B_R}\phi\,.

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: By Stokes' Theorem applied to $\phi\textnormal{d}\theta$ on $\ov{B_R}\!-\!B_{\delta}$, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \oint_{\partial B_R}\!\!\!\phi\,\textnormal{d}\theta-\oint_{\partial B_{\delta}}\!\!\!\phi\,\textnormal{d}\theta &=\int_{\ov{B_R-B_{\delta}}}\!\phi_r\,\textnormal{d} r\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d}\theta =\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_{\delta}^R(r\phi_r)r^{-1}\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta\\ &=\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln\delta)\delta\,\phi_r(\delta,\theta)\textnormal{d}\theta +\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_{\delta}^R\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln r)(\phi_{rr}+r^{-1}\phi_r)r\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta\,; \end{split}\end{equation*} the last equality above is obtained by applying integration by parts to the functions $\ln r\!-\!\ln R$ and~$r\phi_r$. Sending $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$ and using~(\ref{LaplPol_e}), we obtain $$\frac1R\int_{\partial B_R}\phi - 2\pi\,\phi(0)=0+ \int_{(r,\theta)\in B_R}\!\!(\ln R\!-\!\ln r)\Delta\phi\,,$$ which is equivalent to~(\ref{Lapl_e1}).
nodes.statement_short: Stokes' Theorem on an annulus, integration by parts in r, and the polar Laplacian formula.

nodes.name: mean value bound for subharmonic-type functions
nodes.statement: If $\phi\!:\ov{B_R}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R$ is $C^2$ and $\Delta\phi\!\ge\!-C$ for some $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, then \BE{Lapl_e2} \phi(0)\le \frac18 CR^2+\frac1{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.\end{equation}
conclusions: \phi(0)\le \frac18 CR^2+\frac1{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.
nodes.label: Lapl_crl

nodes.name: Eq. Lapl_e2
nodes.statement: \phi(0)\le \frac18 CR^2+\frac1{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 4.5
nodes.statement: By (\ref{Lapl_e1}), $$2\pi r\,\phi(0)\le Cr\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\int_0^r(\ln r\!-\!\ln\rho) \rho\,\textnormal{d}\rho\,\textnormal{d}\theta+\int_{\partial B_r}\!\!\phi =Cr\cdot 2\pi\cdot\frac{r^2}{4}+\int_{\partial B_r}\!\!\phi \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,R).$$ Integrating the above in $r\!\in\!(0,R)$, we obtain $$2\pi\phi(0)\cdot\frac{R^2}{2} \le 2\pi C\cdot\frac{R^4}{16} +\int_{B_R}\phi.$$ This inequality is equivalent to~(\ref{Lapl_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Green-type representation of Lemma 4.4 on each circle and integrate in r.

nodes.name: bound on circles
nodes.statement: By (\ref{Lapl_e1}), $$2\pi r\,\phi(0)\le Cr\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\int_0^r(\ln r\!-\!\ln\rho) \rho\,\textnormal{d}\rho\,\textnormal{d}\theta+\int_{\partial B_r}\!\!\phi =Cr\cdot 2\pi\cdot\frac{r^2}{4}+\int_{\partial B_r}\!\!\phi \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,R).$$
nodes.statement_short: Use Delta phi >= -C in (4.4) for each r.

nodes.name: integrate in r
nodes.statement: Integrating the above in $r\!\in\!(0,R)$, we obtain $$2\pi\phi(0)\cdot\frac{R^2}{2} \le 2\pi C\cdot\frac{R^4}{16} +\int_{B_R}\phi.$$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over r in (0,R).

nodes.name: rearrange
nodes.statement: This inequality is equivalent to~(\ref{Lapl_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange to (4.5).

nodes.name: mean value inequality for Delta phi >= -A phi^2
nodes.statement: If $\phi\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^{\ge0}$ is $C^2$ and there exists $A\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $\Delta\phi\!\ge\!-A\phi^2$ and $\displaystyle\int_{B_R}\phi<\frac{\pi}{8A}$, then \BE{Lapl_e3} \phi(0)\le \frac8{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.\end{equation}
assumptions: there exists $A\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that $\Delta\phi\!\ge\!-A\phi^2$ and $\displaystyle\int_{B_R}\phi<\frac{\pi}{8A}$
conclusions: \phi(0)\le \frac8{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.
nodes.label: Lapl_prp

nodes.name: Eq. Lapl_e3
nodes.statement: \phi(0)\le \frac8{\pi R^2}\int_{B_R}\phi\,.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement: Replacing $A$ by $\ti{A}\!=\!R^2A$ and $\phi$ by $$\ti\phi\!: B_1\longrightarrow\mathbb R, \qquad\ti\phi(z)=\phi(Rz),$$ we can assume that $R\!=\!1$, as well as that $\phi$ is defined on~$\ov{B_1}$.\\ \noindent (1) Define $$f\!:[0,1)\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{\ge0} \qquad\hbox{by}\qquad f(r)=(1\!-\!r)^2\max_{\ov{B_r}}\phi\,.$$ In particular, $f(0)\!=\!\phi(0)$ and $f(1)\!=\!0$. Choose $r^*\!\in\![0,1)$ and $z^*\!\in\!B_{r^*}$ such~that $$f(r^*)=\sup f \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad \phi(z^*)=\sup_{B_{r^*}}\phi\equiv c^*\,.$$ Let $\delta\!=\!\frac12(1\!-\!r^*)\!>\!0$; see Figure~\ref{Lapl_fig}. Thus, $$\sup_{B_{\delta}(z^*)}\phi \le \sup_{B_{r^*+\delta}}\phi =\frac{f(r^*\!+\!\delta)}{(1\!-\!(r^*\!+\!\delta))^2} \le \frac{f(r^*)}{\frac14(1\!-\!r^*)^2} =4\phi(z^*)=4c^*\,.$$ In particular, $\Delta\phi\ge -A\phi^2\ge -16Ac^{*2}$ on $B_{\delta}(z^*)$.\\ \noindent (2) Using Corollary~\ref{Lapl_crl}, we thus find that \BE{cbnd_e} c^*=\phi(z^*)\le\frac18\cdot 16Ac^{*2}\cdot\rho^2 +\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_{\rho}(z^*)}\!\!\!\phi \le 2Ac^{*2}\rho^2+\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_1}\!\!\!\phi \qquad\forall~\rho\!\in\![0,\delta]\,.\end{equation} If $2Ac^*\delta^2\le\frac12$, the $\rho\!=\!\delta$ case of the above inequality gives $$\frac12 c^*\le \frac{1}{\pi\delta^2}\int_{B_1}\phi \,, \qquad \phi(0)=f(0)\le f(r^*)=4c^*\cdot \delta^2 \le \frac8\pi \int_{B_1}\phi\,,$$ as claimed. If $2Ac^*\delta^2\ge\frac12$, $\rho\!\equiv\!(4Ac^*)^{-\frac12}\le\delta$ and (\ref{cbnd_e}) gives $$c^*\le 2Ac^{*2}\cdot\frac{1}{4Ac^*}+\frac{4Ac^*}{\pi}\int_{B_1}\phi\,.$$ Thus, $\displaystyle\frac{\pi}{8A}\le\int_{B_1}\!\!\phi$, contrary to the assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Heinz trick: maximize (1-r)^2 max phi, apply Corollary 4.5 on a small disk around the maximum, and split according to the size of 2Ac^*delta^2.

nodes.name: rescale to R = 1
nodes.statement: Replacing $A$ by $\ti{A}\!=\!R^2A$ and $\phi$ by $$\ti\phi\!: B_1\longrightarrow\mathbb R, \qquad\ti\phi(z)=\phi(Rz),$$ we can assume that $R\!=\!1$, as well as that $\phi$ is defined on~$\ov{B_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale to R = 1.

nodes.name: maximize the weighted supremum
nodes.statement: (1) Define $$f\!:[0,1)\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{\ge0} \qquad\hbox{by}\qquad f(r)=(1\!-\!r)^2\max_{\ov{B_r}}\phi\,.$$ In particular, $f(0)\!=\!\phi(0)$ and $f(1)\!=\!0$. Choose $r^*\!\in\![0,1)$ and $z^*\!\in\!B_{r^*}$ such~that $$f(r^*)=\sup f \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad \phi(z^*)=\sup_{B_{r^*}}\phi\equiv c^*\,.$$ Let $\delta\!=\!\frac12(1\!-\!r^*)\!>\!0$; see Figure~\ref{Lapl_fig}. Thus, $$\sup_{B_{\delta}(z^*)}\phi \le \sup_{B_{r^*+\delta}}\phi =\frac{f(r^*\!+\!\delta)}{(1\!-\!(r^*\!+\!\delta))^2} \le \frac{f(r^*)}{\frac14(1\!-\!r^*)^2} =4\phi(z^*)=4c^*\,.$$ In particular, $\Delta\phi\ge -A\phi^2\ge -16Ac^{*2}$ on $B_{\delta}(z^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define f(r) = (1-r)^2 max phi, pick its maximum r^* and z^*, and bound phi on B_delta(z^*).

nodes.name: apply Corollary 4.5 and split cases
nodes.statement: (2) Using Corollary~\ref{Lapl_crl}, we thus find that \BE{cbnd_e} c^*=\phi(z^*)\le\frac18\cdot 16Ac^{*2}\cdot\rho^2 +\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_{\rho}(z^*)}\!\!\!\phi \le 2Ac^{*2}\rho^2+\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_1}\!\!\!\phi \qquad\forall~\rho\!\in\![0,\delta]\,.\end{equation} If $2Ac^*\delta^2\le\frac12$, the $\rho\!=\!\delta$ case of the above inequality gives $$\frac12 c^*\le \frac{1}{\pi\delta^2}\int_{B_1}\phi \,, \qquad \phi(0)=f(0)\le f(r^*)=4c^*\cdot \delta^2 \le \frac8\pi \int_{B_1}\phi\,,$$ as claimed. If $2Ac^*\delta^2\ge\frac12$, $\rho\!\equiv\!(4Ac^*)^{-\frac12}\le\delta$ and (\ref{cbnd_e}) gives $$c^*\le 2Ac^{*2}\cdot\frac{1}{4Ac^*}+\frac{4Ac^*}{\pi}\int_{B_1}\phi\,.$$ Thus, $\displaystyle\frac{\pi}{8A}\le\int_{B_1}\!\!\phi$, contrary to the assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 4.5 on B_rho(z^*) gives the bound when 2Ac^*delta^2 <= 1/2; the other case contradicts the energy assumption.

nodes.name: Eq. cbnd_e
nodes.statement: c^*=\phi(z^*)\le\frac18\cdot 16Ac^{*2}\cdot\rho^2 +\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_{\rho}(z^*)}\!\!\!\phi \le 2Ac^{*2}\rho^2+\frac{1}{\pi\rho^2}\int_{B_1}\!\!\!\phi \qquad\forall~\rho\!\in\![0,\delta]\,.

nodes.name: Laplacian of the energy density
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$, there exists a continuous function \hbox{$A_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property. If $\Omega\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset, $u\!:\Omega\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map, and $u(\Omega)\!\subset\!B_r^g(x)$ for some $x\!\in\!X$ and $r\!\in\!\mathbb R$, then the function $\phi(z)\!\equiv\!\frac12|\textnormal{d}_zu|^2_g$ satisfies $\Delta\phi\ge-A_{J,g}(x,r)\phi^2$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$
$\Omega\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset, $u\!:\Omega\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map
conclusions: there exists a continuous function \hbox{$A_{J,g}\!:X\!\times\!\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$} with the following property
the function $\phi(z)\!\equiv\!\frac12|\textnormal{d}_zu|^2_g$ satisfies $\Delta\phi\ge-A_{J,g}(x,r)\phi^2$
