nodes.name: continuous extensions of holomorphic maps are holomorphic
nodes.statement: By Cauchy's Integral Formula, a continuous extension of a holomorphic map \hbox{$u\!:B_{\mathbb R}^*\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$} over the origin is necessarily holomorphic.

nodes.name: regularity of continuous finite-energy J-holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold and $g$ be a Riemannian metric on~$X$. If $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and $u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a continuous map such that $u|_{B_R^*}$ is a $J$-holomorphic map and $E_g(u;B_R^*)\!<\!\infty$, then $u$ is smooth and $J$-holomorphic on~$B_R$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold and $g$ be a Riemannian metric on~$X$
$R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and $u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a continuous map
conclusions: $u$ is smooth and $J$-holomorphic on~$B_R$
also_stated_at: Another important implication of Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} is that a continuous map from a Riemann surface $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ into an almost complex manifold~$(X,J)$ which is holomorphic outside of a discrete collection of points and has bounded energy is in fact holomorphic on all of~$\Sigma$; see Proposition~\ref{JHolomreg_prp}.
nodes.label: JHolomreg_prp

nodes.name: velocity and length of a loop
nodes.statement: For a smooth loop $\gamma\!:S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$, define $$\gamma'(\theta)=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\theta}\gamma\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)\in T_{\gamma(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})}X \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad \ell_g(\gamma)=\int_0^{2\pi}\!\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_g \textnormal{d}\theta\in\mathbb R^{\ge0}$$ to be the \sf{velocity} of~$\gamma$ and the \sf{length} of~$\gamma$, respectively.

nodes.name: Isoperimetric Inequality
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J,g)$, $R$, and $u$ be as in Proposition~\ref{JHolomreg_prp} and $$\gamma_r\!:S^1\longrightarrow X,\quad \gamma_r\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big) \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,R).$$ There exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that \BE{JHolomreg1_e}E_g\big(u;B_r^*\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2 \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).\end{equation}
conclusions: There exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such that \BE{JHolomreg1_e}E_g\big(u;B_r^*\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2 \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).
nodes.label: JHolomreg_lmm

nodes.name: Eq. JHolomreg1_e
nodes.statement: E_g\big(u;B_r^*\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2 \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.9 (Isoperimetric Inequality)
nodes.statement: Let $\exp$ be as above the statement of Lemma~\ref{distder_lmm}, $\delta_g$ and $\omega_x$ be as in the first two sentences in the proof of Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp}, $$x_0=u(0), \quad \delta_0=\delta_g(x_0), \quad \omega_0=\omega_{x_0}, \qquad E\!:(0,R)\longrightarrow \mathbb R, ~~ E(r)\!=\!E_g(u;B_r^*).$$ We can assume that the metric~$g$ is determined by~$J$ and~$\omega_0$ on $B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$.\\ \noindent For a smooth loop $\gamma\!:S^1\!\longrightarrow\!B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$, define \begin{gather*} \xi_{\gamma}\!: S^1\longrightarrow T_{x_0}X \qquad\hbox{by}\quad \exp_{x_0}\xi_{\gamma}\!\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=\gamma\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big), ~~\big|\xi_{\gamma}\!(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|<\delta_0,\\ f_{\gamma}\!: B_1\longrightarrow X, \qquad f_{\gamma}\big(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)= \exp_{x_0}\!\!\big(r\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\!\big). \end{gather*} In particular, \begin{gather*} \big|\partial_rf_{\gamma}(\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g =\big|\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g\le\ell_g(\gamma)/2,\quad \big|r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}f_{\gamma}(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g =\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})}(\xi_{\gamma}'(\theta))\big|_g\le C\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_g \end{gather*} for some $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ determined by~$x_0$. Thus, \BE{JHolomreg1_e3}\begin{split} \bigg|\int_{B_1}\!f_{\gamma}^*\omega_0\bigg| &\le C\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^1 \big|\partial_rf_{\gamma}(\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g \big|r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}f_{\gamma}(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g r\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta\\ &\le C'\ell_g(\gamma)\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_gr\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta =\frac12 C'\ell_g(\gamma)^2 \end{split}\end{equation} for some $C,C'\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ determined by~$x_0$ and~$\omega_0$.\\ \begin{figure} \begin{pspicture}(0,-.7)(9,3.2) \psset{unit=.3cm} \pscircle[linewidth=.06](11,4){4}\rput(15.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_{\rho}$}} \rput(11.2,4){$f_{\gamma_{\rho}}$} \pscircle[linewidth=.04](26,4){2}\pscircle[linewidth=.06](26,4){6} \rput(26.4,0.4){$u|_{B_r-B_{\rho}}$} \rput(28.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_{\rho}$}}\rput(32.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_r$}} \pscircle[linewidth=.06](41,4){4}\rput(45.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_r$}} \rput(41.2,4){$f_{\gamma_r}$} \end{pspicture} \caption{The maps from an annulus and two disks glued together to form the map \hbox{$F_{\rho;r}\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$} in the proof of Lemma~\ref{JHolomreg_lmm}} \end{figure} \noindent By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and the finiteness assumption on $E(u;B_R^*)$, there exists $\delta\!\in\!(0,R/2)$ such~that \begin{gather} \big|\gamma_r'(\theta)\big|_g^2\equiv \big|\partial_{\theta}u(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2=r^2\big|\partial_ru(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2 \le \frac{32}{\pi}E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta),\\ \ell_g(\gamma_r)^2=128\pi E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta). \end{gather} By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $u(B_{2\delta})\!\subset\!B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$. For $r\!\in\!(0,\delta)$ and $\rho\!\in\!(0,r)$, define $$F_{\rho;r}\!:S^2\longrightarrow X$$ to be the map obtained from $u|_{B_r-B_{\rho}}$ by attaching disks to the boundary components $\partial B_r$ and $\partial B_{\rho}$ and letting $F_{\rho;r}$ be given by $f_{\gamma_r}$ and~$f_{\gamma_{\rho}}$ on these two disks, respectively; see Figure~\ref{JHolomreg_fig}. Since $F_{\rho;r}$ is homotopic to a constant~map and $\omega_0$ is closed, $$0=\int_{S^2}\!F_{\rho;r}^{\,*}\omega_0 =E_g\big(u;B_r\!-\!B_{\rho}\big)+\int_{B_1}\!\!\!f_{\gamma_{\rho}}^{\,*}\omega_0 -\int_{B_1}\!\!\!f_{\gamma_r}^{\,*}\omega_0\,.$$ Combining this with~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e3}) and~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e7}), we obtain \BE{JHolomreg1_e11}E_g\big(u;B_r\!-\!B_{\rho}\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2+CE(2\rho)\end{equation} for some $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ independent of $r$ and $\rho$ as above. Since $E_g(u;B_R^*)\!<\!0$, $E(2\rho)\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as \hbox{$\rho\!\longrightarrow\!0$}. Taking the limit of~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e11}) as $\rho\!\longrightarrow\!0$, we thus obtain~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Cap off the annulus image by exponential cones on the boundary loops, use that the resulting sphere has zero symplectic area, and bound the cone areas by the loop lengths.

nodes.name: local setup
nodes.statement: Let $\exp$ be as above the statement of Lemma~\ref{distder_lmm}, $\delta_g$ and $\omega_x$ be as in the first two sentences in the proof of Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp}, $$x_0=u(0), \quad \delta_0=\delta_g(x_0), \quad \omega_0=\omega_{x_0}, \qquad E\!:(0,R)\longrightarrow \mathbb R, ~~ E(r)\!=\!E_g(u;B_r^*).$$ We can assume that the metric~$g$ is determined by~$J$ and~$\omega_0$ on $B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall exp, delta_g and omega_x; WLOG g is determined by J and omega_0.

nodes.name: exponential cone on a loop
nodes.statement: For a smooth loop $\gamma\!:S^1\!\longrightarrow\!B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$, define \begin{gather*} \xi_{\gamma}\!: S^1\longrightarrow T_{x_0}X \qquad\hbox{by}\quad \exp_{x_0}\xi_{\gamma}\!\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=\gamma\big(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big), ~~\big|\xi_{\gamma}\!(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|<\delta_0,\\ f_{\gamma}\!: B_1\longrightarrow X, \qquad f_{\gamma}\big(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)= \exp_{x_0}\!\!\big(r\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\!\big). \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Define xi_gamma and the cone f_gamma.

nodes.name: derivative bounds for the cone
nodes.statement: In particular, \begin{gather*} \big|\partial_rf_{\gamma}(\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g =\big|\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g\le\ell_g(\gamma)/2,\quad \big|r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}f_{\gamma}(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g =\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\xi_{\gamma}(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})}(\xi_{\gamma}'(\theta))\big|_g\le C\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_g \end{gather*} for some $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ determined by~$x_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the partial derivatives of f_gamma by the length and velocity of gamma.

nodes.name: area of the cone
nodes.statement: Thus, \BE{JHolomreg1_e3}\begin{split} \bigg|\int_{B_1}\!f_{\gamma}^*\omega_0\bigg| &\le C\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^1 \big|\partial_rf_{\gamma}(\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g \big|r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}f_{\gamma}(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g r\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta\\ &\le C'\ell_g(\gamma)\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_gr\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta =\frac12 C'\ell_g(\gamma)^2 \end{split}\end{equation} for some $C,C'\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ determined by~$x_0$ and~$\omega_0$.\\ \begin{figure} \begin{pspicture}(0,-.7)(9,3.2) \psset{unit=.3cm} \pscircle[linewidth=.06](11,4){4}\rput(15.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_{\rho}$}} \rput(11.2,4){$f_{\gamma_{\rho}}$} \pscircle[linewidth=.04](26,4){2}\pscircle[linewidth=.06](26,4){6} \rput(26.4,0.4){$u|_{B_r-B_{\rho}}$} \rput(28.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_{\rho}$}}\rput(32.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_r$}} \pscircle[linewidth=.06](41,4){4}\rput(45.8,4){\sm{$\gamma_r$}} \rput(41.2,4){$f_{\gamma_r}$} \end{pspicture} \caption{The maps from an annulus and two disks glued together to form the map \hbox{$F_{\rho;r}\!:S^2\!\longrightarrow\!X$} in the proof of Lemma~\ref{JHolomreg_lmm}} \end{figure}
nodes.statement_short: The symplectic area of f_gamma is at most C ell(gamma)^2.

nodes.name: Eq. JHolomreg1_e3
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \bigg|\int_{B_1}\!f_{\gamma}^*\omega_0\bigg| &\le C\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^1 \big|\partial_rf_{\gamma}(\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g \big|r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}f_{\gamma}(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g r\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta\\ &\le C'\ell_g(\gamma)\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\big|\gamma'(\theta)\big|_gr\,\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta =\frac12 C'\ell_g(\gamma)^2 \end{split}

nodes.name: apply the Mean Value Inequality
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and the finiteness assumption on $E(u;B_R^*)$, there exists $\delta\!\in\!(0,R/2)$ such~that \begin{gather} \big|\gamma_r'(\theta)\big|_g^2\equiv \big|\partial_{\theta}u(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2=r^2\big|\partial_ru(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2 \le \frac{32}{\pi}E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta),\\ \ell_g(\gamma_r)^2=128\pi E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta). \end{gather}
nodes.statement_short: Bound |gamma_r'| and the length of gamma_r by the energy.

nodes.name: Eq. (4.1) JHolomreg1_e6
nodes.statement: \big|\gamma_r'(\theta)\big|_g^2\equiv \big|\partial_{\theta}u(r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2=r^2\big|\partial_ru(\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta})\big|_g^2 \le \frac{32}{\pi}E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta),
nodes.label: JHolomreg1_e6

nodes.name: Eq. (4.2) JHolomreg1_e7
nodes.statement: \ell_g(\gamma_r)^2=128\pi E(2r) \qquad\forall~r\!\in\!(0,\delta).
nodes.label: JHolomreg1_e7

nodes.name: small image
nodes.statement: By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $u(B_{2\delta})\!\subset\!B_{\delta_0}^g(x_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG u(B_{2 delta}) lies in a small ball.

nodes.name: glued sphere
nodes.statement: For $r\!\in\!(0,\delta)$ and $\rho\!\in\!(0,r)$, define $$F_{\rho;r}\!:S^2\longrightarrow X$$ to be the map obtained from $u|_{B_r-B_{\rho}}$ by attaching disks to the boundary components $\partial B_r$ and $\partial B_{\rho}$ and letting $F_{\rho;r}$ be given by $f_{\gamma_r}$ and~$f_{\gamma_{\rho}}$ on these two disks, respectively; see Figure~\ref{JHolomreg_fig}.
nodes.statement_short: Glue the annulus map and two cones into F_{rho;r}.

nodes.name: zero symplectic area
nodes.statement: Since $F_{\rho;r}$ is homotopic to a constant~map and $\omega_0$ is closed, $$0=\int_{S^2}\!F_{\rho;r}^{\,*}\omega_0 =E_g\big(u;B_r\!-\!B_{\rho}\big)+\int_{B_1}\!\!\!f_{\gamma_{\rho}}^{\,*}\omega_0 -\int_{B_1}\!\!\!f_{\gamma_r}^{\,*}\omega_0\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: F_{rho;r} is null-homotopic, so its omega_0-area vanishes.

nodes.name: annulus energy bound
nodes.statement: Combining this with~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e3}) and~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e7}), we obtain \BE{JHolomreg1_e11}E_g\big(u;B_r\!-\!B_{\rho}\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2+CE(2\rho)\end{equation} for some $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ independent of $r$ and $\rho$ as above.

nodes.name: Eq. JHolomreg1_e11
nodes.statement: E_g\big(u;B_r\!-\!B_{\rho}\big)\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2+CE(2\rho)

nodes.name: let rho tend to 0
nodes.statement: Since $E_g(u;B_R^*)\!<\!0$, $E(2\rho)\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as \hbox{$\rho\!\longrightarrow\!0$}. Taking the limit of~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e11}) as $\rho\!\longrightarrow\!0$, we thus obtain~(\ref{JHolomreg1_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Let rho tend to 0.

nodes.name: Holder-type decay of du near the puncture
nodes.statement: If $(X,J,g)$, $R$, and $u$ are as in Proposition~\ref{JHolomreg_prp}, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $\mu,C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{JHolomreg2_e} \big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\le Cr^{\mu-1} \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).\end{equation}
conclusions: there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $\mu,C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{JHolomreg2_e} \big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\le Cr^{\mu-1} \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).
nodes.label: JHolomreg_crl

nodes.name: Eq. JHolomreg2_e
nodes.statement: \big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\le Cr^{\mu-1} \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 4.10
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_r$, $\delta$, $C$, and $E(r)$ be as in the statement and proof of Lemma~\ref{JHolomreg_lmm}. Thus, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} E(r)\equiv\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\! \big|\textnormal{d}_{\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2 \rho\textnormal{d}\rho\textnormal{d}\theta &\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2= \frac12 Cr^2 \bigg(\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\textnormal{d}\theta\!\!\bigg)^{\!\!2}\\ &\le C\pi r^2\!\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2\textnormal{d}\theta =2C\pi r E'(r) \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta). \end{split}\end{equation*} This implies that $$\big(r^{-1/2C\pi}E(r)\big)'\ge0, ~~ E(r)\le \delta^{-1/2C\pi}E(\delta)\cdot r^{1/2C\pi}\equiv C'r^{2\mu} \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).$$ Combining this with (\ref{JHolomreg1_e6}), we obtain~(\ref{JHolomreg2_e}) with $\delta$ replaced by~$\delta/2$.
nodes.statement_short: The Isoperimetric Inequality gives E(r) <= 2C pi r E'(r), so E(r) grows like a power of r; then use (4.11).

nodes.name: differential inequality for E
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_r$, $\delta$, $C$, and $E(r)$ be as in the statement and proof of Lemma~\ref{JHolomreg_lmm}. Thus, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} E(r)\equiv\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\! \big|\textnormal{d}_{\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2 \rho\textnormal{d}\rho\textnormal{d}\theta &\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2= \frac12 Cr^2 \bigg(\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\textnormal{d}\theta\!\!\bigg)^{\!\!2}\\ &\le C\pi r^2\!\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2\textnormal{d}\theta =2C\pi r E'(r) \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta). \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Isoperimetric Inequality and Cauchy-Schwarz give E(r) <= 2 C pi r E'(r).

nodes.name: power growth
nodes.statement: This implies that $$\big(r^{-1/2C\pi}E(r)\big)'\ge0, ~~ E(r)\le \delta^{-1/2C\pi}E(\delta)\cdot r^{1/2C\pi}\equiv C'r^{2\mu} \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).$$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get E(r) <= C' r^{2 mu}.

nodes.name: pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Combining this with (\ref{JHolomreg1_e6}), we obtain~(\ref{JHolomreg2_e}) with $\delta$ replaced by~$\delta/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Use (4.11) to get the bound on |du|.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement: With $\mu$ as in Corollary~\ref{JHolomreg_crl}, let $p\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that $p\!>\!2$ and $(1\!-\!\mu)p\!<\!2$. In particular, $$u|_{B_{R/2}}\in L^p_1\big(B_{R/2};X\big), \qquad \bar\partial_Ju|_{B_{R/2}}=0\in L^p\big(B_{R/2};X\big).$$ By elliptic regularity, this implies that $u$ is smooth; see \cite[Theorem~B.4.1]{MS12}. By the continuity of $\bar\partial_Ju$, $u$ is then $J$-holomorphic on all of~$B_R$.
nodes.statement_short: The decay bound places u in L^p_1 for some p > 2; elliptic regularity then gives smoothness.

nodes.name: u lies in L^p_1
nodes.statement: With $\mu$ as in Corollary~\ref{JHolomreg_crl}, let $p\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that $p\!>\!2$ and $(1\!-\!\mu)p\!<\!2$. In particular, $$u|_{B_{R/2}}\in L^p_1\big(B_{R/2};X\big), \qquad \bar\partial_Ju|_{B_{R/2}}=0\in L^p\big(B_{R/2};X\big).$$
nodes.statement_short: Choose p > 2 with (1-mu)p < 2 so u is in L^p_1.

nodes.name: elliptic regularity
nodes.statement: By elliptic regularity, this implies that $u$ is smooth; see \cite[Theorem~B.4.1]{MS12}.
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic regularity gives smoothness.

nodes.name: J-holomorphic everywhere
nodes.statement: By the continuity of $\bar\partial_Ju$, $u$ is then $J$-holomorphic on all of~$B_R$.
nodes.statement_short: By continuity u is J-holomorphic on B_R.

nodes.name: simple maps are somewhere injective
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface, $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a $J$-holomorphic map. If $u$ is simple, then $u$ is somewhere injective and all limit points of the~set \BE{SimplMap_e}\big\{z\!\in\!\Sigma\!:\,|u^{-1}(u(z))|\!>\!1\big\}\end{equation} are critical points of~$u$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface
conclusions: $u$ is somewhere injective and all limit points of the~set \BE{SimplMap_e}\big\{z\!\in\!\Sigma\!:\,|u^{-1}(u(z))|\!>\!1\big\}\end{equation} are critical points of~$u$
nodes.label: SimplMap_prp

nodes.name: regular part Sigma_u^* and relation R_u^*
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface, and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map. Let \BE{Siudfn_e}\Sigma_u^*=\Sigma-u^{-1}\big(u\big(\{z\!\in\!\Sigma:\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\!\big)\end{equation} be the preimage of the regular values of~$u$ and $$\mathcal R_u^*\subset \Sigma_u^*\!\times\!\Sigma_u^*$$ be the subset of pairs $(z,z')$ such that there exists a diffeomorphism $\varphi_{z'z}\!:U_z\!\longrightarrow\!U_{z'}$ between neighborhoods of~$z$ and~$z'$ in~$\Sigma$ satisfying \BE{vphcond_e}\varphi_{z'z}(z)=z' \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u|_{U_z}=u\!\circ\!\varphi_{z'z}.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sigma_u^*: preimage of the regular values; R_u^*: pairs of points related by a local diffeomorphism intertwining u.

nodes.name: Eq. Siudfn_e
nodes.statement: \Sigma_u^*=\Sigma-u^{-1}\big(u\big(\{z\!\in\!\Sigma:\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\!\big)

nodes.name: Eq. vphcond_e
nodes.statement: \varphi_{z'z}(z)=z' \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u|_{U_z}=u\!\circ\!\varphi_{z'z}.

nodes.name: closure R_u
nodes.statement: Denote by $\mathcal R_u\!\subset\!\Sigma\!\times\!\Sigma$ the closure of $\mathcal R_u^*$.

nodes.name: R_u is an equivalence relation compatible with u
nodes.statement: It is immediate that $\mathcal R_u^*$ is an equivalence relation on~$\Sigma$ and $u(z)\!=\!u(z')$ whenever $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$. Thus, $\mathcal R_u$ is also a reflexive and symmetric relation and $u(z)\!=\!u(z')$ whenever $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$. By Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm4} below, $\mathcal R_u$ is transitive as well.

nodes.name: equivalence relation sim_u
nodes.statement: We denote this equivalence relation by~$\sim_u$.

nodes.name: quotient map h_u and induced map u'
nodes.statement: Let \BE{SimplMap_e2}h_u\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow\Sigma'\!\equiv\!\Sigma/\!\!\sim_u \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u'\!:\Sigma'\longrightarrow X\end{equation} be the quotient map and the continuous map induced by $u$, respectively. In particular, $$u\!=\!u'\!\circ\!h_u\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow X.$$

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap_e2
nodes.statement: h_u\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow\Sigma'\!\equiv\!\Sigma/\!\!\sim_u \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u'\!:\Sigma'\longrightarrow X

nodes.name: local covering structure of h_u near an isolated critical point
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, and $u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map such that $\textnormal{d}_zu\!\neq\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_R^*$. Then there exist $m\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ such~that \BE{SimplMap2_e}h_u\!: U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\longrightarrow h_u\big(U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\big)\subset B_R'\end{equation} is a covering projection of degree~$m$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$
$u\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map such that $\textnormal{d}_zu\!\neq\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_R^*$
conclusions: there exist $m\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ such~that \BE{SimplMap2_e}h_u\!: U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\longrightarrow h_u\big(U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\big)\subset B_R'\end{equation} is a covering projection of degree~$m$
nodes.label: SimplMap_lmm2

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap2_e
nodes.statement: h_u\!: U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\longrightarrow h_u\big(U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\big)\subset B_R'

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.12
nodes.statement:
By the continuity of $u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $u(0)\!=\!0$, and $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$. As shown in the proof of Corollary~ef{FHS_crl3}, there exist $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon/2)$ such~that $$U_0\equiv u^{-1} ig(u(B_{\delta}) ig)\!\cap\!B_{\epsilon}\subset B_{2\delta}.$$ By Proposition~ef{FHS_prp} and the compactness of $\ov{B_{2\delta}}\!\subset\!B_R$, the number $$m(z)\equiv  ig|h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0 ig|$$ is finite for every $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$.\ 
oindent Suppose $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*$ and $z_i'\!\in\!U_0$ are sequences such that~$z_i$ converges to some $z_0\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*$ with $z_i\!
eq\!z_0$ for all~$i$ and \hbox{$h_u(z_i)\!=\!h_u(z_i')$} for all~$i$. Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that $z_i'$ converges to some \hbox{$z_0'\!\in\!\ov{B_{2\delta}}$}. By the continuity of~$u$, $u(z_0')\!=\!u(z_0)$ and so $z_0'\!\in\!U_0$. Corollary~ef{FHS_crl2b} then implies that $h_u(z_0')\!=\!h_u(z_0)$. Since $B_{\delta}^*$ is connected, this implies that the number~$m(z)$ is independent of $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$; we denote it by~$m$.\ 
oindent Suppose $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$ and $$h_u^{-1} ig(h_u(z) ig)\cap U_0= ig\{z_1,\ldots,z_m ig\}\,.$$ Let $\varphi_i\!:U_1\!\longrightarrow\!U_i$ for $i\!=\!1,\ldots,m$ be diffeomorphisms between neighborhoods of~$z_1$ and~$z_i$ in~$U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$ such that $$\varphi_i(z_1)=z_i,~~ u=u\!\circ\!\varphi_i~~ orall\,i,\qquad U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset~~ orall\,i\!
eq\!j,$$ and $u\!:U_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is injective. Then $h_u(U_1)\!\subset\!B_R'$ is an open neighborhood of $h_u(z)$, $$h_u^{-1}\! ig(h_u(U_1)\! ig)\cap U_0= igsqcup_{i=1}^mU_i\,,$$ and $h_u\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!h_u(U_1)$ is a homeomorphism. Thus, (ef{SimplMap2_e}) is a covering projection of degree~$m$.
nodes.statement_short: Localize via the proof of Corollary 3.11, use Carleman similarity for finiteness of fibers and Corollary 3.10 to show the fiber count is locally constant, then exhibit evenly covered neighborhoods.

nodes.name: local model
nodes.statement: By the continuity of $u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, $u(0)\!=\!0$, and $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Work in C^n with u(0) = 0.

nodes.name: choose U_0
nodes.statement: As shown in the proof of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl3}, there exist $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,R)$ and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon/2)$ such~that $$U_0\equiv u^{-1}\big(u(B_{\delta})\big)\!\cap\!B_{\epsilon}\subset B_{2\delta}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Choose U_0 inside B_{2 delta}.

nodes.name: finite fibers
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp} and the compactness of $\ov{B_{2\delta}}\!\subset\!B_R$, the number $$m(z)\equiv \big|h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0\big|$$ is finite for every $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$.
nodes.statement_short: The fiber count m(z) is finite.

nodes.name: fiber count is locally constant
nodes.statement: Suppose $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*$ and $z_i'\!\in\!U_0$ are sequences such that~$z_i$ converges to some $z_0\!\in\!B_{\delta}^*$ with $z_i\!\neq\!z_0$ for all~$i$ and \hbox{$h_u(z_i)\!=\!h_u(z_i')$} for all~$i$. Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that $z_i'$ converges to some \hbox{$z_0'\!\in\!\ov{B_{2\delta}}$}. By the continuity of~$u$, $u(z_0')\!=\!u(z_0)$ and so $z_0'\!\in\!U_0$. Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2b} then implies that $h_u(z_0')\!=\!h_u(z_0)$. Since $B_{\delta}^*$ is connected, this implies that the number~$m(z)$ is independent of $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$; we denote it by~$m$.
nodes.statement_short: Using Corollary 3.10, m(z) is constant on the punctured disk.

nodes.name: covering projection
nodes.statement: Suppose $z\!\in\!U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$ and $$h_u^{-1}\big(h_u(z)\big)\cap U_0=\big\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\big\}\,.$$ Let $\varphi_i\!:U_1\!\longrightarrow\!U_i$ for $i\!=\!1,\ldots,m$ be diffeomorphisms between neighborhoods of~$z_1$ and~$z_i$ in~$U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*$ such that $$\varphi_i(z_1)=z_i,~~ u=u\!\circ\!\varphi_i~~\forall\,i,\qquad U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset~~\forall\,i\!\neq\!j,$$ and $u\!:U_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is injective. Then $h_u(U_1)\!\subset\!B_R'$ is an open neighborhood of $h_u(z)$, $$h_u^{-1}\!\big(h_u(U_1)\!\big)\cap U_0=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^mU_i\,,$$ and $h_u\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!h_u(U_1)$ is a homeomorphism. Thus, (\ref{SimplMap2_e}) is a covering projection of degree~$m$.
nodes.statement_short: Evenly covered neighborhoods show h_u is a degree m covering.

nodes.name: holomorphic chart on the quotient near a critical point
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$, $R$, and $u$ are as in Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2}. Then there exists a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ such~that \BE{SimplMap3_e}\Psi_0\!: h_u(U_0)\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad h_u(z)=\prod_{z'\in h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\cap U_0}\hspace{-.2in}z',\end{equation} is a homeomorphism from an open neighborhood of $h_u(0)$ in $B_R'$ to an open neighborhood of~0 in~$\mathbb{C}$ and $\Psi_0\!\circ\!h_u|_{U_0}$ is a holomorphic map.
conclusions: there exists a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ such~that \BE{SimplMap3_e}\Psi_0\!: h_u(U_0)\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad h_u(z)=\prod_{z'\in h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\cap U_0}\hspace{-.2in}z',\end{equation} is a homeomorphism from an open neighborhood of $h_u(0)$ in $B_R'$ to an open neighborhood of~0 in~$\mathbb{C}$ and $\Psi_0\!\circ\!h_u|_{U_0}$ is a holomorphic map
nodes.label: SimplMap_lmm3

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap3_e
nodes.statement: \Psi_0\!: h_u(U_0)\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad h_u(z)=\prod_{z'\in h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\cap U_0}\hspace{-.2in}z',

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.13
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2}, there exists a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ so that (\ref{SimplMap2_e}) is a covering projection of some degree~$m\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$. Since the restriction of~$u$ to $B_R^*$ is a $J$-holomorphic immersion, the diffeomorphisms~$\varphi_i$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2} are holomorphic. Thus, the~map $$\Psi_0\!\circ\!h_u|_{U_0\cap B_R^*}\!:U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad z\longrightarrow\prod_{z'\in h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\cap U_0}\hspace{-.2in}z'$$ is holomorphic. Since it is also bounded, it extends to a holomorphic map $$\wt\Psi_0\!: U_0\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}.$$ This extension is non-constant and vanishes at~0.\\ \noindent After possibly shrinking~$U_0$, we can assume that there exist $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{SimplMap3_e3} C^{-k}|z|^k\le \big|\wt\Psi_0(z)\big|\le C^k|z|^k \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!U_0.\end{equation} Since $\wt\Psi_0(z')\!=\!\wt\Psi_0(z)$ for all $z'\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0$, it follows~that \begin{gather*} C^{-2}|z|\le |z'|\le C^2|z| \qquad\forall~z'\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0,~z\!\in\!U_0,\\ C^{-2m}|z|^m\le \big|\wt\Psi_0(z)\big|\le C^{2m}|z|^m \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!U_0. \end{gather*} Along with~(\ref{SimplMap3_e3}), the last estimate implies that $k\!=\!m$ and that $\wt\Phi_0$ has a zero of order precisely~$m$ at $z\!=\!0$. Thus, shrinking $\delta$ in the proof of Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2} if necessary, we can assume that~$\wt\Phi_0$ is $m\!:\!1$ over $\ov{U_0}\!\cap\!B_R^*$. This implies that the map~(\ref{SimplMap3_e}) and its extension over the closure of $h_u(U_0)$ in~$B_R'$ are continuous and injective. Since the closure of $h_u(U_0)$ is compact and~$\mathbb{C}$ is Hausdorff, we conclude that~(\ref{SimplMap3_e}) is a homeomorphism onto an open subset of~$\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: The product of the preimages is a bounded holomorphic function on the punctured disk, extends holomorphically with a zero of order m, and so gives a chart.

nodes.name: covering projection
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2}, there exists a neighborhood~$U_0$ of~$0$ in~$B_R$ so that (\ref{SimplMap2_e}) is a covering projection of some degree~$m\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 4.12, h_u is a degree m covering near 0.

nodes.name: holomorphic extension
nodes.statement: Since the restriction of~$u$ to $B_R^*$ is a $J$-holomorphic immersion, the diffeomorphisms~$\varphi_i$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2} are holomorphic. Thus, the~map $$\Psi_0\!\circ\!h_u|_{U_0\cap B_R^*}\!:U_0\!\cap\!B_R^*\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \qquad z\longrightarrow\prod_{z'\in h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\cap U_0}\hspace{-.2in}z'$$ is holomorphic. Since it is also bounded, it extends to a holomorphic map $$\wt\Psi_0\!: U_0\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}.$$ This extension is non-constant and vanishes at~0.
nodes.statement_short: The product map is holomorphic and bounded, hence extends.

nodes.name: comparable growth
nodes.statement: After possibly shrinking~$U_0$, we can assume that there exist $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that \BE{SimplMap3_e3} C^{-k}|z|^k\le \big|\wt\Psi_0(z)\big|\le C^k|z|^k \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!U_0.\end{equation} Since $\wt\Psi_0(z')\!=\!\wt\Psi_0(z)$ for all $z'\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0$, it follows~that \begin{gather*} C^{-2}|z|\le |z'|\le C^2|z| \qquad\forall~z'\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(z))\!\cap\!U_0,~z\!\in\!U_0,\\ C^{-2m}|z|^m\le \big|\wt\Psi_0(z)\big|\le C^{2m}|z|^m \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!U_0. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Compare |Psi tilde| with |z|^k and |z|^m.

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap3_e3
nodes.statement: C^{-k}|z|^k\le \big|\wt\Psi_0(z)\big|\le C^k|z|^k \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!U_0.

nodes.name: order of the zero
nodes.statement: Along with~(\ref{SimplMap3_e3}), the last estimate implies that $k\!=\!m$ and that $\wt\Phi_0$ has a zero of order precisely~$m$ at $z\!=\!0$. Thus, shrinking $\delta$ in the proof of Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2} if necessary, we can assume that~$\wt\Phi_0$ is $m\!:\!1$ over $\ov{U_0}\!\cap\!B_R^*$.

nodes.name: homeomorphism
nodes.statement: This implies that the map~(\ref{SimplMap3_e}) and its extension over the closure of $h_u(U_0)$ in~$B_R'$ are continuous and injective. Since the closure of $h_u(U_0)$ is compact and~$\mathbb{C}$ is Hausdorff, we conclude that~(\ref{SimplMap3_e}) is a homeomorphism onto an open subset of~$\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuous injective map on a compact set into C is a homeomorphism onto an open set.

nodes.name: R_u is open in the second factor
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, and~$u$ are as in Proposition~\ref{SimplMap_prp} and $(x,y)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$. For every neighborhood~$U_x$ of~$x$ in~$\Sigma$, the image of the projection $$\mathcal R_u\cap (U_x\!\times\!X)\longrightarrow X$$ to the second component contains a neighborhood~$U_y$ of~$y$ in~$\Sigma$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, and~$u$ are as in Proposition~\ref{SimplMap_prp}
conclusions: the image of the projection $$\mathcal R_u\cap (U_x\!\times\!X)\longrightarrow X$$ to the second component contains a neighborhood~$U_y$ of~$y$ in~$\Sigma$

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.14
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~ef{FHS_crl2}, the last set in~(ef{Siudfn_e}) is finite. By the same reasoning as in the last part of the proof of Lemma~ef{SimplMap_lmm2}, \BE{SimplMap4_e1}h_u\!:\Sigma_u^*\longrightarrow h_u(\Sigma_u^*)\subset \Sigma'\end{equation} is a local homeomorphism. Since $u(z)\!=\!u(z')$ for all $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$, the definition of~$\Sigma_u^*$ thus implies that~(ef{SimplMap4_e1}) is a finite-degree covering projection over each topological component of~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$. Since the complement of finitely many points in a connected Riemann surface is connected, the degree of this covering over a point $h_u(z)$ depends only on the topological component of~$\Sigma$ containing~$z$. For any point $z\!\in\!\Sigma$, not necessarily in~$\Sigma_u^*$, we denote this degree by~$d(z)$.\ 
oindent By Corollary~ef{FHS_crl2}, the set $$S\equiv u^{-1} ig(u(x) ig)\subset \Sigma$$ is finite. Let $W\!\subset\!X$ be a neighborhood of $u(x)$ such that the topological components~$\Sigma_s$ of~$u^{-1}(W)$ containing the points $s\!\in\!S$ are pairwise disjoint (if $U$ is a union of disjoint balls around the points of~$S$, then $$W \equiv X-u(\Sigma\!-\!U)$$ works). By Lemma~ef{SimplMap_lmm2}, for each $s\!\in\!S$ there exists a neighborhood~$U_s'$ of~$s$ in~$\Sigma_s$ such~that $$h_u\!: U_s'\!-\!\{s\}\longrightarrow h_u ig(U_s'\!-\!\{s\} ig)\subset \Sigma'$$ is a covering projection of some degree $m_s\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$; we can assume that $U_x'\!\subset\!U_x$. Along with the compactness of~$\Sigma$, the former implies that \BE{SimplMap4_e3} egin{aligned} & ig|h_u^{-1} ig(h_u(y') ig)\cap U_s' ig|\in  ig\{0,m_s ig\} &\qquad & orall\,y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s,s'\!\in\!S, \ &\sum_{s\in S} ig|h_u^{-1} ig(h_u(y') ig)\cap U_s' ig|=d(s') &\qquad & orall~y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s'\!\in\!S. \end{aligned}\end{equation} Define $$\mathcal P_y(S)= ig\{S'\!\subset\!S\!:\sum_{s\in S'}\!m_s\!=\!d(y) ig\}.$$ \vspace{.2in} 
oindent Let $U_y''\!\subset\!U_y'$ be a connected neighborhood of $y$. For each $S'\!\in\!\mathcal P_y(S)$, define $$U_{y;S'}''= ig\{y'\!\in\!U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!: \{s\!\in\!S\!:h_u^{-1}(h_u(y'))\!\cap\!U_s'\!
eq\!\emptyset\}\!=\!S' ig\}.$$ By~(ef{SimplMap4_e3}), these sets partition $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*$. Since each set $$ ig\{y'\!\in\!U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!:h_u^{-1}(h_u(y'))\!\cap\!U_s'\!
eq\!\emptyset ig\}$$ is open, (ef{SimplMap4_e3}) also implies that each set $U_{y;S'}''$ is open. Since the set $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*$ is connected, it follows that $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!=\!U_{y;S_y}''$ for some $S_y\!\in\!\mathcal P_y(S)$. Since $(x,y)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$, $x\!\in\!S_y$. Thus, the image of the projection $$\mathcal R_u\cap (U_x'\!	imes\!X)\longrightarrow X$$ to the second component contains the neighborhood~$U_y''$ of~$y$ in~$\Sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: h_u is a finite covering over regular values; near the finitely many preimages of u(x), local degrees partition a connected neighborhood of y, forcing x into the set of sheets.

nodes.name: finitely many critical values
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2}, the last set in~(\ref{Siudfn_e}) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: The critical preimages are finite.

nodes.name: local homeomorphism
nodes.statement: By the same reasoning as in the last part of the proof of Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2}, \BE{SimplMap4_e1}h_u\!:\Sigma_u^*\longrightarrow h_u(\Sigma_u^*)\subset \Sigma'\end{equation} is a local homeomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: h_u is a local homeomorphism on Sigma_u^*.

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap4_e1
nodes.statement: h_u\!:\Sigma_u^*\longrightarrow h_u(\Sigma_u^*)\subset \Sigma'

nodes.name: finite covering
nodes.statement: Since $u(z)\!=\!u(z')$ for all $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$, the definition of~$\Sigma_u^*$ thus implies that~(\ref{SimplMap4_e1}) is a finite-degree covering projection over each topological component of~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: h_u is a finite covering over each component.

nodes.name: degree d(z)
nodes.statement: Since the complement of finitely many points in a connected Riemann surface is connected, the degree of this covering over a point $h_u(z)$ depends only on the topological component of~$\Sigma$ containing~$z$. For any point $z\!\in\!\Sigma$, not necessarily in~$\Sigma_u^*$, we denote this degree by~$d(z)$.
nodes.statement_short: The covering degree depends only on the component; call it d(z).

nodes.name: finite fiber S
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2}, the set $$S\equiv u^{-1}\big(u(x)\big)\subset \Sigma$$ is finite.
nodes.statement_short: The fiber S over u(x) is finite.

nodes.name: separating neighborhood
nodes.statement: Let $W\!\subset\!X$ be a neighborhood of $u(x)$ such that the topological components~$\Sigma_s$ of~$u^{-1}(W)$ containing the points $s\!\in\!S$ are pairwise disjoint (if $U$ is a union of disjoint balls around the points of~$S$, then $$W \equiv X-u(\Sigma\!-\!U)$$ works).
nodes.statement_short: Choose W separating the components around points of S.

nodes.name: local coverings
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm2}, for each $s\!\in\!S$ there exists a neighborhood~$U_s'$ of~$s$ in~$\Sigma_s$ such~that $$h_u\!: U_s'\!-\!\{s\}\longrightarrow h_u\big(U_s'\!-\!\{s\}\big)\subset \Sigma'$$ is a covering projection of some degree $m_s\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$; we can assume that $U_x'\!\subset\!U_x$.
nodes.statement_short: Each point of S has a punctured neighborhood covering with degree m_s.

nodes.name: counting sheets
nodes.statement: Along with the compactness of~$\Sigma$, the former implies that \BE{SimplMap4_e3}\begin{aligned} &\big|h_u^{-1}\big(h_u(y')\big)\cap U_s'\big|\in \big\{0,m_s\big\} &\qquad &\forall\,y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s,s'\!\in\!S, \\ &\sum_{s\in S}\big|h_u^{-1}\big(h_u(y')\big)\cap U_s'\big|=d(s') &\qquad &\forall~y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s'\!\in\!S. \end{aligned}\end{equation} Define $$\mathcal P_y(S)=\big\{S'\!\subset\!S\!:\sum_{s\in S'}\!m_s\!=\!d(y)\big\}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fiber counts give (4.17); define P_y(S).

nodes.name: Eq. SimplMap4_e3
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\big|h_u^{-1}\big(h_u(y')\big)\cap U_s'\big|\in \big\{0,m_s\big\} &\qquad &\forall\,y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s,s'\!\in\!S, \\ &\sum_{s\in S}\big|h_u^{-1}\big(h_u(y')\big)\cap U_s'\big|=d(s') &\qquad &\forall~y'\!\in\!U_{s'}'\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*,~s'\!\in\!S. \end{aligned}

nodes.name: partition of a neighborhood of y
nodes.statement: Let $U_y''\!\subset\!U_y'$ be a connected neighborhood of $y$. For each $S'\!\in\!\mathcal P_y(S)$, define $$U_{y;S'}''=\big\{y'\!\in\!U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!: \{s\!\in\!S\!:h_u^{-1}(h_u(y'))\!\cap\!U_s'\!\neq\!\emptyset\}\!=\!S'\big\}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Define the sets U''_{y;S'}.

nodes.name: open partition
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{SimplMap4_e3}), these sets partition $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*$. Since each set $$\big\{y'\!\in\!U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!:h_u^{-1}(h_u(y'))\!\cap\!U_s'\!\neq\!\emptyset\big\}$$ is open, (\ref{SimplMap4_e3}) also implies that each set $U_{y;S'}''$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: These sets are open and partition the neighborhood.

nodes.name: connectedness
nodes.statement: Since the set $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*$ is connected, it follows that $U_y''\!\cap\!\Sigma_u^*\!=\!U_{y;S_y}''$ for some $S_y\!\in\!\mathcal P_y(S)$.
nodes.statement_short: By connectedness one S_y works.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Since $(x,y)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$, $x\!\in\!S_y$. Thus, the image of the projection $$\mathcal R_u\cap (U_x'\!\times\!X)\longrightarrow X$$ to the second component contains the neighborhood~$U_y''$ of~$y$ in~$\Sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: x lies in S_y, so the projection contains U''_y.

nodes.name: h_u is open and closed
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, and~$u$ are as in Proposition~\ref{SimplMap_prp}. The quotient map~$h_u$ in~(\ref{SimplMap_e2}) is open and closed.
assumptions: $(X,J)$, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$, and~$u$ are as in Proposition~\ref{SimplMap_prp}
conclusions: The quotient map~$h_u$ in~(\ref{SimplMap_e2}) is open and closed

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 4.15
nodes.statement: The openness of $h_u$ is immediate from Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm4}. Suppose $A\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a closed subset and $y_i\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(A))$ is a sequence converging to some $y\!\in\!\Sigma$. Let $x_i\!\in\!A$ be such that \hbox{$h_u(x_i)\!=\!h_u(y_i)$}. Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the sequence $x_i$ converges to some $x\!\in\!A$. Since $\Sigma\!-\!\Sigma_u^*$ consists of isolated points, we can also assume that $y_i\!\in\!\Sigma_u^*$ and so $(x_i,y_i)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$. Thus, $(x,y)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$ and so $y\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(A))$. We conclude that $h_u$ is a closed~map.
nodes.statement_short: Openness from Lemma 4.14; closedness by a sequence argument using that R_u is the closure of R_u^*.

nodes.name: openness
nodes.statement: The openness of $h_u$ is immediate from Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm4}.
nodes.statement_short: Openness follows from Lemma 4.14.

nodes.name: sequence setup
nodes.statement: Suppose $A\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a closed subset and $y_i\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(A))$ is a sequence converging to some $y\!\in\!\Sigma$. Let $x_i\!\in\!A$ be such that \hbox{$h_u(x_i)\!=\!h_u(y_i)$}.

nodes.statement: Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the sequence $x_i$ converges to some $x\!\in\!A$. Since $\Sigma\!-\!\Sigma_u^*$ consists of isolated points, we can also assume that $y_i\!\in\!\Sigma_u^*$ and so $(x_i,y_i)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$.

nodes.name: closedness
nodes.statement: Thus, $(x,y)\!\in\!\mathcal R_u$ and so $y\!\in\!h_u^{-1}(h_u(A))$. We conclude that $h_u$ is a closed~map.
nodes.statement_short: y lies in h_u^{-1}(h_u(A)).

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4.11
nodes.statement:
Let $\Sigma'$, $h_u$, and $u'$ be as in~(ef{SimplMap_e2}). By the second statement in Corollary~ef{SimplMap_crl} and \cite[Lemma~73.3]{Mu}, $\Sigma'$ is a Hausdorff topological space. Fix a Riemannian metric~$g$ on~$X$.\ 
oindent For $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$ with $z\!
eq\!z'$, the neighborhoods $U_z$ and~$U_{z'}$ as in~(ef{vphcond_e}) can be chosen so that they are disjoint and $u|_{U_z}$ is an embedding. Since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, $\varphi_{z'z}$ is then a biholomorphic map and $h_u|_{U_z}$ is a homeomorphism onto $h_u(U_z)\!\subset\!\Sigma'$. Thus, the Riemann surface structure~$\mathfrak j$ on~$\Sigma$ determines a Riemann surface structure~$\mathfrak j'$ on~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ so that $h_u|_{\Sigma_u^*}$ is a holomorphic covering projection of~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ and $u'|_{h_u(\Sigma_u^*)}$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \BE{SimplMap_e5}E_g ig(u';h_u(\Sigma_u^*) ig)\le E_g(u).\end{equation} By Corollary~ef{FHS_crl2}, $\Sigma_u'\!-\!h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ consists of finitely many points. By the first statement in Corollary~ef{SimplMap_crl} and by Lemma~ef{SimplMap_lmm3}, $\mathfrak j'$ extends over these points to a Riemann surface structure on~$\Sigma'$; we denote the extension also by~$\mathfrak j'$. Since the continuous map $h_u$ is $\mathfrak j'$-holomorphic outside of the finitely many points of $\Sigma\!-\!\Sigma_u^*$, it is holomorphic everywhere. Since the continuous map~$u'$ is $J$-holomorphic on~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$, (ef{SimplMap_e5}) and Proposition~ef{JHolomreg_prp} imply that it is $J$-holomorphic everywhere.\ 
oindent Suppose $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $z_i,z_i'\!\in\!\Sigma$ with $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ are such that $$	extnormal{d}_zu
eq0, \qquad z_i
eq z_i',~u(z_i)=u(z_i')~~ orall\,i, \qquad \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i=z.$$ Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the sequence $z_i'$ converges to some point \hbox{$z'\!\in\!\Sigma$} with $u(z')\!=\!u(z)$. Since the restriction of~$u$ to a neighborhood of~$z$ is an embedding, $z'\!
eq\!z$. By Corollary~ef{FHS_crl2b}, there exists a diffeomorphism~$\varphi_{z'z}$ as in~(ef{vphcond_e}). Thus, $h_u(z)\!=\!h_u(z')$, the map $h_u$ is not injective, and $u$ is not simple.
nodes.statement_short: Build a Riemann surface structure on the quotient Sigma' so that h_u and u' are holomorphic (using Lemma 4.13 and removable singularities via Proposition 4.8); a simple map then has injective h_u, and Corollary 3.10 handles limit points.

nodes.name: recall the quotient
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma'$, $h_u$, and $u'$ be as in~(\ref{SimplMap_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Recall Sigma', h_u, u'.

nodes.name: Hausdorff quotient
nodes.statement: By the second statement in Corollary~\ref{SimplMap_crl} and \cite[Lemma~73.3]{Mu}, $\Sigma'$ is a Hausdorff topological space. Fix a Riemannian metric~$g$ on~$X$.

nodes.name: complex structure on the regular part
nodes.statement: For $(z,z')\!\in\!\mathcal R_u^*$ with $z\!\neq\!z'$, the neighborhoods $U_z$ and~$U_{z'}$ as in~(\ref{vphcond_e}) can be chosen so that they are disjoint and $u|_{U_z}$ is an embedding. Since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, $\varphi_{z'z}$ is then a biholomorphic map and $h_u|_{U_z}$ is a homeomorphism onto $h_u(U_z)\!\subset\!\Sigma'$. Thus, the Riemann surface structure~$\mathfrak j$ on~$\Sigma$ determines a Riemann surface structure~$\mathfrak j'$ on~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ so that $h_u|_{\Sigma_u^*}$ is a holomorphic covering projection of~$h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ and $u'|_{h_u(\Sigma_u^*)}$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \BE{SimplMap_e5}E_g\big(u';h_u(\Sigma_u^*)\big)\le E_g(u).\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The structure j descends over h_u(Sigma_u^*).

nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2}, $\Sigma_u'\!-\!h_u(\Sigma_u^*)$ consists of finitely many points.

nodes.statement: By the first statement in Corollary~\ref{SimplMap_crl} and by Lemma~\ref{SimplMap_lmm3}, $\mathfrak j'$ extends over these points to a Riemann surface structure on~$\Sigma'$; we denote the extension also by~$\mathfrak j'$.

Suppose $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $z_i,z_i'\!\in\!\Sigma$ with $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ are such that $$	extnormal{d}_zu

eq z_i',~u(z_i)=u(z_i')~~ orall\,i, \qquad \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}z_i=z.$$ Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the sequence $z_i'$ converges to some point \hbox{$z'\!\in\!\Sigma$} with $u(z')\!=\!u(z)$. Since the restriction of~$u$ to a neighborhood of~$z$ is an embedding, $z'\!
eq\!z$.

nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl2b}, there exists a diffeomorphism~$\varphi_{z'z}$ as in~(\ref{vphcond_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 3.10 provides phi_{z'z}.
