nodes.statement_short: h_u is not injective, so u is not simple.

nodes.name: energy bound on long cylinders
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, then there exist continuous functions $\delta_{J,g},\hbar_{J,g},C_{J,g}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following properties. If \hbox{$u\!:[-R,R]\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} map such that $\textnormal{Im}\,u\subset B_{\delta_{J,g}(u(0,1))}^g(u(0,1))$, then \BE{CylEner_e} E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big)\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) \qquad\forall~T\ge0\,.\end{equation} If in addition $E_g(u)<\hbar_{J,g}\big(u(0,1)\big)$, then \BE{CylEner_e2} \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big) \textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~T\ge1\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: On a long cylinder with image in a small ball, energy and image diameter of the middle part decay exponentially in the distance T to the ends.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$
conclusions: there exist continuous functions $\delta_{J,g},\hbar_{J,g},C_{J,g}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following properties
E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big)\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) \qquad\forall~T\ge0\,.
\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big) \textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~T\ge1\,.
E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big)\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) \qquad\forall~T\ge0\,.
\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big) \textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~T\ge1\,.

nodes.label: CylEner_prp

nodes.name: Eq. CylEner_e
nodes.statement: E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big)\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) \qquad\forall~T\ge0\,.

nodes.name: Eq. CylEner_e2
nodes.statement: \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) \le C_{J,g}\big(u(1,0)\big) \textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~T\ge1\,.

nodes.name: energy bound on long cylinders for compact targets
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, there exist $\hbar_{J,g},C_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $u\!:[-R,R]\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} map such that $E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$, then \begin{alignat*}{2} E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) &\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) &\qquad&\forall~T\ge1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) &\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} &\quad&\forall~T\ge2\,. \end{alignat*}
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$
conclusions: there exist $\hbar_{J,g},C_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property

E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1\big) &\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T}E_g(u) &\qquad&\forall~T\ge1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\!\times\!S^1)\big) &\le C_{J,g}\textnormal{e}^{-T/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)} &\quad&\forall~T\ge2\,.
nodes.label: CylEner_crl

nodes.name: energy of the standard map from a cylinder
nodes.statement: As an example, the energy of the injective map $$[-R,R]\times S^1\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}, \qquad (s,\theta)\longrightarrow s\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\,,$$ is the area of its image, i.e.~$\pi(\textnormal{e}^{2R}\!-\!\textnormal{e}^{-2R}\big)$. Thus, the exponent $\textnormal{e}^{-T}$ in~(\ref{CylEner_e}) can be replaced by~$\textnormal{e}^{-2T}$ in this case.

nodes.name: the exponent in the cylinder energy bound
nodes.statement: The proof of Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp} shows that in general the exponent can be taken to be~$\textnormal{e}^{-\mu T}$ with $\mu$ arbitrarily close to~2, but at the cost of increasing~$C_{J,g}$ and reducing~$\delta_{J,g}$.

nodes.name: Poincare Inequality
nodes.statement: If $f\!: S^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^n$ is a smooth function such that $\int_0^{2\pi}\!f(\theta)\textnormal{d}\theta\!=\!0$, then $$\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\le\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f'(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta.$$
assumptions: $f\!: S^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^n$ is a smooth function
conclusions: $$\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\le\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f'(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta.$$
nodes.label: poin_lmm

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.18 (Poincare Inequality)
nodes.statement: We can write $f(\theta)=\sum\limits_{k>-\infty}\limits^{k<\infty}\!a_k\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i k\theta}$. Since $\int_0^{2\pi}\!f(\theta)\textnormal{d}\theta\!=\!0$, $a_0\!=\!0$. Thus, $$\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta= \sum_{k>-\infty}^{k<\infty}\!|a_k|^2\le \sum_{k>-\infty}^{k<\infty}\!|ka_k|^2= \int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f'(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta.$$
nodes.statement_short: Fourier series: the mean-zero condition kills a_0 and |a_k| <= |k a_k|.

nodes.name: Fourier expansion
nodes.statement: We can write $f(\theta)=\sum\limits_{k>-\infty}\limits^{k<\infty}\!a_k\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i k\theta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand f in Fourier series.

nodes.name: compare coefficients
nodes.statement: Since $\int_0^{2\pi}\!f(\theta)\textnormal{d}\theta\!=\!0$, $a_0\!=\!0$. Thus, $$\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta= \sum_{k>-\infty}^{k<\infty}\!|a_k|^2\le \sum_{k>-\infty}^{k<\infty}\!|ka_k|^2= \int_0^{2\pi}\!\!|f'(\theta)|^2\textnormal{d}\theta.$$
nodes.statement_short: a_0 = 0 and Parseval gives the inequality.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4.16
nodes.statement: It is sufficient to establish the first statement under the assumption that $(X,g)$ is $\mathbb{C}^n$ with the standard Riemannian metric, $J$ agrees with the standard complex structure~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at $0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n$, and $u(0,1)\!=\!0$. Let $$\bar\partial u=\frac12\big(u_t+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}u_{\theta}\big)\,.$$ By our assumptions, there exist $\delta',C\!>\!0$ (dependent on~$u(0,1)$) such that \BE{CylEnerPf_e1} \big|\bar\partial_z u\big|\le C\delta \big|\textnormal{d}_z u\big| \qquad\forall~z\in u^{-1}\big(B_{\delta}(0)\big),~\delta\le\delta'\,.\end{equation} Write $u\!=\!f\!+\!\mathfrak i g$, with $f,g$ taking values in~$\mathbb R^n$ and assume that $\textnormal{Im}\,u\!\subset\!B_{\delta}(0)$. By~(\ref{omEner_e}), $$|\textnormal{d} u|^2=4\big|\bar\partial u\big|^2+2\textnormal{d}(f\!\cdot\!\textnormal{d} g).$$ Combining this with~(\ref{CylEnerPf_e1}) and Stokes' Theorem, we obtain \BE{CylEnerPf_e3} \int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 \le 4C^2\delta^2\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 +2\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta -2\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\,.\end{equation} Let $\ti{f}\!=\!f\!-\!\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\!f\textnormal{d}\theta$. By H\"older's inequality and Lemma~\ref{poin_lmm}, \BE{CylEnerPf_e5}\begin{split} \bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| &=\bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!\ti{f}\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| \le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}\\ &\le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \le \frac12 \int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|u_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\,. \end{split}\end{equation} Since $$3|u_{\theta}|^2=2|u_{\theta}|^2+\big|u_t-2\bar\partial u\big|^2 \le 2|\textnormal{d} u|^2 + 8\big|\bar\partial u\big|^2\,, $$ the inequalities (\ref{CylEnerPf_e1})-(\ref{CylEnerPf_e5}) give $$ \big(1\!-\!4C^2\delta^2\big)\!\!\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 \le \frac{2}{3}\big(1\!+\!4C^2\delta^2\big) \bigg(\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta +\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg).$$ Thus, the function $$\varepsilon(T)\equiv E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\big) \equiv \frac12\int_{[-R+T,R-T]\times S^1}\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\textnormal{d} t$$ satisfies $\varepsilon(T)\!\le\!-\varepsilon'(T)$ for all $T\!\in\![-R,R]$, if $\delta$ is sufficiently small (depending on~$C$). This implies~(\ref{CylEner_e}).\\ \noindent Let $h_{J,g}(x)\!=\!(x,\delta_{J,g}(x))$, with $h_{J,g}(\cdot,\cdot)$ as in Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and $\delta_{J,g}(\cdot)$ as provided by the previous paragraph. Suppose $u$ also satisfies the last condition in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp}. By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and~(\ref{CylEner_e}), $$|\textnormal{d}_{(t,\theta)}u|\le 3\sqrt{E_g(u;[-|t|\!-\!1,|t|\!+\!1]\!\times\!S^1)} \le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}$$ for all $t\in[-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]$ and $\theta\!\in\!S^1$. Thus, for all $t_1,t_2\!\in\![-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]$ with $T\!\ge\!1$ and $\theta_1,\theta_2\!\in\!S^1$, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} d_g\big(u(t_1,\theta_1),u(t_2,\theta_2)\big) &\le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))E_g(u)} \bigg(\pi\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t_1|-R)/2}+\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\!\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\\ &\le \big(3\pi\!+\!12\big) \sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\,\textnormal{e}^{(1-T)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}\,. \end{split}\end{equation*} This establishes~(\ref{CylEner_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Isoperimetric-type differential inequality for the energy of the middle segment, eps(T) <= -eps'(T), from Stokes' Theorem and the Poincare Inequality; the diameter bound then follows from the Mean Value Inequality.

nodes.name: local model
nodes.statement: It is sufficient to establish the first statement under the assumption that $(X,g)$ is $\mathbb{C}^n$ with the standard Riemannian metric, $J$ agrees with the standard complex structure~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at $0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n$, and $u(0,1)\!=\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to C^n with J standard at 0.

nodes.name: dbar small
nodes.statement: Let $$\bar\partial u=\frac12\big(u_t+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}u_{\theta}\big)\,.$$ By our assumptions, there exist $\delta',C\!>\!0$ (dependent on~$u(0,1)$) such that \BE{CylEnerPf_e1} \big|\bar\partial_z u\big|\le C\delta \big|\textnormal{d}_z u\big| \qquad\forall~z\in u^{-1}\big(B_{\delta}(0)\big),~\delta\le\delta'\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: dbar u is small relative to du near 0.

nodes.name: Eq. CylEnerPf_e1
nodes.statement: \big|\bar\partial_z u\big|\le C\delta \big|\textnormal{d}_z u\big| \qquad\forall~z\in u^{-1}\big(B_{\delta}(0)\big),~\delta\le\delta'\,.

nodes.name: Stokes formula
nodes.statement: Write $u\!=\!f\!+\!\mathfrak i g$, with $f,g$ taking values in~$\mathbb R^n$ and assume that $\textnormal{Im}\,u\!\subset\!B_{\delta}(0)$. By~(\ref{omEner_e}), $$|\textnormal{d} u|^2=4\big|\bar\partial u\big|^2+2\textnormal{d}(f\!\cdot\!\textnormal{d} g).$$ Combining this with~(\ref{CylEnerPf_e1}) and Stokes' Theorem, we obtain \BE{CylEnerPf_e3} \int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 \le 4C^2\delta^2\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 +2\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta -2\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Energy density splits into a dbar part and an exact form; apply Stokes' Theorem.

nodes.name: Eq. CylEnerPf_e3
nodes.statement: \int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 \le 4C^2\delta^2\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 +2\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta -2\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\,.

nodes.name: boundary terms via Poincare
nodes.statement: Let $\ti{f}\!=\!f\!-\!\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\!f\textnormal{d}\theta$. By H\"older's inequality and Lemma~\ref{poin_lmm}, \BE{CylEnerPf_e5}\begin{split} \bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| &=\bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!\ti{f}\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| \le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}\\ &\le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \le \frac12 \int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|u_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\,. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the boundary terms by Holder and the Poincare Inequality.

nodes.name: Eq. CylEnerPf_e5
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| &=\bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!\ti{f}\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg| \le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}\\ &\le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12} \le \frac12 \int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|u_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\,. \end{split}

nodes.name: energy inequality
nodes.statement: Since $$3|u_{\theta}|^2=2|u_{\theta}|^2+\big|u_t-2\bar\partial u\big|^2 \le 2|\textnormal{d} u|^2 + 8\big|\bar\partial u\big|^2\,, $$ the inequalities (\ref{CylEnerPf_e1})-(\ref{CylEnerPf_e5}) give $$ \big(1\!-\!4C^2\delta^2\big)\!\!\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2 \le \frac{2}{3}\big(1\!+\!4C^2\delta^2\big) \bigg(\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta +\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg).$$
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound the middle energy by boundary energy.

nodes.name: exponential decay
nodes.statement: Thus, the function $$\varepsilon(T)\equiv E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\big) \equiv \frac12\int_{[-R+T,R-T]\times S^1}\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\textnormal{d} t$$ satisfies $\varepsilon(T)\!\le\!-\varepsilon'(T)$ for all $T\!\in\![-R,R]$, if $\delta$ is sufficiently small (depending on~$C$). This implies~(\ref{CylEner_e}).
nodes.statement_short: eps(T) <= -eps'(T), giving (4.20).

nodes.name: small energy setup
nodes.statement: Let $h_{J,g}(x)\!=\!(x,\delta_{J,g}(x))$, with $h_{J,g}(\cdot,\cdot)$ as in Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and $\delta_{J,g}(\cdot)$ as provided by the previous paragraph. Suppose $u$ also satisfies the last condition in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose constants for the second statement.

nodes.name: pointwise derivative decay
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and~(\ref{CylEner_e}), $$|\textnormal{d}_{(t,\theta)}u|\le 3\sqrt{E_g(u;[-|t|\!-\!1,|t|\!+\!1]\!\times\!S^1)} \le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}$$ for all $t\in[-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]$ and $\theta\!\in\!S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: Mean Value Inequality and (4.20) bound |du| exponentially.

nodes.name: diameter bound
nodes.statement: Thus, for all $t_1,t_2\!\in\![-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]$ with $T\!\ge\!1$ and $\theta_1,\theta_2\!\in\!S^1$, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} d_g\big(u(t_1,\theta_1),u(t_2,\theta_2)\big) &\le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))E_g(u)} \bigg(\pi\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t_1|-R)/2}+\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\!\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\\ &\le \big(3\pi\!+\!12\big) \sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\,\textnormal{e}^{(1-T)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}\,. \end{split}\end{equation*} This establishes~(\ref{CylEner_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Integrate along paths to get (4.21).

nodes.name: small energy implies small diameter on cylinders
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$, there exists a continuous function $\epsilon_{J,g}\!:\mathbb R^+\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and \hbox{$u\!:(-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\epsilon_{J,g}(\delta)$, then $$\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u\big([-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1\big)\big)\le \delta\,.$$
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$
$\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and \hbox{$u\!:(-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\epsilon_{J,g}(\delta)$
conclusions: there exists a continuous function $\epsilon_{J,g}\!:\mathbb R^+\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property
$$\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u\big([-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1\big)\big)\le \delta\,.$$
nodes.label: CylCoord_lmm

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 4.19
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp} and the compactness of~$X$, there exists $c_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact connected Riemann surface with boundary, \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map, $x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are such~that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then \BE{CylCoord_e3} E_g(u)\ge c_{J,g}\delta^2\,.\end{equation} Let $\hbar_{J,g}\!>\!0$ be the minimal value of the function~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in the statement of Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} on the compact space $X\!\times\![0,\textnormal{diam}_g(X)]$.\\ \noindent Suppose $u\!:(-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$ and $$\delta_u\equiv\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1)\big)>32\sqrt{E_g(u)}.$$ By the first condition on~$u$, \begin{gather} \notag \big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g^2\le \frac{16}{\pi} E_g(u) \qquad\forall~z\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u(r\!\times\!S^1)\big)\le 8\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~r\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]. \end{gather} Let $r_-,r_0,r_+\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]$ and $\theta_-,\theta_0,\theta_+\!\in\!S^1$ be such that $$r_-<r_0<r_+,\quad d_g\big(u(r_0,\theta_0),u(r_{\pm},\theta_{\pm})\big)\ge \frac12\delta_u\,.$$ By~(\ref{CylCoord_e7}), we can apply~(\ref{CylCoord_e3}) with $$\Sigma=[r_-,r_+]\!\times\!S^1,\qquad x=u(r_0,\theta_0), \qquad \delta=\frac14\delta_u,$$ and $u$ replaced by its restriction to~$\Sigma$. We conclude~that $$E_g(u)\ge \frac{c_{J,g}}{16}\delta_u^2\,.$$ It follows that the function $$\epsilon_{J,g}\!:\mathbb R^+\longrightarrow\mathbb R^+, \qquad \epsilon_{J,g}(\delta)=\min\bigg(\hbar_{J,g},\frac{\delta^2}{32^2}, \frac{c_{J,g}}{16}\delta^2\bigg),$$ has the desired property.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity Lemma gives a lower energy bound for any large diameter, while the Mean Value Inequality bounds the diameter of circles.

nodes.name: uniform constants
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{MonotLmm_prp} and the compactness of~$X$, there exists $c_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact connected Riemann surface with boundary, \hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map, $x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are such~that $u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then \BE{CylCoord_e3} E_g(u)\ge c_{J,g}\delta^2\,.\end{equation} Let $\hbar_{J,g}\!>\!0$ be the minimal value of the function~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in the statement of Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} on the compact space $X\!\times\![0,\textnormal{diam}_g(X)]$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform constant c_{J,g} in the Monotonicity Lemma and hbar from the Mean Value Inequality.

nodes.name: Eq. CylCoord_e3
nodes.statement: E_g(u)\ge c_{J,g}\delta^2\,.

nodes.name: large diameter assumption
nodes.statement: Suppose $u\!:(-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with $E_g(u)\!<\!\hbar_{J,g}$ and $$\delta_u\equiv\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u([-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1)\big)>32\sqrt{E_g(u)}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Suppose the diameter is large compared to sqrt(E).

nodes.name: circles are small
nodes.statement: By the first condition on~$u$, \begin{gather} \notag \big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g^2\le \frac{16}{\pi} E_g(u) \qquad\forall~z\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u(r\!\times\!S^1)\big)\le 8\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~r\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]. \end{gather}
nodes.statement_short: Mean Value Inequality bounds |du| and circle diameters.

nodes.name: Eq. (4.3) CylCoord_e7
nodes.statement: \notag \big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g^2\le \frac{16}{\pi} E_g(u) \qquad\forall~z\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]\!\times\!S^1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u(r\!\times\!S^1)\big)\le 8\sqrt{E_g(u)} \quad\forall~r\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1].
nodes.label: CylCoord_e7

nodes.name: three circles
nodes.statement: Let $r_-,r_0,r_+\!\in\![-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]$ and $\theta_-,\theta_0,\theta_+\!\in\!S^1$ be such that $$r_-<r_0<r_+,\quad d_g\big(u(r_0,\theta_0),u(r_{\pm},\theta_{\pm})\big)\ge \frac12\delta_u\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Pick circles at distance at least half the diameter.

nodes.name: apply monotonicity
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{CylCoord_e7}), we can apply~(\ref{CylCoord_e3}) with $$\Sigma=[r_-,r_+]\!\times\!S^1,\qquad x=u(r_0,\theta_0), \qquad \delta=\frac14\delta_u,$$ and $u$ replaced by its restriction to~$\Sigma$. We conclude~that $$E_g(u)\ge \frac{c_{J,g}}{16}\delta_u^2\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity gives E >= c delta_u^2/16.

nodes.name: choice of epsilon
nodes.statement: It follows that the function $$\epsilon_{J,g}\!:\mathbb R^+\longrightarrow\mathbb R^+, \qquad \epsilon_{J,g}(\delta)=\min\bigg(\hbar_{J,g},\frac{\delta^2}{32^2}, \frac{c_{J,g}}{16}\delta^2\bigg),$$ has the desired property.
nodes.statement_short: epsilon_{J,g} has the property.

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 4.17
nodes.statement: Let $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be the minimum of the function~$\delta_{J,g}$ in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp} and $\varepsilon_{J,g}(\cdot)$ be as in Lemma~\ref{CylCoord_lmm}. Take $C_{J,g}$ to be the maximum of the function~$C_{J,g}$ in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp} times~$\textnormal{e}$ and $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ to be smaller than the minimum of the function~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp} and the number~$\varepsilon_{J,g}(\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the extrema of the functions in Proposition 4.16 over compact X, together with Lemma 4.19.

nodes.name: bounded holomorphic maps on punctured disks extend
nodes.statement: By Cauchy's Integral Formula, a bounded holomorphic map $u\!:B_{\mathbb R}^*\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ extends over the origin.

nodes.name: Removal of Singularity
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold and $u\!:B_R^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a $J$-holomorphic map. If the energy $E_g(u)$ of~$u$, with respect to any metric~$g$ on~$X$, is finite, then $u$ extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\ti{u}\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold
the energy $E_g(u)$ of~$u$, with respect to any metric~$g$ on~$X$, is finite
conclusions: $u$ extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\ti{u}\!:B_R\!\longrightarrow\!X$
nodes.label: RemSing_prp

nodes.name: 1/z has infinite energy
nodes.statement: A basic example of a holomorphic function $u\!:\mathbb{C}^*\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}$ that does not extend over the origin $0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ is $z\!\longrightarrow\!1/z$. The energy of $u|_{B_R^*}$ with respect to the standard metric on~$\mathbb{C}$ is given~by $$E\big(u;B_R^*\big) =\frac12\int_{B_R}|\textnormal{d} u|^2 =\int_{B_R}\frac{1}{|z|^2} =\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^R\!\! r^{-1}\textnormal{d} r\textnormal{d}\theta \not<\infty.$$ The above integral would have been finite if $|\textnormal{d} u|^2$ were replaced by $|\textnormal{d} u|^{2-\epsilon}$ for {\it any} $\epsilon\!>\!0$.

nodes.name: removal of singularity for integrable J in a chart
nodes.statement: By Cauchy's Integral Formula, the conclusion of Proposition~\ref{RemSing_prp} holds if $J$ is an integrable almost complex structure and $u(B_{\delta}^*)$ is contained in a complex coordinate chart for some $\delta\!\in\!(0,R)$.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 5.1 (Removal of Singularity)
nodes.statement: In light of Proposition~\ref{JHolomreg_prp}, it is to sufficient to show that $u$ extends continuously over the origin. Let $c_{J,g},\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{CylCoord_lmm}. We can assume that $R\!=\!1$ and $u$ is non-constant. Define $$v\!: \mathbb R^-\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X, \qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}).$$ This map is $J$-holomorphic and satisfies $E_g(v)\!=\!E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$.\\ \noindent Since $E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$, \BE{RemSing_e3}\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1\big) =\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u;B_{e^r}^*\big)=0.\end{equation} In particular, there exists $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^-$ such that $$E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~r\!<\!R.$$ By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and our choice of $\hbar_{J,g}$, this implies that \begin{gather*} \big|\textnormal{d}_zv\big|_g^2\le \frac{16}{\pi}E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r\!+\!1)\!\times\!S^1\big) \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1,~r\!<\!R\!-\!1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(v(\{r\}\!\times\!S^1)\big)\le4\sqrt{\pi} \sqrt{E_g(v;(-\infty,r\!+\!1)\!\times\!S^1)} \quad\forall~r\!<\!R\!-\!1. \end{gather*} Combining the last bound with~(\ref{RemSing_e3}), we obtain $$\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\textnormal{diam}_g\big(v(\{r\}\!\times\!S^1)\big)=0.$$ Thus, it remains to show that $\lim\limits_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!v(r,1)$ exists.\\ \noindent Since $X$ is compact, every sequence in~$X$ has a convergent subsequence. Suppose there exist \begin{gather*} \delta\in\mathbb R^+,~~x,y\in X,~~i_k,r_k\in\mathbb R^- \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\\ d_g(x,y)>3\delta,~~ r_{k+1}<i_k<r_k,~~ v\big(\{i_k\}\!\times\!S^1\big)\subset B_{\delta}(x), ~~ v\big(\{r_k\}\!\times\!S^1\big)\subset B_{\delta}(y). \end{gather*} We thus can apply~(\ref{CylCoord_e3}) with $\Sigma$, $x$, and $u$ replaced by $$\Sigma_k\equiv[r_{k+1},r_k]\!\times\!S^1,\qquad x_k\equiv u(i_k,1), \quad\hbox{and}\quad v_k\equiv v|_{\Sigma_k}\,,$$ respectively. We conclude~that $$E_g(v)\ge \sum_kE_g\big(v;\Sigma_k\big) = \sum_kE_g(v_k) \ge \sum_k c_{J,g}\delta^2=\infty\,.$$ However, this contradicts the assumption that $E_g(v)\!=\!E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: By Proposition 4.8 it suffices to extend continuously; small circles have small image by the Mean Value Inequality, and oscillation between two far points would cost infinite energy by the Monotonicity Lemma.

nodes.name: reduce to continuity
nodes.statement: In light of Proposition~\ref{JHolomreg_prp}, it is to sufficient to show that $u$ extends continuously over the origin.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to extend u continuously.

nodes.name: cylinder coordinates
nodes.statement: Let $c_{J,g},\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{CylCoord_lmm}. We can assume that $R\!=\!1$ and $u$ is non-constant. Define $$v\!: \mathbb R^-\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X, \qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}).$$ This map is $J$-holomorphic and satisfies $E_g(v)\!=\!E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the half-cylinder map v.

nodes.name: energy tails vanish
nodes.statement: Since $E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$, \BE{RemSing_e3}\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1\big) =\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u;B_{e^r}^*\big)=0.\end{equation} In particular, there exists $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^-$ such that $$E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~r\!<\!R.$$
nodes.statement_short: Energy of the ends tends to 0.

nodes.name: Eq. RemSing_e3
nodes.statement: \lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1\big) =\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u;B_{e^r}^*\big)=0.

nodes.name: circle diameters
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and our choice of $\hbar_{J,g}$, this implies that \begin{gather*} \big|\textnormal{d}_zv\big|_g^2\le \frac{16}{\pi}E_g\big(v;(-\infty,r\!+\!1)\!\times\!S^1\big) \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!(-\infty,r)\!\times\!S^1,~r\!<\!R\!-\!1,\\ \textnormal{diam}_g\big(v(\{r\}\!\times\!S^1)\big)\le4\sqrt{\pi} \sqrt{E_g(v;(-\infty,r\!+\!1)\!\times\!S^1)} \quad\forall~r\!<\!R\!-\!1. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Mean Value Inequality bounds circle diameters.

nodes.name: circles shrink
nodes.statement: Combining the last bound with~(\ref{RemSing_e3}), we obtain $$\lim_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\textnormal{diam}_g\big(v(\{r\}\!\times\!S^1)\big)=0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Diameters of circles tend to 0.

nodes.name: reduce to a limit along a ray
nodes.statement: Thus, it remains to show that $\lim\limits_{r\longrightarrow-\infty}\!v(r,1)$ exists.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to show v(r,1) converges.

nodes.name: assume oscillation
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is compact, every sequence in~$X$ has a convergent subsequence. Suppose there exist \begin{gather*} \delta\in\mathbb R^+,~~x,y\in X,~~i_k,r_k\in\mathbb R^- \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\\ d_g(x,y)>3\delta,~~ r_{k+1}<i_k<r_k,~~ v\big(\{i_k\}\!\times\!S^1\big)\subset B_{\delta}(x), ~~ v\big(\{r_k\}\!\times\!S^1\big)\subset B_{\delta}(y). \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Suppose v oscillates between neighborhoods of x and y.

nodes.name: monotonicity on each segment
nodes.statement: We thus can apply~(\ref{CylCoord_e3}) with $\Sigma$, $x$, and $u$ replaced by $$\Sigma_k\equiv[r_{k+1},r_k]\!\times\!S^1,\qquad x_k\equiv u(i_k,1), \quad\hbox{and}\quad v_k\equiv v|_{\Sigma_k}\,,$$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Each segment carries energy at least c delta^2.

nodes.name: contradiction
nodes.statement: We conclude~that $$E_g(v)\ge \sum_kE_g\big(v;\Sigma_k\big) = \sum_kE_g(v_k) \ge \sum_k c_{J,g}\delta^2=\infty\,.$$ However, this contradicts the assumption that $E_g(v)\!=\!E_g(u)\!<\!\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Infinite energy contradicts finiteness.

nodes.name: energy concentration function at a bubble point
nodes.statement: Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$ and \hbox{$u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such that the limit \BE{fmdfn_e}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation} exists and is nonzero. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item The limit $\mathfrak m(\delta)\equiv\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})$ exists and is a continuous, non-decreasing function of~$\delta$. \item For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0, $\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))\!=\!\mathfrak m(\delta)$. \item For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0, $\mu\!\in\!(0,\mathfrak m)$, and $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,1\!-\!|z_i|)$ such that $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$. Furthermore, \BE{EnerPres1Elim_e} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big) =\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu.\end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Energy concentration at a bubble point: the limiting energy function m(delta) is continuous and monotone, independent of the centers, and defines rescaling radii delta_i(mu).
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$

\hbox{$u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such that the limit \BE{fmdfn_e}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation} exists and is nonzero
conclusions: The limit $\mathfrak m(\delta)\equiv\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})$ exists and is a continuous, non-decreasing function of~$\delta$
For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0, $\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))\!=\!\mathfrak m(\delta)$

For every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_1$ converging to~0, $\mu\!\in\!(0,\mathfrak m)$, and $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,1\!-\!|z_i|)$ such that $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$. Furthermore, \BE{EnerPres1Elim_e} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big) =\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu.
nodes.label: EnerPres1_lmm

nodes.name: Eq. fmdfn_e
nodes.statement: \mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres1Elim_e
nodes.statement: \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big) =\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu.

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement:
ef{deEner_it} Since $	extnormal{d} u_i$ converges uniformly to $	extnormal{d} u$ on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$,  egin{equation*} egin{split} \mathfrak m(\delta)\equiv\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta} ig) &=\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta'} ig)+ \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}\!-\!B_{\delta'} ig)\ &=\mathfrak m+\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}E_g ig(u;B_{\delta}\!-\!B_{\delta'} ig) =\mathfrak m+E_g(u;B_{\delta}). \end{split}\end{equation*} Since $E_g(u;B_{\delta})$ is a continuous, non-decreasing function of~$\delta$, so is~$\mathfrak m(\delta)$.\ 
oindent ef{SeqEner_it} For all $\delta,\delta'\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta'}$, $B_{\delta-\delta'}\!\subset\!B_{\delta}(z_i)\!\subset\!B_{\delta+\delta'}$. Thus, $$E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta-\delta'} ig)\le E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i) ig) \le E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta+\delta'} ig)$$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large and $$\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta\!-\!\delta')\le \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i) ig) \le \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta\!+\!\delta') \qquad orall~\delta'\in\mathbb R^+\,.$$ The claim now follows from~ef{deEner_it}.\ 
oindent ef{dela_it} By~ef{SeqEner_it}, ef{deEner_it}, and~(ef{fmdfn_e}), $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i) ig)=\mathfrak m(\delta)\ge\mathfrak m\,.$$ Thus, there exists $i(\mu)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $$E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))>\mu \qquad orall~i\ge i(\mu).$$ Since $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))$ is a continuous, increasing function of~$\delta$ which vanishes at~$\delta\!=\!0$, for every $i\!\ge\!i(\mu)$ there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,\delta)$ such that $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$.\ 
oindent By~ef{SeqEner_it}, ef{deEner_it}, and~(ef{fmdfn_e}),  egin{equation*} egin{split} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i) ig) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(R\delta)=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m. \end{split}\end{equation*} Combining this with the definition of~$\delta_i(\mu)$, we obtain~(ef{EnerPres1Elim_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Direct limit arguments using uniform convergence away from 0 and continuity and monotonicity of the energy in the radius.

nodes.name: part (1)
nodes.statement: \ref{deEner_it} Since $\textnormal{d} u_i$ converges uniformly to $\textnormal{d} u$ on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \mathfrak m(\delta)\equiv\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}\big) &=\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta'}\big)+ \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}\!-\!B_{\delta'}\big)\\ &=\mathfrak m+\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}E_g\big(u;B_{\delta}\!-\!B_{\delta'}\big) =\mathfrak m+E_g(u;B_{\delta}). \end{split}\end{equation*} Since $E_g(u;B_{\delta})$ is a continuous, non-decreasing function of~$\delta$, so is~$\mathfrak m(\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: m(delta) = m + E_g(u; B_delta) is continuous and non-decreasing.

nodes.name: part (2)
nodes.statement: \ref{SeqEner_it} For all $\delta,\delta'\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ and $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta'}$, $B_{\delta-\delta'}\!\subset\!B_{\delta}(z_i)\!\subset\!B_{\delta+\delta'}$. Thus, $$E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta-\delta'}\big)\le E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big) \le E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta+\delta'}\big)$$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large and $$\lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta\!-\!\delta')\le \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big) \le \lim_{\delta'\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta\!+\!\delta') \qquad\forall~\delta'\in\mathbb R^+\,.$$ The claim now follows from~\ref{deEner_it}.
nodes.statement_short: Squeeze B_delta(z_i) between balls centered at 0.

nodes.name: part (3)
nodes.statement: \ref{dela_it} By~\ref{SeqEner_it}, \ref{deEner_it}, and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m(\delta)\ge\mathfrak m\,.$$ Thus, there exists $i(\mu)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $$E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))>\mu \qquad\forall~i\ge i(\mu).$$ Since $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))$ is a continuous, increasing function of~$\delta$ which vanishes at~$\delta\!=\!0$, for every $i\!\ge\!i(\mu)$ there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,\delta)$ such that $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$.\\ \noindent By~\ref{SeqEner_it}, \ref{deEner_it}, and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\big) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(R\delta)=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m. \end{split}\end{equation*} Combining this with the definition of~$\delta_i(\mu)$, we obtain~(\ref{EnerPres1Elim_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Existence of delta_i(mu) by continuity and the energy limit (5.3).

nodes.name: existence of delta_i(mu)
nodes.statement: \ref{dela_it} By~\ref{SeqEner_it}, \ref{deEner_it}, and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m(\delta)\ge\mathfrak m\,.$$ Thus, there exists $i(\mu)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $$E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))>\mu \qquad\forall~i\ge i(\mu).$$ Since $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i))$ is a continuous, increasing function of~$\delta$ which vanishes at~$\delta\!=\!0$, for every $i\!\ge\!i(\mu)$ there exists a unique $\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,\delta)$ such that $E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\!=\!\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Energy in B_delta(z_i) exceeds mu for large i, so a unique radius delta_i(mu) exists.

nodes.name: energy limit
nodes.statement: By~\ref{SeqEner_it}, \ref{deEner_it}, and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\big) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(R\delta)=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m. \end{split}\end{equation*} Combining this with the definition of~$\delta_i(\mu)$, we obtain~(\ref{EnerPres1Elim_e}).
nodes.statement_short: Compute the double limit to get (5.3).

nodes.name: no energy loss in the neck
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$, then there exists $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following properties. If $u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|_g=\infty$$ and the limit~(\ref{fmdfn_e}) exists, then \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item $\mathfrak m\ge\hbar_{J,g}$; \item for every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta}$ converging to~0 and $\mu\!\in\!(\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g},\mathfrak m)$, the numbers \hbox{$\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,1\!-\!|z_i|)$} of Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{dela_it} satisfy \begin{gather} \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))=\mathfrak m,\\ \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0} \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\big)=0. \end{gather} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Energy concentrating at a blow-up point is at least hbar, and no energy is lost and the image diameter vanishes in the neck between rescaling scales.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$

$u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|_g=\infty$$ and the limit~(\ref{fmdfn_e}) exists
conclusions: there exists $\hbar_{J,g}\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following properties

for every sequence $z_i\!\in\!B_{\delta}$ converging to~0 and $\mu\!\in\!(\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g},\mathfrak m)$, the numbers \hbox{$\delta_i(\mu)\!\in\!(0,1\!-\!|z_i|)$} of Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{dela_it} satisfy

nodes.name: Eq. (5.1) noEloss_e1
nodes.statement: \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))=\mathfrak m,

nodes.name: Eq. (5.2) noEloss_e2
nodes.statement: \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0} \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\big)=0.

nodes.name: proof of Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement_short: Part (1): rescale at points of maximal |du| to get a non-constant J-holomorphic plane, extend it to a sphere by removal of singularity, and use the lower energy bound. Part (2): the neck region is a long cylinder with small energy, so Corollary 4.17 gives energy and diameter decay.

nodes.name: choose hbar
nodes.statement: Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the smaller of the constants~$\hbar_{J,g}$ in Corollaries~\ref{LowEner_crl} and~\ref{CylEner_crl}. Let $u_i$, $u$, and~$\mathfrak m$ be as in the statement of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Take hbar the smaller of the constants in Corollaries 4.2 and 4.17.

nodes.name: part (1)
nodes.statement: \ref{fmLowBnd_it} For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let $$M_i=\max_{\ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\in\mathbb R^+$$ and $z_i\!\in\!\ov{B_{1/2}}$ be such that $|\textnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i|_g\!=\!M_i$. Since $M_i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ and $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to~$u$, $z_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$. For $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $|z_i|\!+\!1/\sqrt{M_i}\!<\!1/2$, define $$v_i\!:B_{\sqrt{M_i}}\longrightarrow X, \qquad v_i(z)=u_i\big(z_i\!+\!z/M_i\big).$$ Thus, $v_i$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \BE{EnerPres2_e3}\sup\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_0v_i\big|_g=1, \qquad E_g(v_i)=E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big)\le E_g\big(u_i;B_{|z_i|+1/\sqrt{M_i}}\big)\,.\end{equation} By the first statement in~(\ref{EnerPres2_e3}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator, a subsequence of~$v_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\mathbb{C}$ to a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v\!:\mathbb{C}\!\longrightarrow\!X$}. By the second statement in~(\ref{EnerPres2_e3}) and Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{deEner_it}, \BE{EnerPres2_e5} E_g(v) \le \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big) \le \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}\big)=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} By Proposition~\ref{RemSing_prp}, $v$ thus extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\wt{v}\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. By Corollary~\ref{LowEner_crl}, $$E_g(v)=E_g(\wt{v})\ge \hbar_{J,g}\,.$$ Combining this with~(\ref{EnerPres2_e5}), we obtain the first claim.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaling gives a bubble sphere of energy at most m and at least hbar.

nodes.name: points of maximal derivative
nodes.statement: \ref{fmLowBnd_it} For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let $$M_i=\max_{\ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\in\mathbb R^+$$ and $z_i\!\in\!\ov{B_{1/2}}$ be such that $|\textnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i|_g\!=\!M_i$. Since $M_i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ and $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to~$u$, $z_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$.
nodes.statement_short: Take M_i = max |du_i| attained at z_i -> 0.

nodes.name: rescaled maps
nodes.statement: For $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that $|z_i|\!+\!1/\sqrt{M_i}\!<\!1/2$, define $$v_i\!:B_{\sqrt{M_i}}\longrightarrow X, \qquad v_i(z)=u_i\big(z_i\!+\!z/M_i\big).$$ Thus, $v_i$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \BE{EnerPres2_e3}\sup\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_0v_i\big|_g=1, \qquad E_g(v_i)=E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big)\le E_g\big(u_i;B_{|z_i|+1/\sqrt{M_i}}\big)\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define v_i(z) = u_i(z_i + z/M_i) with |dv_i| <= 1 = |d_0 v_i|.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres2_e3
nodes.statement: \sup\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_0v_i\big|_g=1, \qquad E_g(v_i)=E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big)\le E_g\big(u_i;B_{|z_i|+1/\sqrt{M_i}}\big)\,.

nodes.name: limit plane
nodes.statement: By the first statement in~(\ref{EnerPres2_e3}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator, a subsequence of~$v_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\mathbb{C}$ to a non-constant $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v\!:\mathbb{C}\!\longrightarrow\!X$}.
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic bootstrapping gives a non-constant limit v: C -> X.

nodes.name: energy of the limit
nodes.statement: By the second statement in~(\ref{EnerPres2_e3}) and Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{deEner_it}, \BE{EnerPres2_e5} E_g(v) \le \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big) \le \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}\big)=\mathfrak m.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: E_g(v) <= m.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres2_e5
nodes.statement: E_g(v) \le \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/\sqrt{M_i}}(z_i)\big) \le \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}\big)=\mathfrak m.

nodes.name: extend to a sphere
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{RemSing_prp}, $v$ thus extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\wt{v}\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
nodes.statement_short: Removal of Singularity extends v over infinity.

nodes.name: lower bound
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{LowEner_crl}, $$E_g(v)=E_g(\wt{v})\ge \hbar_{J,g}\,.$$ Combining this with~(\ref{EnerPres2_e5}), we obtain the first claim.
nodes.statement_short: Lower Energy Bound gives m >= hbar.

nodes.name: part (2)
nodes.statement: \ref{noLoss_it} By the first two statements in Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm} and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), \BE{noLoss_e2} \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big)= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta)=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} After passing to a subsequence of~$u_i$, we can thus assume that there exists a sequence $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$ such~that \BE{noLoss_e3} \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} Since $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$, (\ref{noLoss_e2}) and (\ref{noLoss_e3}) imply that \BE{noLoss_e5}\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{R\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} \vspace{.1in} \noindent Suppose $\mu\!\in\!(\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g},\mathfrak m)$. By (\ref{noLoss_e5}) and the definition of~$\delta_i(\mu)$, $$ \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u;B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big) =\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu<\hbar_{J,g}\,.$$ Thus, Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl} applies with $(R,T)$ replaced by $(\frac12\ln(R\delta_i/\delta_i(\mu)),\ln R)$ and $u$ replaced by the $J$-holomorphic~map $$v\!: (-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X,\qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(z_i\!+\!\sqrt{R\delta_i\delta_i(\mu)}\,\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}\big).$$ By the first statement of Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl}, $$E_g\big(u;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)-E_g\big(u;B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)= E_g\big(u;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)\le \frac{C_{J,g}}{R}E_g(u)$$ for all $i$ sufficiently large (depending on~$R$); see Figure~\ref{CylEner_fig}. Combining this with (\ref{noLoss_e3}), we obtain~(\ref{noEloss_e1}).\\ \begin{figure} \begin{pspicture}(3,-.3)(9,2.7) \psset{unit=.3cm} \psline[linewidth=.06](56,7)(20,7) \psline[linewidth=.06](56,1)(20,1) \psarc[linewidth=.04](59,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](53,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](48,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](42,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](34,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](28,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](23,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](17,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \rput(56,7.8){$\mathfrak m$}\rput(56,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i\!+\!\ln R$}} \rput(45.2,7.8){$\mathfrak m$}\rput(45,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i$}} \rput(20.2,7.8){$\mu$}\rput(20,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i(\mu)$}} \rput(31.3,8){$\mu^*$}\rput(31,0){\sm{$\delta_i(\mu)\!+\!\ln R$}} \rput(38,4.5){\small{disappearing}}\rput(38,3){\small{energy}} \end{pspicture} \caption{Illustration for the proof of~(\ref{noEloss_e1})} \end{figure} \noindent It remains to establish~(\ref{noEloss_e2}). By~(\ref{EnerPres1Elim_e}), for all $R\!>\!0$ and sufficiently small $\delta\!>\!0$ (depending on~$R$) there exists $i(R,\delta)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such~that $$E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~i>i(R,\delta).$$ Thus, Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl} applies with $(R,T)$ replaced by $(\frac12\ln(R\delta/\delta_i(\mu)),\ln R)$ and $u$ replaced by the $J$-holomorphic~map $$v\!: (-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X,\qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(z_i\!+\!\sqrt{R\delta\delta_i(\mu)}\,\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}\big).$$ By the second statement of Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl}, $$\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\big) \le \frac{C_{J,g}}{\sqrt{R}}\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~i>i(R,\delta).$$ This gives~(\ref{noEloss_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: The neck between the rescaled scales is a long cylinder of small energy.

nodes.name: shrinking radii
nodes.statement: \ref{noLoss_it} By the first two statements in Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm} and~(\ref{fmdfn_e}), \BE{noLoss_e2} \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big)= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta)=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} After passing to a subsequence of~$u_i$, we can thus assume that there exists a sequence $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$ such~that \BE{noLoss_e3} \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.\end{equation} Since $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$, (\ref{noLoss_e2}) and (\ref{noLoss_e3}) imply that \BE{noLoss_e5}\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{R\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Choose delta_i -> 0 capturing all energy m.

nodes.name: Eq. noLoss_e2
nodes.statement: \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_i)\big)= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\mathfrak m(\delta)=\mathfrak m.

nodes.name: Eq. noLoss_e3
nodes.statement: \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.

nodes.name: Eq. noLoss_e5
nodes.statement: \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{R\delta_i}(z_i))=\mathfrak m.

nodes.name: neck as a cylinder
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mu\!\in\!(\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g},\mathfrak m)$. By (\ref{noLoss_e5}) and the definition of~$\delta_i(\mu)$, $$ \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u;B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big) =\mathfrak m\!-\!\mu<\hbar_{J,g}\,.$$ Thus, Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl} applies with $(R,T)$ replaced by $(\frac12\ln(R\delta_i/\delta_i(\mu)),\ln R)$ and $u$ replaced by the $J$-holomorphic~map $$v\!: (-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X,\qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(z_i\!+\!\sqrt{R\delta_i\delta_i(\mu)}\,\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}\big).$$
nodes.statement_short: The neck has energy below hbar, so Corollary 4.17 applies.

nodes.name: no energy loss
nodes.statement: By the first statement of Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl}, $$E_g\big(u;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)-E_g\big(u;B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)= E_g\big(u;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)\le \frac{C_{J,g}}{R}E_g(u)$$ for all $i$ sufficiently large (depending on~$R$); see Figure~\ref{CylEner_fig}. Combining this with (\ref{noLoss_e3}), we obtain~(\ref{noEloss_e1}).\\ \begin{figure} \begin{pspicture}(3,-.3)(9,2.7) \psset{unit=.3cm} \psline[linewidth=.06](56,7)(20,7) \psline[linewidth=.06](56,1)(20,1) \psarc[linewidth=.04](59,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](53,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](48,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](42,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](34,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](28,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \psarc[linewidth=.04](23,4){4.24}{135}{225} \psarc[linewidth=.04,linestyle=dotted](17,4){4.24}{-45}{45} \rput(56,7.8){$\mathfrak m$}\rput(56,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i\!+\!\ln R$}} \rput(45.2,7.8){$\mathfrak m$}\rput(45,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i$}} \rput(20.2,7.8){$\mu$}\rput(20,0){\sm{$\ln\delta_i(\mu)$}} \rput(31.3,8){$\mu^*$}\rput(31,0){\sm{$\delta_i(\mu)\!+\!\ln R$}} \rput(38,4.5){\small{disappearing}}\rput(38,3){\small{energy}} \end{pspicture} \caption{Illustration for the proof of~(\ref{noEloss_e1})} \end{figure}
nodes.statement_short: Energy in the neck decays like 1/R, giving (5.6).

nodes.name: neck for the diameter
nodes.statement: It remains to establish~(\ref{noEloss_e2}). By~(\ref{EnerPres1Elim_e}), for all $R\!>\!0$ and sufficiently small $\delta\!>\!0$ (depending on~$R$) there exists $i(R,\delta)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such~that $$E_g\big(u_i;B_{R\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i)\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~i>i(R,\delta).$$ Thus, Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl} applies with $(R,T)$ replaced by $(\frac12\ln(R\delta/\delta_i(\mu)),\ln R)$ and $u$ replaced by the $J$-holomorphic~map $$v\!: (-R,R)\!\times\!S^1\longrightarrow X,\qquad v\big(r,\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}\big)=u\big(z_i\!+\!\sqrt{R\delta\delta_i(\mu)}\,\textnormal{e}^{r+\mathfrak i\theta}\big).$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Corollary 4.17 to the neck between delta and R delta_i(mu).

nodes.name: diameter decay
nodes.statement: By the second statement of Corollary~\ref{CylEner_crl}, $$\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i(\mu)}(z_i))\big) \le \frac{C_{J,g}}{\sqrt{R}}\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\forall~i>i(R,\delta).$$ This gives~(\ref{noEloss_e2}).
nodes.statement_short: Diameter bound gives (5.7).

nodes.name: convergence away from finitely many bubble points
nodes.statement: If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$, then there exists a function $N\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!{\mathbb Z}$ with the following property. If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is compact Riemann surface, $S_0\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a finite subset, and $u_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps from open subsets of~$\Sigma$ with \BE{EnerPres3_e}U_i\subset U_{i+1}, \qquad \Sigma\!-\!S_0=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}\!U_i, \quad\hbox{and}\quad E\!\equiv\!\liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)<\infty,\end{equation} then there exist a subset $S\!\subset\!\Sigma$ with $|S|\!\le\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$ and a subsequence of $u_i$ converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!S$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded-energy sequences converge after passing to a subsequence away from at most N(E)+|S_0| points to a J-holomorphic map on all of Sigma.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is compact Riemann surface, $S_0\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a finite subset

$u_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps from open subsets of~$\Sigma$ with \BE{EnerPres3_e}U_i\subset U_{i+1}, \qquad \Sigma\!-\!S_0=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}\!U_i, \quad\hbox{and}\quad E\!\equiv\!\liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)<\infty
conclusions: there exists a function $N\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!{\mathbb Z}$ with the following property

there exist a subset $S\!\subset\!\Sigma$ with $|S|\!\le\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$ and a subsequence of $u_i$ converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!S$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$
nodes.label: EnerPres3_lmm

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres3_e
nodes.statement: U_i\subset U_{i+1}, \qquad \Sigma\!-\!S_0=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}\!U_i, \quad\hbox{and}\quad E\!\equiv\!\liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)<\infty,

nodes.name: proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement_short: Points where at least hbar of energy concentrates are at most N(E); away from them the Mean Value Inequality bounds |du_i|, so a diagonal subsequence converges; removal of singularity extends the limit.

nodes.name: define N(E)
nodes.statement: Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the minimal value of the function provided by Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}. For $E\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, let $N(E)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$ be the smallest integer such that $E\!\le\!N(E)\hbar_{J,g}$.
nodes.statement_short: N(E) is the least integer with E <= N(E) hbar.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma$, $S_0$, $u_i$, and $E$ be as in the statement of the lemma and $N\!=\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$. Fix a Riemannian metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ on~$\Sigma$. For $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $\delta\!\in\!\Sigma$, let $B_{\delta}(z)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ denote the ball of radius~$\delta$ around~$z$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a metric on Sigma and balls B_delta(z).

nodes.name: pointwise bound from small energy
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}, there exists $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property. If $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map, $z\!\in\!\Sigma$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, then \BE{EnerPres3_e3} E_g\big(u;B_{\delta}(z)\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g\le C/\delta^2\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Small energy on a ball bounds |du| at its center.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres3_e3
nodes.statement: E_g\big(u;B_{\delta}(z)\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g\le C/\delta^2\,.

nodes.name: energy concentration points
nodes.statement: For every pair $i,j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let $\{z_{ij}^k\}_{k=1}^N$ be a subset of points of~$\Sigma$ containing~$S_0$ such~that \BE{EnerPres3_e5} z\in \Sigma_{ij}^*\equiv\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{k=1}^N\!B_{2/j}\big(z_{ij}^k\big) \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/j}(z)\!\cap\!U_i\big)<\hbar_{J,g}\,.\end{equation} By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e3}) and~(\ref{EnerPres3_e5}), \BE{EnerPres3_e7} \big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!\Sigma_{ij}^* ~\hbox{s.t.}~B_{1/j}(z)\!\subset\!U_i\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: At most N points carry concentrated energy; elsewhere |du_i| <= C j^2.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres3_e5
nodes.statement: z\in \Sigma_{ij}^*\equiv\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{k=1}^N\!B_{2/j}\big(z_{ij}^k\big) \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/j}(z)\!\cap\!U_i\big)<\hbar_{J,g}\,.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres3_e7
nodes.statement: \big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!\Sigma_{ij}^* ~\hbox{s.t.}~B_{1/j}(z)\!\subset\!U_i\,.

nodes.name: converging concentration points
nodes.statement: After passing to a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, we can assume that the sequence $E_g(u_i)$ converges to~$E$ and that the sequence $\{z_{ij}^k\}_{i\in{\mathbb Z}^+}$ converges to some $z_j^k\!\in\!\Sigma$ for every $k\!=\!1,\ldots,N$ and $j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$. Along with~(\ref{EnerPres3_e7}) and the first two assumptions in~(\ref{EnerPres3_e}), this implies that \BE{EnerPres3_e9} \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 \qquad\forall\,z\in\Sigma_{ij}^*\,.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a subsequence where the concentration points converge.

nodes.name: Eq. EnerPres3_e9
nodes.statement: \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 \qquad\forall\,z\in\Sigma_{ij}^*\,.

nodes.name: limit points
nodes.statement: After passing to another subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, we can assume that the sequence $\{z_j^k\}_{j\in{\mathbb Z}^+}$ converges to some $z^k\!\in\!\Sigma$ for every $k\!=\!1,\ldots,N$.
nodes.statement_short: The points z_j^k converge to z^k.

nodes.name: convergence on the first pieces
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e9}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator, a subsequence of~$u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_1\!:\Sigma_1^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$}. By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e9}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator, a subsequence of this subsequence in turn converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_2^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_2\!:\Sigma_2^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$}.
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic bootstrapping gives convergence on Sigma_1^*, then Sigma_2^*.

nodes.name: diagonal argument
nodes.statement: Continuing in this way, we obtain a subsequence of~$u_i$ converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_j^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_j\!:\Sigma_j^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$} for every $j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$. The limiting maps satisfy $$v_j|_{\Sigma_j\cap\Sigma_{j'}^*}=v_{j'}|_{\Sigma_j^*\cap\Sigma_{j'}^*} \qquad\forall~j,j'\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+\,.$$ Thus, the~map $$u\!:\Sigma^*\!\equiv\!\Sigma^*\!-\!\big\{z^k\big\}\longrightarrow X, \qquad u(z)=v_j(z)~~\forall\,z\!\in\!\Sigma_j^*, $$ is well-defined and $J$-holomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal subsequence converges on every Sigma_j^* to a well-defined limit u.

nodes.name: extend the limit
nodes.statement: By construction, the final subsequence of $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma^*$ to~$u$. This implies~that $$E_g(u)\le \liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=E\,.$$ By Proposition~\ref{RemSing_prp}, $u$ thus extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
nodes.statement_short: The limit has energy at most E and extends over the points by Removal of Singularity.

nodes.name: tree of spheres
nodes.statement: We next show that a sequence of maps as in Corollary~\ref{EnerPres2_crl} gives rise to a continuous map from a \textsf{tree of spheres} attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$, i.e.~a connected union of spheres that have a distinguished, base component and no loops; the distinguished component will be attached at $\infty\!\in\!S^2$ to $0\!\in\!B_1$.

nodes.name: rooted linearly ordered set
nodes.statement: The combinatorial structure of such a tree is described by a finite \textsf{rooted linearly ordered set}, i.e.~a partially ordered set~$(I,\prec)$ such~that \begin{enumerate}[label=(RS\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item there is a minimal element (\textsf{root}) $i_0\!\in\!I$, i.e.~$i_0\!\prec\!h$ for every $h\!\in\!I\!-\!\{i_0\}$, and \item for all $h_1,h_2,i\!\in\!I$ with $h_1,h_2\!\prec\!i$, either $h_1\!=\!h_2$, or $h_1\!\prec\!h_2$, or $h_2\!\prec\!h_1$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: immediate predecessor
nodes.statement: For each $i\!\in\!I\!-\!\{i_0\}$, let $p(i)\!\in\!I$ denote \textsf{the immediate predecessor of~$i$}, i.e.~$p(i)\!\in\!I$ such that $h\!\prec\!p(i)\!\prec\!i$ for all $h\!\in\!I\!-\!\{p(i)\}$ such that $h\!\prec\!i$.

nodes.name: existence and uniqueness of immediate predecessors
nodes.statement: Such $p(i)\!\in\!I$ exists by~\ref{minelem_it} and is unique by~\ref{smalelem_it}.

nodes.name: tree of spheres associated with (I, z)
nodes.statement: Given a finite rooted linearly ordered set~$(I,\prec)$ with minimal element~$i_0$ and a function \BE{zcond_e}z\!:\,I\!-\!\{i_0\}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \quad i\longrightarrow z_i, \quad\hbox{s.t.}\quad \big(p(i_1),z_{i_1}\big)\neq \big(p(i_2),z_{i_2}\big) ~~\forall~i_1,i_2\in I\!-\!\{i_0\},~i_1\!\neq\!i_2,\end{equation} let $$\Sigma=\bigg(\bigsqcup_{i\in I}\{i\}\!\times\!S^2\!\bigg)\!\Big/\!\!\sim, \qquad (i,\infty)\sim\big(p(i),z_i)~~~\forall~i\!\in\!I\!-\!\{i_0\};$$ see the second diagram in Figure~\ref{glos_fig}.

nodes.name: Eq. zcond_e
nodes.statement: z\!:\,I\!-\!\{i_0\}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}, \quad i\longrightarrow z_i, \quad\hbox{s.t.}\quad \big(p(i_1),z_{i_1}\big)\neq \big(p(i_2),z_{i_2}\big) ~~\forall~i_1,i_2\in I\!-\!\{i_0\},~i_1\!\neq\!i_2,

nodes.name: the tree of spheres is a nodal Riemann surface
nodes.statement: The last condition in~(\ref{zcond_e}) insures that $\Sigma$ is a \textsf{nodal} Riemann surface, i.e.~each non-smooth point (\textsf{node}) has only two local branches (pieces homeomorphic to~$\mathbb{C}$).

nodes.name: bubble tree at a bubble point
nodes.statement: Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$ and $u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. If the limit \BE{fmdfn_e2}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation} exists and is nonzero, then there exist \begin{enumerate}[ref=\arabic*,label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item a nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ consisting of $B_1$ with a tree of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$, \item a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$, \item a subsequence of $\{u_i\}$ still denoted by $\{u_i\}$, and \item a biholomorphic map $\psi_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!B_{1/2}$, where $U_i\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset, \end{enumerate} such that \begin{enumerate}[label=(\ref{psi_it}\alph*),leftmargin=*] \item $E_g(u_{\infty};\Sigma_{\infty}\!-\!B_1)=\mathfrak m$, $U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$, and $\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_i$, \item $u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes $\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*$ in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_0^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$, \item if $u_{\infty}|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}$ is constant, $\mathbb{P}^1_0$ contains at least three nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$; \item (\ref{psi_it}) applies with $B_1$, $(\{u_i\},0)$, and~$\mathfrak m$ replaced by a neighborhood of~$w_r^*$ in~$\mathbb{C}$, $(\{u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\},w_r^*)$, and \BE{fmdfn_e3}\mathfrak m_r'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big),\end{equation} respectively, for each $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: At a point where energy m>0 concentrates, a subsequence converges after rescaling to a stable tree of J-holomorphic spheres carrying exactly energy m.
assumptions: $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
the limit \BE{fmdfn_e2}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation} exists and is nonzero
conclusions: there exist \begin{enumerate}[ref=\arabic*,label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item a nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ consisting of $B_1$ with a tree of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$, \item a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$, \item a subsequence of $\{u_i\}$ still denoted by $\{u_i\}$, and \item\label{psi_it} a biholomorphic map $\psi_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!B_{1/2}$, where $U_i\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset, \end{enumerate} such that \begin{enumerate}[label=(\ref{psi_it}\alph*),leftmargin=*] \item\label{Ccov_it} $E_g(u_{\infty};\Sigma_{\infty}\!-\!B_1)=\mathfrak m$, $U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$, and $\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_i$, \item\label{vcon_it} $u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes $\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*$ in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_0^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$, \item\label{stab_it} if $u_{\infty}|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}$ is constant, $\mathbb{P}^1_0$ contains at least three nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$; \item (\ref{psi_it}) applies with $B_1$, $(\{u_i\},0)$, and~$\mathfrak m$ replaced by a neighborhood of~$w_r^*$ in~$\mathbb{C}$, $(\{u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\},w_r^*)$, and \BE{fmdfn_e3}\mathfrak m_r'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big),\end{equation} respectively, for each $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.
nodes.label: EnerPres_prp

nodes.name: Eq. fmdfn_e2
nodes.statement: \mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})

nodes.name: Eq. fmdfn_e3
nodes.statement: \mathfrak m_r'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big),

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 5.5
nodes.statement:
Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the smaller of the numbers $\hbar_{J,g}$ in Corollaries~ef{LowEner_crl} and~ef{EnerPres2_crl}. In particular, $\mathfrak m\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.\ 
oindent For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, choose $z_i\!\in\!\ov{B_{1/2}}$ so~that \BE{maxdui_e} \max_{z\in \ov{B_{1/2}}} ig|	extnormal{d} u_i ig|_g= ig|	extnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i ig|_g.\end{equation} Since $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to~$u$, $z_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. Thus, $B_{1/2}(z_i)\!\subset\!B_1$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large. By Lemma~ef{EnerPres1_lmm}ef{dela_it}, for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exists $\delta_i\!\in\!(0,1/2)$ such~that \BE{dejidfn_e} E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i) ig)=\mathfrak m- rac{\hbar_{J,g}}{2}\,.\end{equation} Define $$\psi_i\!:U_i\!\equiv\! ig\{w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!: z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\!\in\!B_{1/2} ig\} \longrightarrow B_{1/2} \qquad\hbox{by}\qquad \psi_i(w)=z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\,.$$ Since $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the second property in ef{Ccov_it} holds.\ 
oindent For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, let $$v_i=u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\!: U_i\longrightarrow X.$$ Since $u_i$ is $J$-holomorphic and $\psi_i$ is biholomorphic onto its image, $v_i$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \hbox{$E_g(v_i)=E_g(u_i;B_{1/2})$}. Along with Lemma~ef{EnerPres1_lmm}ef{SeqEner_it}, this implies that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(v_i)=\mathfrak m(1/2)<\infty\,.$$ By Lemma~ef{EnerPres3_lmm}, there thus exist a finite collection $w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ of distinct points and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, such that $v_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. In particular, ef{vcon_it} holds and $|	extnormal{d} v_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$. We can also assume that the limit~(ef{fmdfn_e3}) exists for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. We note~that \BE{EnerBub_e} egin{split} E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!\mathfrak m_r' &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\! E_g\! ig(v_i,B_R\!-\! igcup_{r=1}^k\! B_{\delta}(w_r^*) ig) +\sum_{r=1}^k\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g ig(v_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*) ig)\ &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g ig(v_i,B_R ig) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g ig(u_i,B_{R\delta_i}(z_i) ig)=\mathfrak m\,; \end{split}\end{equation} the last equality holds by~(ef{noEloss_e1}).\ 
oindent Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)$ are pairwise disjoint. If $$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}} ig|	extnormal{d} v_i ig|<\infty$$ for some~$r$, then $\{v_i\}$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}$ to~$v$ by the ellipticity of the $ ar\partial$-operator. Thus, we can assume~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}} ig|	extnormal{d} v_i ig|=\infty$$ for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. In light of Corollary~ef{EnerPres2_crl}ef{fmLowBnd_it}, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.\  egin{figure}  egin{pspicture}(-.5,-2.5)(10,3.5) \psset{unit=.4cm} \pscircle[linewidth=.1](18,1){3}\pscircle*(21,1){.2}put(21.5,1){\sm{$1$}} \pscircle[linewidth=.07,linestyle=dotted](18,1){7}\pscircle*(25,1){.2} put(26.5,1){\sm{$\delta_0/\delta_i$}} put(18,1){\sm{$\mathfrak m- rac{\hbar}{2}$}}put(18,-4){\sm{$ rac{\hbar}{2}-\epsilon_i$}} \end{pspicture} \caption{The energy distribution of the rescaled map~$v_i$ in the proof of Proposition~ef{EnerPres_prp}} \end{figure} 
oindent We next show that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$, i.e.~that the bubble $(\mathbb{P}_0^1,v)$ connects to $(B_1,u)$ at~$z\!=\!0$. Note~that  egin{equation*} egin{split} d_g ig(u(0),v(\infty) ig) &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}d_g ig(u(\delta),v(R) ig) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}d_g ig(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),v_i(R) ig)\ &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} d_g ig(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),u_i(z_i\!+\!R\delta_i) ig)\ &\le \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} 	extnormal{diam}_g ig(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)) ig). \end{split}\end{equation*} Along with~(ef{noEloss_e2}), this implies that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$.\ 
oindent Suppose $v\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a constant map. By~(ef{EnerBub_e}), $k\!\ge\!1$ and so there exists $w^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ such that $|	extnormal{d}_{w^*}v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. By~(ef{maxdui_e}) and the definition of~$\psi_i$, $|	extnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\ge\!|	extnormal{d}_wv_i|$ for all $w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ contained in the domain of~$v_i$ and so $|	extnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. By~(ef{fmdfn_e3}) and~(ef{dejidfn_e}), $$\mathfrak m_0'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g(v_i) \le \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g ig(v_i;B_1 ig) =\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i) ig) = \mathfrak m- rac{\hbar}{2}<\mathfrak m,$$ and so $k\!\ge\!2$, as claimed in~ef{stab_it}. Since the amount of energy of $v_i$ contained in $\mathbb{C}\!-\!B_1$ approaches $\hbar_{J,g}/2$, as illustrated in Figure~ef{EnerDist_fig}, there must be in particular a bubble point~$w_r^*$ with $|w_r^*|\!=\!1$, though this is not material.\ 
oindent The above establishes Proposition~ef{EnerPres_prp} whenever $k\!=\!0$ by taking $$u_{\infty} ig|_{B^1}=u \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u_{\infty} ig|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}=v.$$ Since $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every~$r$, $k\!=\!0$ if $\mathfrak m\!<\!2\hbar_{J,g}$. If $k\!\ge\!1$, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\le\!\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g}$ by~(ef{EnerBub_e}) because \hbox{$E_g(v)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$} if $v$ is not constant by Corollary~ef{LowEner_crl} and $k\!\ge\!2$ otherwise by the above. Thus, by induction on $[\mathfrak m/\hbar_{J,g}]\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, we can assume that Proposition~ef{EnerPres_prp} holds when applied to~$\{v_i\}$ on $B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ with $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. This yields a tree~$\Sigma_r$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_r\!:\Sigma_r\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_r(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and $E_g(v_r)\!=\!\mathfrak m_r'$. Combining the last equality with~(ef{EnerBub_e}), we obtain $$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!E_g(v_r)=\mathfrak m\,.$$ Identifying $\infty$ in the base sphere of each~$\Sigma_r$ with $w_r^*\!\in\!\mathbb{P}_0^1$, which has been already attached to $0\!\in\!B_1^*$, we obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties; see Figure~ef{GrLim_fig2}.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale at points of maximal derivative so that all but hbar/2 of the energy lies in the unit disk, take the limit bubble via Lemma 5.4, show no energy is lost and the bubble connects (Corollary 5.3), check stability, and induct on m/hbar at the secondary bubble points.

nodes.name: choose hbar
nodes.statement: Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the smaller of the numbers $\hbar_{J,g}$ in Corollaries~\ref{LowEner_crl} and~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}. In particular, $\mathfrak m\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take hbar from Corollaries 4.2 and 5.3, so m >= hbar.

nodes.name: points of maximal derivative
nodes.statement: For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, choose $z_i\!\in\!\ov{B_{1/2}}$ so~that \BE{maxdui_e} \max_{z\in \ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i\big|_g.\end{equation} Since $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to~$u$, $z_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. Thus, $B_{1/2}(z_i)\!\subset\!B_1$ for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large.
nodes.statement_short: Pick z_i maximizing |du_i|; z_i -> 0.

nodes.name: Eq. maxdui_e
nodes.statement: \max_{z\in \ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i\big|_g.

nodes.name: rescaling maps
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{dela_it}, for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exists $\delta_i\!\in\!(0,1/2)$ such~that \BE{dejidfn_e} E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar_{J,g}}{2}\,.\end{equation} Define $$\psi_i\!:U_i\!\equiv\!\big\{w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!: z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\!\in\!B_{1/2}\big\} \longrightarrow B_{1/2} \qquad\hbox{by}\qquad \psi_i(w)=z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\,.$$ Since $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the second property in \ref{Ccov_it} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Choose delta_i with energy m - hbar/2 in B_{delta_i}(z_i) and define psi_i.

nodes.name: Eq. dejidfn_e
nodes.statement: E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar_{J,g}}{2}\,.

nodes.name: rescaled maps
