nodes.statement: For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, let $$v_i=u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\!: U_i\longrightarrow X.$$ Since $u_i$ is $J$-holomorphic and $\psi_i$ is biholomorphic onto its image, $v_i$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \hbox{$E_g(v_i)=E_g(u_i;B_{1/2})$}. Along with Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{SeqEner_it}, this implies that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(v_i)=\mathfrak m(1/2)<\infty\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: v_i = u_i o psi_i has bounded energy.

nodes.name: limit bubble
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres3_lmm}, there thus exist a finite collection $w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ of distinct points and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, such that $v_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. In particular, \ref{vcon_it} holds and $|\textnormal{d} v_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$. We can also assume that the limit~(\ref{fmdfn_e3}) exists for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.4 gives a limit v away from finitely many points w_r^*.

nodes.name: energy balance
nodes.statement: We note~that \BE{EnerBub_e}\begin{split} E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!\mathfrak m_r' &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\! E_g\!\big(v_i,B_R\!-\!\bigcup_{r=1}^k\! B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big) +\sum_{r=1}^k\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big)\\ &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i,B_R\big) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u_i,B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m\,; \end{split}\end{equation} the last equality holds by~(\ref{noEloss_e1}).
nodes.statement_short: E_g(v) + sum m_r' = m by (5.6).

nodes.name: Eq. EnerBub_e
nodes.statement: \begin{split} E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!\mathfrak m_r' &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\! E_g\!\big(v_i,B_R\!-\!\bigcup_{r=1}^k\! B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big) +\sum_{r=1}^k\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big)\\ &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i,B_R\big) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u_i,B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m\,; \end{split}

nodes.name: genuine bubble points
nodes.statement: Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)$ are pairwise disjoint. If $$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|<\infty$$ for some~$r$, then $\{v_i\}$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}$ to~$v$ by the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator. Thus, we can assume~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|=\infty$$ for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. In light of Corollary~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}\ref{fmLowBnd_it}, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.\\ \begin{figure} \begin{pspicture}(-.5,-2.5)(10,3.5) \psset{unit=.4cm} \pscircle[linewidth=.1](18,1){3}\pscircle*(21,1){.2}\rput(21.5,1){\sm{$1$}} \pscircle[linewidth=.07,linestyle=dotted](18,1){7}\pscircle*(25,1){.2} \rput(26.5,1){\sm{$\delta_0/\delta_i$}} \rput(18,1){\sm{$\mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar}{2}$}}\rput(18,-4){\sm{$\frac{\hbar}{2}-\epsilon_i$}} \end{pspicture} \caption{The energy distribution of the rescaled map~$v_i$ in the proof of Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp}} \end{figure}
nodes.statement_short: WLOG each w_r^* is a genuine blow-up point, so m_r' >= hbar.

nodes.name: the bubble connects
nodes.statement: We next show that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$, i.e.~that the bubble $(\mathbb{P}_0^1,v)$ connects to $(B_1,u)$ at~$z\!=\!0$. Note~that \begin{equation*}\begin{split} d_g\big(u(0),v(\infty)\big) &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}d_g\big(u(\delta),v(R)\big) =\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}d_g\big(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),v_i(R)\big)\\ &=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} d_g\big(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),u_i(z_i\!+\!R\delta_i)\big)\\ &\le \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} \textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i}(z_i))\big). \end{split}\end{equation*} Along with~(\ref{noEloss_e2}), this implies that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: The neck diameter estimate (5.7) gives u(0) = v(infinity).

nodes.name: stability of the bubble
nodes.statement: Suppose $v\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a constant map. By~(\ref{EnerBub_e}), $k\!\ge\!1$ and so there exists $w^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ such that $|\textnormal{d}_{w^*}v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. By~(\ref{maxdui_e}) and the definition of~$\psi_i$, $|\textnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\ge\!|\textnormal{d}_wv_i|$ for all $w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ contained in the domain of~$v_i$ and so $|\textnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$. By~(\ref{fmdfn_e3}) and~(\ref{dejidfn_e}), $$\mathfrak m_0'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g(v_i) \le \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(v_i;B_1\big) =\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big) = \mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar}{2}<\mathfrak m,$$ and so $k\!\ge\!2$, as claimed in~\ref{stab_it}. Since the amount of energy of $v_i$ contained in $\mathbb{C}\!-\!B_1$ approaches $\hbar_{J,g}/2$, as illustrated in Figure~\ref{EnerDist_fig}, there must be in particular a bubble point~$w_r^*$ with $|w_r^*|\!=\!1$, though this is not material.
nodes.statement_short: A constant bubble carries at least two further bubble points.

nodes.name: no secondary bubbles
nodes.statement: The above establishes Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} whenever $k\!=\!0$ by taking $$u_{\infty}\big|_{B^1}=u \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u_{\infty}\big|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}=v.$$ Since $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every~$r$, $k\!=\!0$ if $\mathfrak m\!<\!2\hbar_{J,g}$. If $k\!\ge\!1$, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\le\!\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g}$ by~(\ref{EnerBub_e}) because \hbox{$E_g(v)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$} if $v$ is not constant by Corollary~\ref{LowEner_crl} and $k\!\ge\!2$ otherwise by the above.
nodes.statement_short: If k = 0 we are done; this holds if m < 2 hbar.

nodes.name: induction on m/hbar
nodes.statement: Thus, by induction on $[\mathfrak m/\hbar_{J,g}]\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, we can assume that Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} holds when applied to~$\{v_i\}$ on $B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ with $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$. This yields a tree~$\Sigma_r$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_r\!:\Sigma_r\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_r(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and $E_g(v_r)\!=\!\mathfrak m_r'$. Combining the last equality with~(\ref{EnerBub_e}), we obtain $$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!E_g(v_r)=\mathfrak m\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the proposition inductively at each w_r^*.

nodes.name: assemble the tree
nodes.statement: Identifying $\infty$ in the base sphere of each~$\Sigma_r$ with $w_r^*\!\in\!\mathbb{P}_0^1$, which has been already attached to $0\!\in\!B_1^*$, we obtain a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties; see Figure~\ref{GrLim_fig2}.
nodes.statement_short: Attach the bubble trees to get u_infinity.

nodes.name: proof of Theorem 1.2 (Gromov's Compactness I)
nodes.statement:
Fix a Riemannian metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ on~$\Sigma$. For $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $\delta\!\in\!\Sigma$, let $B_{\delta}(z)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ denote the ball of radius~$\delta$ around~$z$.\ 
oindent By Lemma~ef{EnerPres3_lmm}, there exist a finite collection $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma$ of distinct points and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, such that $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$. In particular, $|	extnormal{d} u_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$. We can also assume that the~limit $$\mathfrak m_j\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*) ig)$$ exists for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$. We note that \BE{Egtot_e} egin{split} E_g(u)+\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\mathfrak m_j&= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u;\Sigma\!-\! igcup_{j=1}^{\ell}B_{\delta}(z_j^*) ig) +\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g ig(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*) ig)\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i).\ \end{split}\end{equation} \vspace{.1in} 
oindent Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)$ are pairwise disjoint. If $$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}} ig|	extnormal{d} u_i ig|<\infty$$ for some~$j$, then $\{u_i\}$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}$ to~$u$ by the ellipticity of the $ ar\partial$-operator. Thus, we can assume~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)}} ig|	extnormal{d} u_i ig|=\infty$$ for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$.\ 
oindent For each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$, Proposition~ef{EnerPres_prp} provides a tree~$\Sigma_j$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_j\!:\Sigma_j\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_j(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and $E_g(v_j)\!=\!\mathfrak m_j$. Combining the last equality with~(ef{Egtot_e}), we obtain $$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\!E_g(v_j)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)\,.$$ Identifying the distinguished point~$\infty$ of each~$\Sigma_j$ with $z_j^*\!\in\!\Sigma$, we obtain a Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties.\ 
oindent If $\Sigma\!=\!\mathbb{P}^1$ and the limit map~$u$ above is constant, then $\ell\!\ge\!1$ by~(ef{Egtot_e}). Suppose $\ell\!\in\!\{1,2\}$. Let $$M_i=\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_1^*)}} ig|	extnormal{d} u_i ig|$$ and parametrize~$\mathbb{P}^1$ so that $z_1^*\!=\!0$. Define $$h_i\!: \mathbb{P}^1\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1, \qquad h_i(z)=z_i\!+\!z/M_i,$$ and apply the preceding argument with $u_i$ replaced by~$u_i\!\circ\!h_i$. By the proof of Corollary~ef{EnerPres2_crl}ef{fmLowBnd_it}, the limiting map $u|_{\Sigma}$ is then non-constant and $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u)$ is a stable $J$-holomorphic map.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.4 gives convergence away from finitely many bubble points; Proposition 5.5 produces a bubble tree at each, energy adds up by (5.9), and a reparametrization handles stability for constant limits on P^1.

nodes.name: convergence away from bubble points
nodes.statement: Fix a Riemannian metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ on~$\Sigma$. For $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $\delta\!\in\!\Sigma$, let $B_{\delta}(z)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ denote the ball of radius~$\delta$ around~$z$.\\ \noindent By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres3_lmm}, there exist a finite collection $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma$ of distinct points and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, such that $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$ to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$. In particular, $|\textnormal{d} u_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a metric on Sigma; Lemma 5.4 gives a limit u off z_1^*, ..., z_ell^*.

nodes.name: energy balance
nodes.statement: We can also assume that the~limit $$\mathfrak m_j\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)$$ exists for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$. We note that \BE{Egtot_e}\begin{split} E_g(u)+\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\mathfrak m_j&= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u;\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{j=1}^{\ell}B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big) +\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)\\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i).\\ \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: E_g(u) + sum m_j = lim E_g(u_i).

nodes.name: Eq. Egtot_e
nodes.statement: \begin{split} E_g(u)+\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\mathfrak m_j&= \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u;\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{j=1}^{\ell}B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big) +\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)\\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i).\\ \end{split}

nodes.name: genuine bubble points
nodes.statement: Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)$ are pairwise disjoint. If $$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|<\infty$$ for some~$j$, then $\{u_i\}$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}$ to~$u$ by the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator. Thus, we can assume~that $$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|=\infty$$ for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG |du_i| blows up near each z_j^*.

nodes.name: bubble trees
nodes.statement: For each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$, Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} provides a tree~$\Sigma_j$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_j\!:\Sigma_j\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_j(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and $E_g(v_j)\!=\!\mathfrak m_j$. Combining the last equality with~(\ref{Egtot_e}), we obtain $$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\!E_g(v_j)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)\,.$$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 5.5 gives a bubble tree at each z_j^*.

nodes.name: assemble the limit
nodes.statement: Identifying the distinguished point~$\infty$ of each~$\Sigma_j$ with $z_j^*\!\in\!\Sigma$, we obtain a Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ and a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties.
nodes.statement_short: Attach the trees to get the stable limit.

nodes.name: stability for constant limits
nodes.statement: If $\Sigma\!=\!\mathbb{P}^1$ and the limit map~$u$ above is constant, then $\ell\!\ge\!1$ by~(\ref{Egtot_e}). Suppose $\ell\!\in\!\{1,2\}$. Let $$M_i=\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_1^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|$$ and parametrize~$\mathbb{P}^1$ so that $z_1^*\!=\!0$. Define $$h_i\!: \mathbb{P}^1\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1, \qquad h_i(z)=z_i\!+\!z/M_i,$$ and apply the preceding argument with $u_i$ replaced by~$u_i\!\circ\!h_i$. By the proof of Corollary~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}\ref{fmLowBnd_it}, the limiting map $u|_{\Sigma}$ is then non-constant and $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u)$ is a stable $J$-holomorphic map.
nodes.statement_short: If the limit on P^1 is constant with at most two bubble points, reparametrize.

nodes.name: positive generator ell of H_2(P^{n-1})
nodes.statement: Let $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, with $n\!\ge\!2$, and $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}\!=\!\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. Denote by $\ell$ the positive generator of $H_2(\mathbb{P}^{n-1};{\mathbb Z})\!\approx\!{\mathbb Z}$, i.e.~the homology class represented by the standard $\mathbb{P}^1\!\subset\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$.

nodes.name: degree d map
nodes.statement: A \textsf{degree~$d$ map} $f\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ is a continuous map such that $f_*[\mathbb{P}^1]\!=\!d\ell$.

nodes.name: holomorphic maps P^1 -> P^{n-1} are given by polynomials
nodes.statement: A holomorphic degree~$d$ map $f\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ is given~by $$[u,v]\longrightarrow\big[R_1(u,v),\ldots,R_n(u,v)\big]$$ for some degree~$d$ homogeneous polynomials $R_1,\ldots,R_d$ on~$\mathbb{C}^2$ without a common linear factor.

nodes.name: space X_{n,d} of polynomial tuples
nodes.statement: Since the tuple $(\lambda R_1,\ldots,\lambda R_n)$ determines the same map as $(R_1,\ldots,R_n)$ for any $\lambda\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^*$, the space of degree~$d$ holomorphic maps $f\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ is a dense open subset of $$\mathfrak X_{n,d}\equiv \big((\textnormal{Sym}^d\mathbb{C}^2)^n-\{0\}\big)\big/\mathbb{C}^* \approx\mathbb{P}^{(d+1)n-1}\,.$$

nodes.name: Gromov limits of holomorphic maps P^1 -> P^{n-1}
nodes.statement:
Suppose $f_k\!: \mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ is a sequence of holomorphic degree $d\!\ge\!1$ maps and $$\mathbf R_k= ig[R_{k;1},\ldots,R_{k;n} ig] \in\mathfrak X_{n,d}$$ are the associated equivalence classes of $n$-tuples of homogeneous polynomials without a common linear factor. Passing to a subsequence, we can assume that $[\mathbf R_k]$ converges to some \BE{bRdfn_e}\mathbf R\equiv ig[(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_1, \ldots,(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_n ig]\in\mathfrak X_{n,d}\,,\end{equation} with $d_1,\ldots,d_m\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ and homogeneous polynomials $$\mathbf S\equiv [S_1,\ldots,S_n]\in \mathfrak X_{n,d_0}$$ without a common linear factor and with $d_0\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$. By~(ef{bRdfn_e}), $$d_0+d_1+\ldots+d_m=d.$$ Rescaling $(R_{k;1},\ldots,R_{k;n})$, we can assume that \BE{Pneg_e3} \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i}=(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_i \qquad orall\,i\!=\!1,\ldots,n.\end{equation} \vspace{.1in} 
oindent Suppose $z_0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!-\!\{u_1/v_1,\ldots,u_m/v_m\}$. Since the polynomials $S_1,\ldots,S_n$ do not have a common linear factor, $S_{i_0}(z_0,1)\!
eq\!0$ for some $i_0\!=\!1,\ldots,n$. This implies that $R_{k;i_0}(z_0,1)\!
eq\!0$ for all $k$ large enough and so $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty} rac{R_{k;i}(z,1)}{R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} = rac{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i}(z,1)}{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} = rac{(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_i(z,1)} {(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_{i_0}(z,1)} = rac{S_i(z,1)}{S_{i_0}(z,1)}\,$$ for all $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$ and $z$ close to~$z_0$. Furthermore, the convergence is uniform on a neighborhood of~$z_0$. Thus, the sequence $f_k$ $C^{\infty}$-converges on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{[u_1,v_1],\ldots,[u_m,v_m]\}$ to the holomorphic degree~$d_0$ map $g\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ determined by~$\mathbf S$.\ 
oindent Let $\omega$ be the Fubini-Study symplectic form on~$\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ normalized so that $\lr{\omega,\ell}\!=\!1$ and $E(\cdot)$ be the energy of maps into~$\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ with respect to the associated Riemannian metric. For each $\delta\!>\!0$ and $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, denote by $B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])$ the ball of radius~$\delta$ around $[u_j,v_j]$ in~$\mathbb{P}^1$ and let $$\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta}=\mathbb{P}^1- igcup_{j=1}^mB_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])\,.$$ For each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, let $$\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]} ig(\{f_k\} ig)=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E ig(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j]) ig)\in\mathbb R^{\ge0}$$ be the energy sinking into the bubble point $[u_j,v_j]$. By Theorem~ef{GromConv_thm1}, the number $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})$ is the value of~$\omega$ on some element of~$H_2(\mathbb{P}^{n-1};{\mathbb Z})$, i.e.~an integer. Below we show that $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})\!=\!d_j$.\ 
oindent Since the sequence $f_k$ $C^{\infty}$-converges to the degree~$d_0$ map $g\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{[u_1,v_1],\ldots,[u_m,v_m]\}$, $$d_0=\lr{\omega,d_0\ell}=E(g) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}E_g ig(g;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E ig(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig).$$ Thus,  egin{equation*} egin{split} \sum_{j=1}^m \mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]} ig(\{f_k\} ig) &=\sum_{j=1}^m\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E ig(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j]) ig) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty} E ig(f_k; igcup_{j=1}^m\!B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j]) ig)\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty\!}  ig(E_g(f_k)\!-\!E_g ig(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig) ig) =d-d_0=d_1+\ldots+d_m\,. \end{split}\end{equation*} In particular, $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})\!=\!d_j$ if $m\!=\!1$, no matter what the ``residual" tuple of polynomials $\mathbf S$~is. We use this below to establish this energy identity for $m\!>\!1$ as well.\ 
oindent By~(ef{Pneg_e3}), for all $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exist $\lambda_{k;i;j;p}\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ with $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, and $p\!=\!1,\ldots,d_j$ and tuples $$\mathbf S_k\equiv  ig[S_{k;1},\ldots,S_{k;n} ig]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d_0}$$ of polynomials without a common linear factor such that  egin{gather*} \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf S_k=\mathbf S, \qquad \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lambda_{k;i;j;p}=1~~ orall\,i,j,p,\ R_{k;i}(u,v)=\prod_{j=1}^m\prod_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)\quad orall~k,i\,. \end{gather*} For each $j_0\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, let $$\mathbf T_{j_0}\equiv  ig[T_{j_0;1},\ldots,T_{j_0;n} ig]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d-d_{j_0}}$$ be a tuple of polynomials without a common linear factor. If in addition, $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R$, and $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let  egin{alignat*}{2} S_{i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv \prod_{j
eq j_0}^m(v_ju\!-\!u_jv)^{d_j} \cdot S_i(u,v)+ \epsilon T_{j_0;i}(u,v)\,, &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n,\ R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv R_{k;i}(u,v)+ \epsilon\prod_{p=1}^{d_{j_0}}(v_{j_0}u\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j_0;p}u_{j_0}v) \cdot T_{j_0;i}(u,v), &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n. \end{alignat*} \vspace{.1in} 
oindent The polynomials within each tuple $(S_{i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ and $(R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ have no common linear factor for all $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small and $k$ sufficiently large (with the conditions on~$\epsilon$ and~$k$ mutually independent). We denote by $$f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$$ the holomorphic degree~$d$ map determined by the~tuple $$\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\equiv ig[R_{k;1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,R_{k;n;j_0;\epsilon} ig]\,.$$ Since $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon} = ig[(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots, (v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{n;j_0;\epsilon} ig] \in\mathfrak X_{n;d}$$ and the polynomials $S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,S_{n;j_0;\epsilon}$ have no linear factor in common, \BE{Pneg_e5} \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\!E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) \equiv \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]} ig(\{f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\} ig) =d_{j_0}\end{equation} by the $m\!=\!1$ case established above.\ 
oindent For $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, and $k$ sufficiently large, $$\prod_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)
eq0 \qquad orall~[u,v]\!\in\!B_{2\delta} ig([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}] ig).$$ Thus, the ratios $$ rac{R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)}{R_{k;i}(u,v)} =1+\epsilon rac{T_{j_0;i}(u,v)} {\prod\limits_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)}$$ converge uniformly to~1 on $B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])$ as $\epsilon\!\longrightarrow\!0$. Thus, there exists $k^*\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such~that $$\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\sup_{k\ge k^*}\sup_{z\in B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])}  igg| rac{|	extnormal{d}_zf_{k;j_0;\epsilon}|}{|	extnormal{d}_zf_k|}-1 igg|=0.$$ It follows that  egin{equation*} egin{split} \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]} ig(\{f_k\} ig) &\equiv \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E ig(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) = \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig)\ &=\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) =\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}d_{j_0}=d_{j_0}; \end{split}\end{equation*} the second-to-last equality above holds by~(ef{Pneg_e5}).\ 
oindent Suppose that either $d_0\!\ge\!1$ or $m\!\ge\!3$. Otherwise, the maps~$f_k$ can be reparametrized so that $d_0\!
eq\!0$; see the last paragraph of the proof of Theorem~ef{GromConv_thm1} at the end of Section~ef{Conver_subs2}. By Theorem~ef{GromConv_thm1} and the above, a subsequence of $\{f_k\}$ converges to the equivalence class of a holomorphic degree~$d_0$ map $f\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, where $\Sigma$ is a nodal Riemann surface consisting of the component~$\Sigma_0\!=\!\mathbb{P}^1$ corresponding to the original~$\mathbb{P}^1$ and finitely many trees of $\mathbb{P}^1$'s coming off from~$\Sigma_0$. The maps on the components in the trees are defined only up reparametrization of the domain. By the above, $f|_{\Sigma_0}$ is the map~$g$ determined by the ``relatively prime part" $\mathbf S$ of the limit~$\mathbf R$ of the tuples of polynomials. The trees are attached at the roots~$[u_j,v_j]$ of the common linear factors $v_ju\!-\!u_jv$ of the polynomials in~$\mathbf R$; the degree of the restriction of~$f$ to each tree is the power of the multiplicity~$d_j$ of the corresponding common linear factor.
nodes.statement_short: Gromov limit of degree-d maps P^1 -> P^{n-1}: the main component is given by the relatively prime part of the limiting polynomials, bubble trees of degree d_j sit at the common roots.

nodes.name: Eq. bRdfn_e
nodes.statement: \mathbf R\equiv\big[(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_1, \ldots,(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_n\big]\in\mathfrak X_{n,d}\,,

nodes.name: Eq. Pneg_e3
nodes.statement: \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i}=(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mu\!-\!u_mv)^{d_m}S_i \qquad\forall\,i\!=\!1,\ldots,n.

nodes.name: proof of convergence away from the common roots
nodes.statement: Suppose $z_0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!-\!\{u_1/v_1,\ldots,u_m/v_m\}$. Since the polynomials $S_1,\ldots,S_n$ do not have a common linear factor, $S_{i_0}(z_0,1)\!\neq\!0$ for some $i_0\!=\!1,\ldots,n$. This implies that $R_{k;i_0}(z_0,1)\!\neq\!0$ for all $k$ large enough and so $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\frac{R_{k;i}(z,1)}{R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i}(z,1)}{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_i(z,1)} {(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_{i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{S_i(z,1)}{S_{i_0}(z,1)}\,$$ for all $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$ and $z$ close to~$z_0$. Furthermore, the convergence is uniform on a neighborhood of~$z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Near a point that is not a common root some S_i is nonzero, so the ratios of the R_{k;i} converge uniformly.

nodes.name: nonvanishing component
nodes.statement: Suppose $z_0\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!-\!\{u_1/v_1,\ldots,u_m/v_m\}$. Since the polynomials $S_1,\ldots,S_n$ do not have a common linear factor, $S_{i_0}(z_0,1)\!\neq\!0$ for some $i_0\!=\!1,\ldots,n$.
nodes.statement_short: Away from the common roots some S_{i_0} is nonzero.

nodes.name: ratios converge
nodes.statement: This implies that $R_{k;i_0}(z_0,1)\!\neq\!0$ for all $k$ large enough and so $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\frac{R_{k;i}(z,1)}{R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i}(z,1)}{\lim\limits_{k\longrightarrow\infty}R_{k;i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_i(z,1)} {(v_1z\!-\!u_1)^{d_1}\ldots(v_mz\!-\!u_m)^{d_m}S_{i_0}(z,1)} =\frac{S_i(z,1)}{S_{i_0}(z,1)}\,$$ for all $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$ and $z$ close to~$z_0$. Furthermore, the convergence is uniform on a neighborhood of~$z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The ratios R_{k;i}/R_{k;i_0} converge uniformly to S_i/S_{i_0}.

nodes.name: convergence away from the common roots
nodes.statement: Thus, the sequence $f_k$ $C^{\infty}$-converges on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{[u_1,v_1],\ldots,[u_m,v_m]\}$ to the holomorphic degree~$d_0$ map $g\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ determined by~$\mathbf S$.

nodes.name: Fubini-Study form and energy on P^{n-1}
nodes.statement: Let $\omega$ be the Fubini-Study symplectic form on~$\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ normalized so that $\lr{\omega,\ell}\!=\!1$ and $E(\cdot)$ be the energy of maps into~$\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ with respect to the associated Riemannian metric.

nodes.name: complement of small balls P^1_delta
nodes.statement: For each $\delta\!>\!0$ and $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, denote by $B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])$ the ball of radius~$\delta$ around $[u_j,v_j]$ in~$\mathbb{P}^1$ and let $$\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta}=\mathbb{P}^1-\bigcup_{j=1}^mB_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])\,.$$

nodes.name: energy sinking into a bubble point
nodes.statement: For each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, let $$\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}\big(\{f_k\}\big)=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E\big(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])\big)\in\mathbb R^{\ge0}$$ be the energy sinking into the bubble point $[u_j,v_j]$.

nodes.name: bubble energies are integers
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1}, the number $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})$ is the value of~$\omega$ on some element of~$H_2(\mathbb{P}^{n-1};{\mathbb Z})$, i.e.~an integer.

nodes.name: energy sinking into a bubble point equals the multiplicity
nodes.statement: Below we show that $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})\!=\!d_j$.

nodes.name: proof that the bubble energy equals the multiplicity
nodes.statement:
Since the sequence $f_k$ $C^{\infty}$-converges to the degree~$d_0$ map $g\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{[u_1,v_1],\ldots,[u_m,v_m]\}$, $$d_0=\lr{\omega,d_0\ell}=E(g) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}E_g ig(g;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E ig(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig).$$ Thus,  egin{equation*} egin{split} \sum_{j=1}^m \mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]} ig(\{f_k\} ig) &=\sum_{j=1}^m\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E ig(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j]) ig) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty} E ig(f_k; igcup_{j=1}^m\!B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j]) ig)\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty\!}  ig(E_g(f_k)\!-\!E_g ig(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta} ig) ig) =d-d_0=d_1+\ldots+d_m\,. \end{split}\end{equation*} In particular, $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})\!=\!d_j$ if $m\!=\!1$, no matter what the ``residual" tuple of polynomials $\mathbf S$~is. We use this below to establish this energy identity for $m\!>\!1$ as well.\ 
oindent By~(ef{Pneg_e3}), for all $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exist $\lambda_{k;i;j;p}\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ with $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, and $p\!=\!1,\ldots,d_j$ and tuples $$\mathbf S_k\equiv  ig[S_{k;1},\ldots,S_{k;n} ig]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d_0}$$ of polynomials without a common linear factor such that  egin{gather*} \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf S_k=\mathbf S, \qquad \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lambda_{k;i;j;p}=1~~ orall\,i,j,p,\ R_{k;i}(u,v)=\prod_{j=1}^m\prod_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)\quad orall~k,i\,. \end{gather*} For each $j_0\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, let $$\mathbf T_{j_0}\equiv  ig[T_{j_0;1},\ldots,T_{j_0;n} ig]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d-d_{j_0}}$$ be a tuple of polynomials without a common linear factor. If in addition, $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R$, and $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let  egin{alignat*}{2} S_{i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv \prod_{j
eq j_0}^m(v_ju\!-\!u_jv)^{d_j} \cdot S_i(u,v)+ \epsilon T_{j_0;i}(u,v)\,, &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n,\ R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv R_{k;i}(u,v)+ \epsilon\prod_{p=1}^{d_{j_0}}(v_{j_0}u\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j_0;p}u_{j_0}v) \cdot T_{j_0;i}(u,v), &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n. \end{alignat*} \vspace{.1in} 
oindent The polynomials within each tuple $(S_{i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ and $(R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ have no common linear factor for all $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small and $k$ sufficiently large (with the conditions on~$\epsilon$ and~$k$ mutually independent). We denote by $$f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$$ the holomorphic degree~$d$ map determined by the~tuple $$\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\equiv ig[R_{k;1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,R_{k;n;j_0;\epsilon} ig]\,.$$ Since $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon} = ig[(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots, (v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{n;j_0;\epsilon} ig] \in\mathfrak X_{n;d}$$ and the polynomials $S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,S_{n;j_0;\epsilon}$ have no linear factor in common, \BE{Pneg_e5} \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\!E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) \equiv \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]} ig(\{f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\} ig) =d_{j_0}\end{equation} by the $m\!=\!1$ case established above.\ 
oindent For $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, and $k$ sufficiently large, $$\prod_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)
eq0 \qquad orall~[u,v]\!\in\!B_{2\delta} ig([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}] ig).$$ Thus, the ratios $$ rac{R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)}{R_{k;i}(u,v)} =1+\epsilon rac{T_{j_0;i}(u,v)} {\prod\limits_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)}$$ converge uniformly to~1 on $B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])$ as $\epsilon\!\longrightarrow\!0$. Thus, there exists $k^*\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such~that $$\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\sup_{k\ge k^*}\sup_{z\in B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])}  igg| rac{|	extnormal{d}_zf_{k;j_0;\epsilon}|}{|	extnormal{d}_zf_k|}-1 igg|=0.$$ It follows that  egin{equation*} egin{split} \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]} ig(\{f_k\} ig) &\equiv \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E ig(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) = \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig)\ &=\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E ig(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]) ig) =\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}d_{j_0}=d_{j_0}; \end{split}\end{equation*} the second-to-last equality above holds by~(ef{Pneg_e5}).
nodes.statement_short: Energy count gives the total d-d_0, which settles m=1; for m>1 perturb the polynomials to isolate one root and compare energies.

nodes.name: energy of the main component
nodes.statement: Since the sequence $f_k$ $C^{\infty}$-converges to the degree~$d_0$ map $g\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ on compact subsets of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{[u_1,v_1],\ldots,[u_m,v_m]\}$, $$d_0=\lr{\omega,d_0\ell}=E(g) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}E_g\big(g;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta}\big) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E\big(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta}\big).$$
nodes.statement_short: The energy away from the roots tends to d_0.

nodes.name: total bubble energy
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \sum_{j=1}^m \mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}\big(\{f_k\}\big) &=\sum_{j=1}^m\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E\big(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])\big) =\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty} E\big(f_k;\bigcup_{j=1}^m\!B_{\delta}([u_j,v_j])\big)\\ &=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty\!} \big(E_g(f_k)\!-\!E_g\big(f_k;\mathbb{P}^1_{\delta}\big)\big) =d-d_0=d_1+\ldots+d_m\,. \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The bubble energies sum to d - d_0.

nodes.name: one root
nodes.statement: In particular, $\mathfrak m_{[u_j,v_j]}(\{f_k\})\!=\!d_j$ if $m\!=\!1$, no matter what the ``residual" tuple of polynomials $\mathbf S$~is. We use this below to establish this energy identity for $m\!>\!1$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: This settles the case m = 1.

nodes.name: factor the polynomials
nodes.statement: By~(\ref{Pneg_e3}), for all $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exist $\lambda_{k;i;j;p}\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ with $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $j\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, and $p\!=\!1,\ldots,d_j$ and tuples $$\mathbf S_k\equiv \big[S_{k;1},\ldots,S_{k;n}\big]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d_0}$$ of polynomials without a common linear factor such that \begin{gather*} \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf S_k=\mathbf S, \qquad \lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lambda_{k;i;j;p}=1~~\forall\,i,j,p,\\ R_{k;i}(u,v)=\prod_{j=1}^m\prod_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)\quad\forall~k,i\,. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Factor R_{k;i} through the perturbed roots.

nodes.name: perturbed tuples
nodes.statement: For each $j_0\!=\!1,\ldots,m$, let $$\mathbf T_{j_0}\equiv \big[T_{j_0;1},\ldots,T_{j_0;n}\big]\in \mathfrak X_{n;d-d_{j_0}}$$ be a tuple of polynomials without a common linear factor. If in addition, $i\!=\!1,\ldots,n$, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R$, and $k\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, let \begin{alignat*}{2} S_{i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv \prod_{j\neq j_0}^m(v_ju\!-\!u_jv)^{d_j} \cdot S_i(u,v)+ \epsilon T_{j_0;i}(u,v)\,, &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n,\\ R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)&\equiv R_{k;i}(u,v)+ \epsilon\prod_{p=1}^{d_{j_0}}(v_{j_0}u\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j_0;p}u_{j_0}v) \cdot T_{j_0;i}(u,v), &\qquad &i=1,\ldots,n. \end{alignat*}
nodes.statement_short: Perturb the polynomials to keep only the root [u_{j_0}, v_{j_0}] common.

nodes.name: apply the m = 1 case
nodes.statement: The polynomials within each tuple $(S_{i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ and $(R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon})_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ have no common linear factor for all $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small and $k$ sufficiently large (with the conditions on~$\epsilon$ and~$k$ mutually independent). We denote by $$f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$$ the holomorphic degree~$d$ map determined by the~tuple $$\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\equiv\big[R_{k;1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,R_{k;n;j_0;\epsilon}\big]\,.$$ Since $$\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\mathbf R_{k;j_0;\epsilon} =\big[(v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots, (v_1u\!-\!u_1v)^{d_{j_0}}S_{n;j_0;\epsilon}\big] \in\mathfrak X_{n;d}$$ and the polynomials $S_{1;j_0;\epsilon},\ldots,S_{n;j_0;\epsilon}$ have no linear factor in common, \BE{Pneg_e5} \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\!E\big(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])\big) \equiv \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]}\big(\{f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\}\big) =d_{j_0}\end{equation} by the $m\!=\!1$ case established above.
nodes.statement_short: The perturbed maps have bubble energy d_{j_0} at the root.

nodes.name: Eq. Pneg_e5
nodes.statement: \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\!E\big(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])\big) \equiv \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]}\big(\{f_{k;j_0;\epsilon}\}\big) =d_{j_0}

nodes.name: compare derivatives
nodes.statement:
For $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, $\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ sufficiently small, and $k$ sufficiently large, $$\prod_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)
eq0 \qquad orall~[u,v]\!\in\!B_{2\delta} ig([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}] ig).$$ Thus, the ratios $$ rac{R_{k;i;j_0;\epsilon}(u,v)}{R_{k;i}(u,v)} =1+\epsilon rac{T_{j_0;i}(u,v)} {\prod\limits_{j
eq j_0}^m\prod\limits_{p=1}^{d_j}(v_ju\!-\!\lambda_{k;i;j;p}u_jv) \cdot S_{k;i}(u,v)}$$ converge uniformly to~1 on $B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])$ as $\epsilon\!\longrightarrow\!0$. Thus, there exists $k^*\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such~that $$\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\sup_{k\ge k^*}\sup_{z\in B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])}  igg| rac{|	extnormal{d}_zf_{k;j_0;\epsilon}|}{|	extnormal{d}_zf_k|}-1 igg|=0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Derivatives of the perturbed and original maps agree to first order near the root.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{equation*}\begin{split} \mathfrak m_{[u_{j_0},v_{j_0}]}\big(\{f_k\}\big) &\equiv \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}E\big(f_k;B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])\big) = \lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}E\big(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])\big)\\ &=\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{k\longrightarrow\infty}\! E\big(f_{k;j_0;\epsilon};B_{\delta}([u_{j_0},v_{j_0}])\big) =\lim_{\epsilon\longrightarrow0}d_{j_0}=d_{j_0}; \end{split}\end{equation*} the second-to-last equality above holds by~(\ref{Pneg_e5}).
nodes.statement_short: Hence the bubble energy at [u_{j_0}, v_{j_0}] is d_{j_0}.

nodes.name: description of the Gromov limit of maps to P^{n-1}
nodes.statement: Suppose that either $d_0\!\ge\!1$ or $m\!\ge\!3$. Otherwise, the maps~$f_k$ can be reparametrized so that $d_0\!\neq\!0$; see the last paragraph of the proof of Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} at the end of Section~\ref{Conver_subs2}. By Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm1} and the above, a subsequence of $\{f_k\}$ converges to the equivalence class of a holomorphic degree~$d_0$ map $f\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, where $\Sigma$ is a nodal Riemann surface consisting of the component~$\Sigma_0\!=\!\mathbb{P}^1$ corresponding to the original~$\mathbb{P}^1$ and finitely many trees of $\mathbb{P}^1$'s coming off from~$\Sigma_0$. The maps on the components in the trees are defined only up reparametrization of the domain. By the above, $f|_{\Sigma_0}$ is the map~$g$ determined by the ``relatively prime part" $\mathbf S$ of the limit~$\mathbf R$ of the tuples of polynomials. The trees are attached at the roots~$[u_j,v_j]$ of the common linear factors $v_ju\!-\!u_jv$ of the polynomials in~$\mathbf R$; the degree of the restriction of~$f$ to each tree is the power of the multiplicity~$d_j$ of the corresponding common linear factor.

nodes.name: argument for the map to the linear sigma model
nodes.statement: The same reasoning as above applies to the sequence of maps $$\big(\textnormal{id}_{\mathbb{P}^1},f_k\big)\!:\mathbb{P}^1\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\!\times\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}\,,$$ but the condition that either $d_0\!\ge\!1$ or $m\!\ge\!3$ is no longer necessary for the analogue of the conclusion in the previous paragraph.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the same analysis to the graphs (id, f_k), where no stability condition is needed.

nodes.name: continuous surjection from the graph space to the linear sigma model
nodes.statement: This implies~that the~map $$\mathfrak M_{0,0}\big(\mathbb{P}^1\!\times\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1},(1,d)\big)\longrightarrow\mathfrak X_{n,d}, \qquad [f,g]\longrightarrow\big[g\!\circ\!f^{-1}\big],$$ from the subspace of $\ov\mathfrak M_{0,0}(\mathbb{P}^1\!\times\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1},(1,d))$ corresponding to maps from~$\mathbb{P}^1$ extends to a continuous surjective map \BE{LinSig_e}\ov\mathfrak M_{0,0}\big(\mathbb{P}^1\!\times\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1},(1,d)\big)\longrightarrow \mathfrak X_{n,d}\,.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Eq. LinSig_e
nodes.statement: \ov\mathfrak M_{0,0}\big(\mathbb{P}^1\!\times\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1},(1,d)\big)\longrightarrow \mathfrak X_{n,d}\,.

nodes.name: Gromov's moduli spaces refine classical compactifications
nodes.statement: In particular, Gromov's moduli spaces refine classical compactifications of spaces of holomorphic maps $\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. On the other hand, the former are defined for arbitrary almost Kahler manifolds, which makes them naturally suited for applying topological methods.

nodes.name: linear sigma model
nodes.statement: The right-hand side of~(\ref{LinSig_e}) is known as the \textsf{linear sigma model} in the Mirror Symmetry literature.

nodes.name: role in mirror symmetry
nodes.statement: The morphism~(\ref{LinSig_e}) plays a prominent role in the proof of mirror symmetry for the genus~0 Gromov-Witten invariants in~\cite{Gi} and~\cite{LLY}; see \cite[Section~30.2]{MirSym}.
